title: Building a Fraud Risk Management Program
name: Building a Fraud Risk Management Program
subtitle: Domain 1 Knowledge Assessment

questions.stem: Consumers initiate app payments after being convinced by callers that their existing balance is unsafe. Which investment addresses the causal vulnerability more directly than conventional unauthorized-login controls alone?
options: Controls combining behavioral indicators, contextual warnings and customer education
Treating successful authentication as proof that no fraud occurred
Only retrospective investigation of unauthorized card transactions
Disabling all payment products permanently
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes socially engineered authorized push payments from unauthorized access and emphasizes behavior-based controls and education.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management process
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management process

questions.stem: A board receives a proposal for biometrics technology with no explicit link to assessed fraud exposure or customer experience. Which step should occur before approving the investment?
options: Establish an assessed use case, integration requirements and anticipated fraud/customer benefits
Measure success only through the vendor’s feature list
Let IT decide without legal, compliance or operational involvement
Purchase immediately to keep up with competitors
questions.explanation: The guide calls for a risk-driven use case, cost/benefit assessment and engagement with IT, legal, compliance, finance and vendors.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Best practices for setting up an anti-fraud technology portfolio
questions.sourceSection: Best practices for setting up an anti-fraud technology portfolio

questions.stem: An internal control redesign is complete, and directors ask who should deliver a separate independent review of its effectiveness. Which line of defense should primarily provide this independent assurance?
options: Second line, through policy ownership
Third line, through internal audit
First line, through fraud operations
First line, through fraud analytics
questions.explanation: The guide places prevention, detection and response in the first line; policy and oversight in the second; independent assurance/testing in the third.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management framework
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management framework

questions.stem: A new merchant is registered in one region but the activity profile and supporting documents consistently indicate operations elsewhere. Which transactional risk dimension is most directly implicated?
options: Channel risk, because digital payments are involved
Product risk, because all money transfers are equivalent
Customer risk, because location details never inform fraud assessment
Jurisdiction risk, because identity and activity may not align with claimed geography
questions.explanation: The guide treats alignment of documents and account activity with jurisdictions of residence, establishment and operation as jurisdiction-related risk.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Transactional fraud risk: Customer, jurisdiction, product, channel
questions.sourceSection: Transactional fraud risk: Customer, jurisdiction, product, channel

questions.stem: An internal team submits a harmless simulated fake invoice and tests whether dual authorization and vendor-account checks detect it. What is the most accurate purpose of the exercise?
options: To replace the need for periodic risk assessment
To prove every employee involved is dishonest
To test operating effectiveness and potential bypass of fraud controls
To quantify employee satisfaction with the finance team
questions.explanation: The guide describes scenario-based “mystery shopper” tests as assessments of control operation and potential circumvention.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud control tests
questions.sourceSection: Fraud control tests

questions.stem: An audit identifies unintentional data corruption as well as a supervisor’s intentional manipulation of records for gain. Which feature differentiates the fraud component from a broader operational failure?
options: It causes a measurable financial loss
It occurs within a regulated financial institution
It involves deliberate deception for an improper advantage
It requires breakdown of at least one technology control
questions.explanation: Fraud is a form of operational risk distinguished by intentional deception or malicious manipulation; operational failure need not be intentional.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk is a form of operational risk
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk is a form of operational risk

questions.stem: A board receives an urgent request for new fraud controls, while existing spending commitments compete for the same budget. Which TWO actions support a risk-based investment decision?
options: Incorporate emerging fraud patterns and likely customer impacts when reviewing controls.
Approve the most expensive preventive tool before assessing exposure
Reassess evolving inherent risk, current controls, residual risk and priorities before allocating resources
Delay all spending until a confirmed fraud event occurs
Allocate identical resources to all products regardless of risk
questions.explanation: Fraud risk investments should follow an updated enterprise risk assessment, control evaluation and prioritization of material residual exposures.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Principles for an effective fraud risk assessment
questions.sourceSection: Principles for an effective fraud risk assessment

questions.stem: Several channels use conflicting names for identical scam patterns, weakening enterprise reporting and control mapping. What should be standardized FIRST to make cross-unit assessment consistent?
options: All product-level transaction limits to one number
Fraud taxonomy and associated scheme classifications
The customer reimbursement threshold alone
Investigator headcount in every business line
questions.explanation: A common fraud taxonomy consistently identifies risk typologies across products and businesses, supporting targeted control design and reporting.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management framework
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management framework

questions.stem: A card issuer reports lower approved volume because most flagged users are genuine. Which TWO metrics or analyses should influence the success assessment?
options: Compare confirmed fraud caught against legitimate transaction declines by customer segment.
Only how often analysts log into the system
Only the count of rule triggers
Number of new marketing campaigns
Customer friction and false-positive impact alongside prevented losses
questions.explanation: The guide includes unnecessary customer friction, false positives and feedback as KPIs alongside loss and mitigation outcomes.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Key performance indicators relevant for fraud risk management
questions.sourceSection: Key performance indicators relevant for fraud risk management

questions.stem: A senior cashier is being pressed by creditors, can reconcile her own cash drawer, and privately describes diversion of funds as a temporary loan. Which factor most directly creates the opportunity element of the Fraud Triangle?
options: The personal debt exerting pressure on the employee
The unchallenged ability to initiate and conceal transactions
The likely financial benefit from successfully diverting funds
The employee’s belief that the conduct is justified
questions.explanation: Opportunity is the exploitable control weakness; financial pressure and rationalization are the other two components.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud
questions.sourceSection: Fraud

questions.stem: A rapidly growing bank lacks routine senior-level visibility of fraud trends and mitigation gaps. Which TWO enhancements would strengthen governance?
options: Report only confirmed criminal convictions
Use incident lessons and audit findings to update control priorities and report the results.
Implement consistent risk reporting, assigned oversight, measurable KPIs and escalation
Allow risk decisions to remain with individual analysts only
Stop the independent audit function to reduce bureaucracy
questions.explanation: Governance provides accountability, transparent decision-making, risk metrics and regular reporting to leadership and oversight committees.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Governance and reporting for fraud risk programs
questions.sourceSection: Governance and reporting for fraud risk programs

questions.stem: A suspicious transfer is stopped before settlement but circumstances suggest attempted fraud and potential financial crime. What principle in the guide governs possible suspicious activity reporting?
options: Any staff member should independently send reports to media
Close the file because all prevented fraud is outside reporting scope
Reporting can never be considered unless money has actually moved
Consider reporting under applicable SAR/STR rules, even if a transaction did not occur
questions.explanation: The guide notes suspicious reporting may be required for attempted activity; reporting follows internal designated-officer procedures and local obligations.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · What is a suspicious activity report?
questions.sourceSection: What is a suspicious activity report?

questions.stem: In the examiner’s account of gambling debts, unsupervised journal-posting rights and the claim that a diversion is only a temporary loan, which TWO statements correctly distinguish Fraud Triangle components?
options: Opportunity arises because one person can post and reverse entries
The opportunity disappears whenever the employee expects a bonus
Pressure arising from debt is a possible motive, not the justification
Calling the diversion a temporary loan supplies a rationale for misconduct
An established personal financial need is equivalent to rationalization
questions.explanation: The employee’s “temporary loan” explanation is rationalization; unilateral journal powers create opportunity. Debt is pressure, but a motive alone is not a justification. Domain 1, p. 9.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud · page 9
questions.sourceSection: Fraud

questions.stem: An EU payment provider is strengthening electronic-payment authentication while separately reviewing permission to process personal data. Which pairing correctly aligns the two distinct objectives?
options: MAR for payments authentication; OLAF for personal-data processing
SOX for authentication; PSD2 for general data privacy
PSD2 for payment authentication; GDPR for personal-data protection
GDPR for secure customer authentication; PSD2 for insider dealing
questions.explanation: The study guide links PSD2 to secure electronic payments and authentication, while GDPR governs personal-data collection, processing and protection.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · EU anti-fraud regulations
questions.sourceSection: EU anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: During a fraud review, a customer confirms willingly providing identity documents to a friend so that the friend could apply for a credit product in the customer’s name. The customer never opened or controlled the resulting account. Which classification in the guide most precisely fits that consensual conduct?
options: False chargeback as first-party fraud
Consensual identity theft as second-party fraud
Unintentional money muling
Account takeover as third-party fraud
questions.explanation: The guide places knowing provision of one’s personal information for another person’s fraud under consensual identity theft, a second-party type. It is not involuntary identity compromise. Domain 1, p. 15.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Types of fraud · page 15
questions.sourceSection: Types of fraud

questions.stem: A lender focuses on onboarding validation yet fails to control authorized device changes during account servicing. Which redesign best follows the guide’s fraud mitigation life cycle?
options: Eliminate preventive controls if ongoing monitoring exists
Concentrate every control exclusively on account origination
Manage risk only when a claim reaches the fraud unit
Implement controls through onboarding, account use, transaction activity and exit
questions.explanation: Fraud mitigation spans the customer relationship: identity proofing at onboarding, ongoing authentication/monitoring and controlled exit.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud mitigation life cycle
questions.sourceSection: Fraud mitigation life cycle

questions.stem: A US consumer disputes an unauthorized electronic transfer, and operations staff suggest applying corporate invoice-recovery rules instead. Which source-derived response fits the transaction type BEST?
options: Rely exclusively on SOX accounting certification requirements
Treat the claim as deliberate chargeback fraud by default
Apply Regulation E’s consumer electronic-transfer protections and investigate the reported transaction
Apply the UK Fraud Act as the primary US payment-dispute rule
questions.explanation: The guide identifies Regulation E as the US framework for unauthorized electronic transfers and associated investigations.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · US anti-fraud regulations
questions.sourceSection: US anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: A new institution has no previous examples of a low-frequency fraud with very high possible losses. Which tool best probes this risk during the assessment?
options: Only historical mean transaction size
Replacing the entire audit function with dashboards
Randomly lowering all transaction limits
Scenario analysis of low-likelihood, high-impact events
questions.explanation: The guide highlights scenario analysis for risks that are unlikely but capable of producing severe losses.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques
questions.sourceSection: Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques

questions.stem: A third-party IT provider needs access to customer-linked infrastructure for an anti-fraud integration. Which TWO controls are most relevant before and during the vendor relationship?
options: Limit review to the vendor’s advertised product price
Monitor the provider’s relevant access privileges and risk throughout the relationship.
Assess vendor screening and cybersecurity compliance before onboarding
Conduct screening solely after a confirmed breach
Check only whether its marketing team has positive customer reviews
questions.explanation: KYV checks include the vendor and key persons and, where IT access is involved, relevant cybersecurity assessments.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Know your employee and vendor
questions.sourceSection: Know your employee and vendor

questions.stem: Following a fraud incident, a director assigns primary responsibility for day-to-day alert operations, fraud loss capture and corrective action to the compliance policy team. The head of fraud operations challenges the proposal. Under the guide’s three-lines model, which allocation is most appropriate?
options: The second line must perform all customer reimbursements
Fraud operations and analytics primarily execute first-line prevention, detection and response
The board should disposition individual fraud alerts
Internal audit should own and operate front-line fraud rules
questions.explanation: The first line commonly manages operational fraud prevention, detection, response, trend data and corrective action, while the second line oversees policy and risk governance. Domain 1, pp. 33–38.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Building a fraud risk management framework · page 33
questions.sourceSection: Building a fraud risk management framework

questions.topic: Criminal use of technology: layered controls
questions.stem: Criminals are using automated tools to test stolen credentials at scale. The fraud leader proposes relying on static passwords because device fingerprinting may inconvenience customers. Which response follows the guide’s approach to evolving technology-enabled threats?
options: Rely exclusively on annual audit testing
Conclude that increased transaction volume proves legitimate demand
Stop collection of all operational device and access signals
Assess and deploy layered controls proportionate to the attack mechanism and customer impact
questions.explanation: Technology-enabled fraud requires risk-based, evolving controls rather than dependence on one compromised factor. The customer effect should be assessed alongside risk reduction. Domain 1, p. 49.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Criminal use of technology · page 49
questions.sourceSection: Criminal use of technology

questions.stem: An issuer adds payment verification after account edits and observes an increase in complaints even as fraud losses fall. Which TWO actions demonstrate an effective feedback loop?
options: Eliminate all controls immediately
Analyze outcomes and customer rejection reasons, then refine controls and monitor measurable results
Treat the original control design as permanent
Assign measurable control-adjustment outcomes and check them against customer experience and fraud loss trends.
Stop collecting feedback once a new control launches
questions.explanation: A feedback loop uses incident and customer outcomes to update fraud controls, measure effectiveness and improve experience.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud incidents analysis to identify lessons learned
questions.sourceSection: Fraud incidents analysis to identify lessons learned

questions.stem: A customer knowingly gives his genuine account to an associate to circulate scam proceeds and retains a commission for each transfer. Under the study guide’s party-based classification, what is the BEST characterization?
options: Second-party fraud because the account holder knowingly collaborates
Third-party fraud because the original victim is unrelated
Third-party fraud because a recruiter initiated the contact
First-party fraud because the legitimate account belongs to the client
questions.explanation: The guide treats collaboration with another actor, including intentional money muling, as second-party fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · First-, second-, and third-party fraud
questions.sourceSection: First-, second-, and third-party fraud

questions.stem: Several issuers each see small parts of a fraud network and seek to compare compatible intelligence. Which TWO design principles best fit a responsible consortium approach?
options: A product-level system that excludes other market participants
Apply lawful information-sharing safeguards to partner data used for fraud detection.
A spreadsheet of only the bank’s resolved cases
A nonconsortium model using only internal records
A consortium model pooling permissible cross-organization fraud signals
questions.explanation: Consortium approaches combine multiple participants’ data/insights and can reveal patterns hidden within individual institutions.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Detecting fraud patterns across different products
questions.sourceSection: Detecting fraud patterns across different products

questions.stem: A regional fraud team wants to copy sensitive customer records onto unapproved removable media to facilitate an investigation. Which TWO controls should govern the proposed data sharing?
options: Limit access to relevant authorized recipients and approved secure channels.
The expected increase in fraud detection accuracy
The organization’s permitted-purpose, access, security and jurisdictional privacy requirements
Whether the recipient promises to delete the data eventually
Whether the data were originally obtained by the financial institution
questions.explanation: The guide requires lawful authority, need-to-know access, approved storage, data-use limitations and relevant jurisdictional conditions.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Data security and privacy
questions.sourceSection: Data security and privacy

questions.stem: A card issuer can either decline a suspicious authorization before completion or review the pattern in an overnight batch. Which capability uniquely supports immediate transaction intervention?
options: A customer survey completed quarterly
Annual retrospective root-cause reporting
Real-time monitoring embedded in the authorization stream
Static policy reviews with no access to transaction data
questions.explanation: The guide says real-time anti-fraud monitoring can flag and stop/decline a payment while it is being authorized.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Real-time anti-fraud monitoring
questions.sourceSection: Real-time anti-fraud monitoring

questions.stem: An assurance team needs to assess case file integrity, outlier dispositions and whether investigations were performed within standards. Which assurance activity BEST addresses this concern?
options: Cancellation of all previously closed files
A comparison of investor publicity statements
Only a customer-facing awareness video
An audit of case samples, documentation, outliers and investigation KPIs
questions.explanation: The guide describes auditing investigation files, performance metrics, high-value cases, outliers and methodology to assess compliance and quality.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Auditing fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Auditing fraud investigations

questions.stem: A bank has documented dual authorization for high-value wires. An assessment finds that one employee routinely logs in using a colleague’s credentials, so every payment appears to have two approvals. What is the key failure?
options: The risk is eliminated because the policy is written
Two approvals are always sufficient even if credential sharing occurs
The primary issue is transaction seasonality
Control design exists but operational enforcement and access integrity are ineffective
questions.explanation: Documented controls are not effective when personnel can bypass their operation; testing should assess execution, not just policy existence. Domain 1, pp. 55–56.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common gaps in fraud prevention · page 56
questions.sourceSection: Common gaps in fraud prevention

questions.stem: An institution has informal fraud playbooks but no documented policy for ownership, suspicious-activity escalation or staff responsibilities. Which policy design feature most directly prevents gaps when a significant fraud event occurs?
options: Defined responsibilities, escalation paths and applicable control procedures
Only a public advertisement describing zero tolerance
Removal of management discretion from every case regardless of context
Confidential exclusion of the compliance function
questions.explanation: Formal fraud risk management policies establish role ownership, reporting and processes rather than relying on informal expectations. Domain 1, pp. 62–63.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management policies and procedures · page 62
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management policies and procedures

questions.stem: A bank runs identical generic fraud awareness sessions for all employees. The wire payments group experiences repeated impersonated-CEO payment requests that were not included in training. Which improvement best addresses this gap?
options: Tell staff to act only after completed fraud losses
Reduce training to a one-time onboarding slide
Tailor staff exercises to their fraud exposures and test applied response actions
Rely exclusively on awareness of retail coupon fraud
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes anti-fraud training aligned to actual roles and evolving fraud methods. Domain 1, p. 68.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Anti-fraud staff training · page 68
questions.sourceSection: Anti-fraud staff training

questions.stem: An issuer proposes collecting mobile device location to corroborate a claimed account takeover. Which additional requirement does the supplied guide highlight?
options: Retain precise location data indefinitely for convenience
Device location is a substitute for every other identity factor
Obtain relevant opt-in/consent and meet privacy requirements for location tracking
Location data can always be captured without customer consent
questions.explanation: The guide notes that device intelligence may leverage geolocation, but location tracking requires relevant customer permission under privacy rules.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud detection tools
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection tools

questions.stem: A fraud unit has excellent identity proofing and a strong transaction detector, but their results cannot be linked at the customer level. Investigators cannot see whether new account anomalies precede suspicious payments. Which portfolio characteristic is missing?
options: Purchase of more disconnected tools with duplicate functions
Removal of identity controls from onboarding
Integration of relevant fraud intelligence across tools and stages
A higher number of standalone vendor contracts
questions.explanation: An effective anti-fraud technology portfolio must support complementary controls and usable signals, rather than isolated capabilities. Domain 1, p. 72.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Best practices for setting up an anti-fraud technology portfolio · page 72
questions.sourceSection: Best practices for setting up an anti-fraud technology portfolio

questions.stem: A coordinated attack causes mass fraudulent payments, but teams disagree on whom to notify and when to secure evidence. Which THREE measures make the coordinated initial response defensible?
options: Assign containment steps with a cross-functional response team and escalation owner.
A single business-unit spreadsheet without escalation rules
An investigator’s personal email archive
Protect evidence and document key internal/external communication contacts and timing.
A policy to postpone triage until all customers complain
A predefined response plan detailing responsibilities, communication, time frames and evidence handling
questions.explanation: The response plan provides event triggers, roles, communications, timing and procedures for evidence protection.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud response plan
questions.sourceSection: Fraud response plan

questions.stem: An insurer has fraud detection procedures but no anti-retaliation provisions for staff who report internal fraud. Which TWO missing policy provisions matter most?
options: Define confidential escalation and response ownership when internal fraud is reported.
A requirement that staff ignore anonymous information
A whistleblower reporting route and protection against reprisals
A monthly advertising plan
Exemption of managers from anti-fraud policy
questions.explanation: The guide includes mechanisms to report internal and external fraud and explicit whistleblower protections as fraud policy components.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management policies and procedures
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management policies and procedures

questions.stem: A business line wants to keep processing transactions despite breach of the enterprise fraud tolerance limit. Which framework element most clearly determines whether the proposed exposure is acceptable?
options: The organization’s formally defined fraud risk appetite or thresholds
An individual investigator’s personal risk preference
The number of operational review meetings held annually
Historical customer onboarding volumes
questions.explanation: Fraud risk appetite defines the risk/loss range the organization is willing to accept and governs escalation and mitigation priorities.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management framework
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management framework

questions.stem: Staff approving wire transfers face CEO fraud, but training covers only retail card theft. Which TWO improvements would best address the training gap?
options: Train only specialist fraud investigators
Refresh guidance as new scams emerge and measure staff understanding after training.
Use continuous, role-specific scenarios, escalation instructions and emerging typologies
Deliver only one course at hiring and discontinue refreshers
Avoid operational examples because they may bias staff
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes periodic education, role-specific use cases, emerging trends and employee response responsibilities.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Anti-fraud staff training
questions.sourceSection: Anti-fraud staff training

questions.stem: After a highly publicized fraud event, the bank compensates direct losses but later loses customers and faces supervisory questions. Which TWO additional consequences belong in a comprehensive fraud impact assessment?
options: Regulatory scrutiny and ongoing operational burden can remain material
The review should include lost customer relationships and future business
Reimbursing a fraud claim always eliminates reputational consequences
Indirect effects must be excluded unless a criminal court orders payment
Once customers are compensated, future revenue effects cannot be attributed to a fraud event
questions.explanation: Fraud consequences may extend to attrition, reduced future business, reputational damage and operational or regulatory consequences. Repayment alone is not a full impact assessment. Domain 1, pp. 16–21.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Reputational impact of fraud · page 20
questions.sourceSection: Reputational impact of fraud

questions.stem: A card issuer identifies extensive raw fraud exposure but also verifies that layered controls operate effectively. What does residual risk describe in this assessment?
options: Total gross exposure before any mitigation
Potential losses prevented by anti-fraud controls alone
Exposure remaining after considering the effectiveness of controls
Risk transferred entirely to the customer by terms and conditions
questions.explanation: Inherent risk is exposure before mitigation. Residual risk is the exposure remaining after relevant controls are considered.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Risk-based approach to fraud prevention
questions.sourceSection: Risk-based approach to fraud prevention

questions.stem: The finance committee of a public issuer examines unreliable books and deficient internal controls supporting its disclosures. Which framework in the guide MOST directly addresses financial-reporting governance and control accuracy?
options: The UK Payment Services Regulations
Sarbanes-Oxley Act
Dodd-Frank consumer whistleblower provisions alone
Regulation E
questions.explanation: The study guide associates SOX with corporate governance, accurate financial records and financial-reporting controls of public companies.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · US anti-fraud regulations
questions.sourceSection: US anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: A fraud network routes small transfers through deposit, card and wallet products. None of the product teams sees an unusual volume in isolation. Which design change most directly exposes the coordinated activity?
options: Cross-product analysis using linked customer and transaction identifiers
Treating each product’s confirmed losses as unrelated
Elimination of transaction timestamps
Separate threshold reviews that cannot share information
questions.explanation: Fraud patterns spanning different products can remain hidden until consistent identifiers and information are analyzed together. Domain 1, p. 74.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Detecting fraud patterns across different products · page 74
questions.sourceSection: Detecting fraud patterns across different products

questions.stem: A payment service is able to generate fraud scores before settlement but the operational team reviews the results only the following morning. Which improvement would change the tool from primarily retrospective detection toward prevention?
options: Stop logging real-time timestamps
Connect sufficiently reliable alerts to appropriate pre-settlement interventions
Increase only the frequency of monthly fraud committees
Publish daily reports after payments have irreversibly settled
questions.explanation: Real-time monitoring has additional preventative value when actionable alerts trigger interventions while payments can still be stopped or challenged. Domain 1, p. 75.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Real-time anti-fraud monitoring · page 75
questions.sourceSection: Real-time anti-fraud monitoring

questions.stem: A bank needs to test an allegation that an employee manufactured an authorization to transfer customer funds. Which combination of internal evidence most directly tests who initiated and approved the instruction?
options: A marketing forecast and general economic statistics
Only publicly available news articles about the bank
The employee’s job title without access history
System access logs, workflow approvals and relevant transaction records
questions.explanation: Internal transaction, audit and access records can corroborate timing and responsibility in a suspected fraud. The guide identifies internal investigation sources. Domain 1, p. 78.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud investigation sources · page 78
questions.sourceSection: Fraud investigation sources

questions.stem: A review team must distinguish institutional fraud oversight from EU privacy law while investigating suspected misuse of EU-supported funds. Which TWO descriptions correctly match the guide?
options: OLAF is the main consumer card authentication regulation
GDPR independently prosecutes all EU grant fraud
GDPR provides rules for personal-data collection and processing
PSD2 is designed primarily as the EU’s anti-bribery law
OLAF addresses fraud, corruption and misconduct affecting EU financial interests
questions.explanation: The guide differentiates OLAF’s fraud-related EU budget role from GDPR’s personal-data governance. Domain 1, p. 25.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · EU anti-fraud regulations · page 25
questions.sourceSection: EU anti-fraud regulations

questions.topic: Regional regulations: UK Fraud Act offenses
questions.stem: A UK review distinguishes intentional deception from negligent accounting and is cataloguing principal fraud offenses. Which TWO statements are consistent with the guide’s UK Fraud Act taxonomy?
options: Dishonest false representations used for financial gain can fall within the UK Fraud Act
The Act treats any inadvertent accounting error as criminal fraud
The three offenses exclude abuse of position
Failing to disclose required information can constitute a specified fraud offense
The Act defines financial crime only through unauthorized electronic transfers
questions.explanation: The guide identifies false representation, failure to disclose information and abuse of position; the offenses depend on dishonest intent rather than mere mistake. Domain 1, p. 26.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · UK anti-fraud regulations · page 26
questions.sourceSection: UK anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: Senior management agrees to strengthen fraud controls but cannot track which projects address the most serious gaps first. Which TWO features make the roadmap actionable?
options: Move all action items to the next annual audit without interim review
Approve every control with identical urgency
Track solely total project spending
Reassess priorities and delivery progress when fraud patterns or control test results change.
Build a risk-prioritized implementation roadmap with owners, milestones, resources and monitoring
questions.explanation: The guide calls for a timeline-driven fraud control roadmap prioritizing high-impact residual risks, ownership and measurable delivery.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Creating a road map for enhancing fraud controls
questions.sourceSection: Creating a road map for enhancing fraud controls

questions.stem: A bank identifies an international wire suspected of fraud and is evaluating recovery action before relevant windows close. Which combination is BEST supported by the guide?
options: Issue a chargeback under card rules for every SWIFT wire
Wait until a criminal conviction before initiating permitted recovery attempts
Assume all cross-border payments can be cancelled automatically at any time
Use available recalls/reversals, contact relevant institutions and preserve documentation within time limits
questions.explanation: The guide identifies prompt cross-institutional engagement, applicable ACH/wire reversals, SWIFT recall options, and compliance with time windows.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Methods of recovering funds lost due to fraud
questions.sourceSection: Methods of recovering funds lost due to fraud

questions.stem: A young job seeker believes an urgent employment opportunity requires using their own account for third-party transfers. Which TWO investigative practices are appropriate?
options: Close any related account without victim-sensitive engagement
Assume a defined age group is automatically culpable
Probe possible coercion or manipulation without assuming guilt from vulnerability alone.
Exclude emotional indicators because only hard transaction values matter
Evaluate the individual’s circumstances, coercion, urgency and exploitation indicators
questions.explanation: Vulnerability, urgency and digital manipulation can increase risk; contextual assessment and customer-sensitive controls are appropriate.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common characteristics of fraud victims
questions.sourceSection: Common characteristics of fraud victims

questions.stem: An internal audit finds that a payments control is disabled during overnight processing. First-line managers restore the control and claim the issue is closed. Which TWO activities maintain the separation of responsibilities described by the guide?
options: Internal audit assumes permanent ownership of the overnight process
A successful control retest makes the original fraud event irrelevant
The business prevents audit access until management certifies completion
The responsible business implements and monitors remediation
Internal audit independently assesses the control and evidence
questions.explanation: Management owns operational remediation; audit provides independent challenge and assurance rather than operating the control. Closure should rest on evidence, not management assertion alone. Domain 1, pp. 33–34.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Building a fraud risk management framework · page 34
questions.sourceSection: Building a fraud risk management framework

questions.stem: A screening vendor changes its engine, which remains operational but misses new attacks. Which TWO actions are consistent with the guide’s vendor management principles?
options: Postpone risk assessment until the original outsourcing contract expires
Review the change through vendor oversight and remediation governance
Assess whether changed detection performance undermines the outsourced fraud control
Treat uptime compliance as conclusive proof that fraud risk is managed
Assume an outsourced model removes first-line oversight duties
questions.explanation: Vendor oversight must consider substantive control performance and changes, not merely availability; the institution remains responsible for fraud governance. Domain 1, p. 35.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Best practices for fraud risk management · page 35
questions.sourceSection: Best practices for fraud risk management

questions.stem: A bank with little loss history is assessing a potentially catastrophic coordinated fraud. Which TWO uses of scenario analysis are justified by the study guide?
options: Explore control effectiveness and consequences for low-frequency exposures
Use scenario outputs as a substitute for every other assessment technique
Assign zero risk to any threat missing from historic loss data
Construct plausible severe events even if they have never occurred locally
Treat hypothetical scenarios as proof that a specific employee is criminal
questions.explanation: Scenario analysis can examine plausible, low-frequency but severe threats and inform control discussions. It neither proves wrongdoing nor replaces other risk assessment inputs. Domain 1, p. 41.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques · page 41
questions.sourceSection: Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques

questions.stem: A UK applicant knowingly makes a false representation to obtain an unjust financial advantage. Which statement BEST captures the UK Fraud Act taxonomy in the guide?
options: Only false representation is an offense; nondisclosure is solely regulatory
The Act applies only when customer funds are transferred electronically
False representation, failure to disclose and abuse of position are three covered offense types
Fraud requires confirmed realized loss in every case
questions.explanation: The guide lists false representation, failure to disclose information and abuse of position, focusing on dishonesty and intent to gain or cause loss or risk of loss.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · UK anti-fraud regulations
questions.sourceSection: UK anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: A fraud investigator finds a social-media post alleging that a corporate beneficiary is fictitious. The account is anonymous and no corroborating registry or other evidence has been obtained. What treatment is most defensible?
options: Use the allegation as an investigative lead and corroborate it through appropriate sources
Notify all customers that the beneficiary is criminal
Treat the anonymous post as conclusive proof of fraud
Disregard all public information as inadmissible in any investigation
questions.explanation: External information may help identify leads but should be checked for credibility and corroboration before being treated as established fact. Domain 1, p. 79.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud investigations external data sources · page 79
questions.sourceSection: Fraud investigations external data sources

questions.stem: An applicant combines a genuine identification number with invented name and address details and requests a new credit card. Which classification is MOST consistent with the guide’s typology table?
options: Account takeover through existing customer credentials
Third-party full-identity theft
Synthetic first-party fraud occurring at origination
Deliberate chargeback fraud after fulfillment
questions.explanation: The guide explicitly classifies synthetic identities using real and made-up data as synthetic first-party fraud at origination.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Origination fraud risk
questions.sourceSection: Origination fraud risk

questions.stem: Front-line specialists list fraud scenarios and assess likelihood, loss severity and existing controls in a business line. Which TWO practices reflect effective line-of-business risk and control self-assessment?
options: Identify risks; assess impact and likelihood; evaluate controls; develop action plans
Assign accountable owners and timelines to documented high-priority remedial measures.
Test model precision; select vendor; automate reporting; perform annual training
Assign corrective plans; define appetite; ignore controls; assign blame
Close all low-value accounts; interview suspects; file reports; assess loss
questions.explanation: RCSA begins with documented risks, assesses impact/likelihood, reviews controls and creates prioritized corrective action plans.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Line of business fraud risk self-assessment
questions.sourceSection: Line of business fraud risk self-assessment

questions.stem: Two data sources disagree about the apparent owner of a receiving account. An internal payment record identifies one entity while a historic external record names another. Which action makes the intelligence interpretation more reliable?
options: Select whichever interpretation supports a preferred allegation
Reconcile source timing, provenance and corroborating information before deciding
Select the external source automatically
Discard both sources without documenting the conflict
questions.explanation: Interpreting fraud intelligence involves examining provenance and consistency rather than selecting a convenient conclusion. Domain 1, p. 81.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Methods for interpreting fraud-related intelligence · page 81
questions.sourceSection: Methods for interpreting fraud-related intelligence

questions.stem: An assurance reviewer finds that investigators consistently close cases quickly but rarely record adverse evidence or explain why alerts were dismissed. Which assessment is most appropriate?
options: Review decision quality and documentation against investigation standards, not speed alone
Assess investigators solely from the number of closures
Conclude that fast closure proves high case quality
Remove evidence-retention requirements for low-value cases
questions.explanation: Auditing fraud investigations concerns adherence to standards, evidence and decision documentation rather than throughput alone. Domain 1, p. 83.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Auditing fraud investigations · page 83
questions.sourceSection: Auditing fraud investigations

questions.stem: A fraud committee must choose between an often-attempted moderate fraud and a rare potentially devastating event. Which TWO inputs should directly shape prioritization?
options: Treat all rare risks as immaterial without considering severity
Consider existing mitigation and exposure that remains after controls
Ignore the organization’s fraud risk appetite when allocating capital
Evaluate each scenario’s likelihood and potential impact
Rank threats only by the largest possible loss
questions.explanation: Risk matrices support evaluation of likelihood and impact, with residual risk and appetite informing priority. A single unadjusted figure is insufficient. Domain 1, pp. 39–42.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Line of business fraud risk self-assessment · page 42
questions.sourceSection: Line of business fraud risk self-assessment

questions.stem: A significant fraud attack affects payments, customer support, technology and legal response. Each team has taken defensible individual action but nobody is coordinating urgent interdependencies. Which capability should the formal response plan supply?
options: Unrestricted unilateral action by every team
A blanket prohibition on involving legal advisers
Replacing incident records with verbal updates
Predefined accountable incident roles and coordinated decision escalation
questions.explanation: Fraud response plans set roles, responsibilities and coordination routes to ensure consistent action across teams. Domain 1, pp. 88–91.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud response roles and responsibilities · page 89
questions.sourceSection: Fraud response roles and responsibilities

questions.stem: Customers are contacting the press about a fraud event before the institution has determined the number of affected accounts. A manager proposes releasing an exact unverified loss figure to reassure the public. Which approach is preferable?
options: Announce an invented precise figure to demonstrate control
Coordinate approved, accurate updates and make uncertainties explicit
Provide every customer with confidential investigation files
Promise that no regulatory reporting will be necessary
questions.explanation: Communication protocols during fraud incidents should support accurate, coordinated and authorized information sharing while facts are developing. Domain 1, p. 91.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Communication protocols and coordination mechanisms during fraud incidents · page 91
questions.sourceSection: Communication protocols and coordination mechanisms during fraud incidents

questions.stem: A suspicious customer account is closed after a fraud review. A case manager proposes deleting investigation records because the relationship has ended. What principle should govern the decision?
options: Relationship exit automatically ends all reporting duties
Notify the alleged fraudster of every suspicious activity filing
Erase all evidence to reduce residual fraud risk
Continue to meet applicable reporting and record-retention requirements
questions.explanation: Fraud case closure does not negate regulatory reporting and retention obligations. Domain 1, p. 93.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Complying with regulatory requirements when closing fraud cases · page 93
questions.sourceSection: Complying with regulatory requirements when closing fraud cases

questions.stem: A lender suspects that manual exception workflows allow the same individual to originate and approve accounts. Which assessment technique best reveals control gaps at workflow handoffs?
options: A review confined to aggregated annual net losses
Process mapping of end-to-end activities and control points
An isolated employee-attitude survey without workflow review
A comparison of product branding and marketing spend
questions.explanation: Process mapping exposes weaknesses in operational workflows, including omitted checks and incompatible responsibilities.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques
questions.sourceSection: Common fraud risk assessment tools and techniques

questions.stem: Head office has completed a fraud RCSA without consulting employees who operate high-risk processes. Which TWO additions best address the resulting assessment weakness?
options: Risk assessment should examine the effectiveness of current controls
An RCSA is reliable only when drafted without operational input
Staff surveys automatically replace transaction and control evidence
A risk assessment should avoid documenting action owners
Front-line practitioners should supply evidence about actual workflow and overrides
questions.explanation: The RCSA uses operational practitioners and fraud specialists to identify risks and evaluate controls; documentation and actions should follow. Domain 1, pp. 42–43.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Line of business fraud risk self-assessment · page 42
questions.sourceSection: Line of business fraud risk self-assessment

questions.stem: A victim loses funds through several routes. One transfer remains at a cooperating receiving bank; another has already been converted to untraceable consumer spending. Which recovery priority is most justified?
options: Treat all routes as equally recoverable
Assume that a victim’s reimbursement is identical to external recovery
Act urgently on traceable funds still susceptible to restriction or recall
Delay recovery until the criminal prosecution ends
questions.explanation: Recovery potential depends on payment route, timing and ability to trace or control funds; early coordinated action may improve outcomes. Domain 1, pp. 94–95.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud types with reasonable recovery potential · page 94
questions.sourceSection: Fraud types with reasonable recovery potential

questions.stem: A tax-refund season spike prompts a call to weaken identity checks so the contact center can process more claims. What is the most defensible response?
options: Apply trend-informed, tailored controls while preserving customer experience
Relax detection thresholds uniformly because traffic is unusually high
Pause analysis until the seasonal spike ends
Treat all seasonal transactions as fraudulent
questions.explanation: The guide advises adapting controls to predictable seasonal vulnerabilities without simply relaxing rules or unnecessarily harming legitimate users.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Seasonal fraud risk
questions.sourceSection: Seasonal fraud risk

questions.stem: After an apparently fraudulent wire transfer, the originating institution sends a recall request. The recipient institution confirms that funds have already been moved onward. Which statement correctly interprets the recall?
options: A recall always creates an automatic chargeback right for any payment
The originating bank is forbidden from pursuing further tracing
The beneficiary must be ignored if the recall fails
A recall is a recovery attempt, not a guarantee that the original transfer will be reversed
questions.explanation: A wire recall can support recovery but does not guarantee successful reversal, especially after onward movement. Domain 1, p. 95.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Methods of recovering funds lost due to fraud · page 95
questions.sourceSection: Methods of recovering funds lost due to fraud

questions.stem: Two financial institutions disagree over how to account for a partially recovered amount after a fraudulent payment. Why should both institutions preserve a reconciled record of claims, recoveries and amounts remitted?
options: To treat all losses as recovered once a claim is opened
To support accurate interbank settlement and avoid double recovery or inconsistent balances
To establish automatic criminal liability for the recipient bank
To remove the need to communicate with the victim
questions.explanation: The guide treats settlement of fraud-related recoveries between institutions as an accountable reconciliation process. Domain 1, p. 97.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Settling fraud-related fund recoveries between financial institutions · page 97
questions.sourceSection: Settling fraud-related fund recoveries between financial institutions

questions.stem: An institution segments fraud exposure by customer, jurisdiction, product and channel. Which TWO interpretations of those dimensions are appropriate?
options: Channel examines how a customer accesses or initiates services
A customer’s domicile always determines the physical location of the payment device
Customer risk and channel risk must be treated as a single identical variable
Jurisdiction evaluates geographic and cross-border exposure
Product risk is irrelevant when all customers have been onboarded
questions.explanation: The four transactional dimensions are distinct: customer, jurisdiction, product and channel. Geography and access mode can contribute independently. Domain 1, p. 44.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Transactional fraud risk: Customer, jurisdiction, product, channel · page 44
questions.sourceSection: Transactional fraud risk: Customer, jurisdiction, product, channel

questions.topic: Duty to report: suspicion versus proof
questions.stem: Investigators detect apparent money-mule activity but cannot yet establish a criminal conviction or identify every underlying victim. A team leader states reporting can be considered only after the suspect admits fraud. What is the strongest response?
options: Close the case because criminal intent is not proven beyond doubt
Automatically file an identical report in every jurisdiction
Evaluate reporting obligations based on applicable suspicion thresholds, without waiting for conviction
Tell the customer that investigators will report only after confession
questions.explanation: Suspicious-activity reporting duties can arise from reasonable suspicion and applicable rules, not necessarily criminal proof or confession. Domain 1, pp. 98–100.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Duty to report fraud · page 98
questions.sourceSection: Duty to report fraud

questions.stem: A relationship manager asks whether a suspicious activity report has been filed about a customer, intending to share the answer with that customer to explain an account restriction. Which principle should govern access and communication?
options: Post the filing status in the public customer portal
Use a copy of the report as the default customer notification
Disclose any filing whenever a commercial relationship is long-standing
Follow confidentiality and authorized information-sharing rules for suspicious activity reporting
questions.explanation: The guide addresses policies and procedures governing suspicious activity reports; reporting information should be handled according to applicable confidentiality and authorization requirements. Domain 1, p. 100.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Suspicious activity reports policies and procedures · page 100
questions.sourceSection: Suspicious activity reports policies and procedures

questions.stem: A lender observes fabricated employment and unverifiable addresses in applications not yet funded. Which TWO actions address origination fraud at its most relevant control point?
options: Rely only on suspicious transaction alerts after the loan is disbursed
Replace identity checks with annual profit forecasts
Use application consistency and independent verification as preventive inputs
Validate identity and supporting details during origination before funding
Assume a syntactically valid identity number establishes a real customer
questions.explanation: Origination fraud is best mitigated with information and identity checks before creating and funding the relationship. Later surveillance can complement, not replace, onboarding controls. Domain 1, p. 45.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Origination fraud risk · page 45
questions.sourceSection: Origination fraud risk

questions.stem: An operations user can create suppliers, change bank details, approve payments and suppress exceptions. Which TWO controls most directly address the resulting fraud opportunity?
options: Let the same manager approve and self-certify all transfers
Use independently reviewed audit trails and reconciliations
Treat maker-checker controls as unnecessary when transactions are electronic
Separate vendor creation from payment authorization
Prevent auditors from reviewing privileged users
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties and independent review help prevent one actor from creating, releasing and concealing fraudulent payments. Domain 1, pp. 46 and 55–56.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Operational processes fraud risk · page 46
questions.sourceSection: Operational processes fraud risk

questions.stem: A borrower opens credit in their real identity, makes disciplined payments, obtains a higher limit and then draws it down with no intention to repay. Which fraud scheme BEST explains the full sequence?
options: Bust-out fraud using a real identity and cultivated repayment history
A simple online card-not-present testing attack
Accidental chargeback caused by merchant description ambiguity
Conventional stolen-identity account takeover
questions.explanation: Bust-out fraud involves establishing legitimate-looking credit performance, increasing credit availability and deliberately exhausting it without repayment intent.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Origination fraud risk
questions.sourceSection: Origination fraud risk

questions.topic: UK APP reimbursement rules as described in guide
questions.stem: A UK bank is designing APP scam reimbursement procedures using only the numeric provisions stated in the supplied study guide. Which guide-based loss allocation is identified?
options: All loss is attributed to the sending PSP
The receiving PSP alone must reimburse the customer
The loss is split equally between sending and receiving PSPs
Liability is decided entirely by the customer’s authentication method
questions.explanation: The supplied guide describes a 50/50 reimbursement split between sending and receiving payment service providers; this is a guide-based study fact, not an independently updated legal check.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · UK anti-fraud regulations
questions.sourceSection: UK anti-fraud regulations

questions.stem: The fraud program presents a 30% fall in detected alerts as proof that fraud is declining. Customer complaints and confirmed losses, however, have risen. Which interpretation is most responsible?
options: Assume a smaller alert count always proves a safer environment
Discard loss data because alert counts are newer
Raise alert thresholds until all monitoring becomes silent
Review detection coverage and independent loss or complaint indicators before claiming improvement
questions.explanation: Fraud KPIs should be triangulated: reduced alerts can reflect weakened controls rather than lower fraud exposure. Domain 1, p. 101.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Key performance indicators relevant for fraud risk management · page 101
questions.sourceSection: Key performance indicators relevant for fraud risk management

questions.stem: An anti-fraud team anticipates a surge of attempted refund fraud during a predictable retail sales period. Which TWO preparations best reflect risk-based seasonal fraud management?
options: Arrange operational capacity to manage expected alert volumes
Disable all fraud rules until peak purchases pass
Analyze prior seasonal typologies and adapt relevant controls
Treat all seasonal transactions as fraudulent
Exclude customer-friction indicators from review
questions.explanation: Seasonal trends should influence control preparation and resourcing, without indiscriminate suspension of safeguards or disregard of genuine customers. Domain 1, p. 47.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Seasonal fraud risk · page 47
questions.sourceSection: Seasonal fraud risk

questions.stem: A cardholder disputes a fulfilled purchase despite reliable evidence that the goods were received. Which TWO conclusions can a careful fraud review support?
options: A chargeback claim itself is not sufficient proof of intentional fraud
A disputed purchase becomes fraudulent solely because it was made online
Verification of merchant fulfillment is irrelevant to the review
Every customer dispute is necessarily a third-party account takeover
Corroborating delivery and customer participation may indicate dishonest first-party dispute behavior
questions.explanation: The guide describes first-party chargeback abuse, but investigation evidence is needed to distinguish deliberate misrepresentation from a valid dispute. Domain 1, pp. 14–15 and 48.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · First-party transaction fraud · page 48
questions.sourceSection: First-party transaction fraud

questions.stem: An annual review confirms that fraud policies and technology contracts exist, but does not sample actual alerts, approvals or customer outcomes. What material limitation should the assurance report disclose?
options: Having policies means operational testing is unnecessary
A vendor contract proves fraud loss is within appetite
A control never needs retesting after deployment
The review cannot conclude operating effectiveness from design evidence alone
questions.explanation: Program assurance should evaluate whether the fraud framework operates effectively, not merely whether documentation exists. Domain 1, pp. 102–103.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management program assurance review · page 102
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management program assurance review

questions.stem: A fraud program review identifies multiple gaps and produces 20 recommendations, but the next committee meeting shows no owners, milestones or closure evidence. Which correction most directly turns findings into improvement?
options: Mark all observations closed when the report is issued
Assign accountable owners, prioritized deadlines and evidence-based monitoring
Transfer every operational fix to internal audit
Replace remediation with a statement that fraud risk is unavoidable
questions.explanation: An assurance review should result in managed corrective actions with traceable progress and ownership. Domain 1, p. 103.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management program review process · page 103
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management program review process

questions.stem: An elderly customer receiving unusual requests from an online companion appears anxious about urgent transfers. Which TWO practices best balance fraud prevention and fair treatment?
options: Customer education can address pressure and secrecy associated with scams
Protective questioning should assess manipulation without assigning guilt prematurely
The bank should disclose a customer’s allegations publicly to deter scams
A beneficiary cannot be questioned if a payment was authorized
Age alone proves a customer knowingly assisted fraud
questions.explanation: Victim vulnerability and manipulation justify proportionate inquiry and awareness, not unsupported culpability judgments. Domain 1, p. 50.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common characteristics of fraud victims · page 50
questions.sourceSection: Common characteristics of fraud victims

questions.stem: Two institutions suffer similar phishing-led account takeovers. One merely restores affected customer balances; the other traces authentication breakdowns and updates training, controls and monitoring. Which distinction matters for future fraud risk?
options: Keeping customer claims out of the incident review
Assuming compensation eliminates the original vulnerability
Reducing executive reporting once refunds are completed
Using root-cause lessons to improve prevention and detection rather than only settling immediate losses
questions.explanation: Incident analysis supports improvements to control design, fraud awareness and responses so that repeated incidents are less likely. Domain 1, p. 105.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud incidents analysis to identify lessons learned · page 105
questions.sourceSection: Fraud incidents analysis to identify lessons learned

questions.stem: An issuer repeatedly reimburses scam victims but does not change its processes after investigations. Which TWO feedback activities would make the mitigation life cycle more effective?
options: Investigative outcomes should feed revised detection or preventive controls
Fraud control rules should remain unchanged after repeated documented failures
The response phase is complete once funds are reimbursed even if the cause persists
A closed case can never support a new fraud typology assessment
Root-cause findings should inform awareness and operating procedures
questions.explanation: The mitigation life cycle incorporates learning from fraud response to strengthen prevention, detection and governance. Domain 1, p. 57.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud mitigation life cycle · page 57
questions.sourceSection: Fraud mitigation life cycle

questions.stem: Retail card controls are copied unchanged into a corporate wire platform with material mandate and authorization risks. Which TWO redesign principles are supported by the guide?
options: Line-of-business risk assessments should inform applicable safeguards
Controls should reflect differences between wholesale wire mandates and retail card fraud
Corporate signatory controls can be omitted if the organization uses fraud scoring
Different payment products cannot have different fraud typologies
An institution must apply exactly the same customer authentication to all products
questions.explanation: The guide supports tailored controls driven by product, channel and line-of-business exposures rather than identical controls for every service. Domain 1, p. 60.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud controls specific to lines of business · page 60
questions.sourceSection: Fraud controls specific to lines of business

questions.topic: KYE and vendor review: ongoing due diligence
questions.stem: An approved supplier is linked to a procurement officer and new financial distress. Which TWO diligence steps are appropriate?
options: Assess employee conflicts or close supplier relationships where indicators exist
Remove all procurement controls when vendor tenure exceeds three years
Refresh the vendor’s risk and financial condition as new adverse facts emerge
Rely solely on verbal vendor assurances to close the concern
Keep prior vendor approval permanently valid without review
questions.explanation: Know-your-employee and vendor controls should address changing vendor risk and insider conflicts; historical onboarding approval is not conclusive. Domain 1, p. 61.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Know your employee and vendor · page 61
questions.sourceSection: Know your employee and vendor

questions.topic: Governance reporting: leading versus lagging measures
questions.stem: Management receives only quarterly confirmed fraud-loss totals. The fraud operations team also sees a rapid increase in suspicious authentication attempts, but no customer losses yet. Which TWO reporting enhancements would better support preventive governance?
options: Treat growing alerts as proof of confirmed fraud
Include emerging alert and attempted-fraud trends
Report control health and remediation actions to senior stakeholders
Wait until losses crystallize before informing leadership
Remove all confirmed-loss reporting
questions.explanation: Governance reporting should include evolving exposure and control performance, not merely historical loss. Attempted-fraud signals must still be distinguished from confirmed cases. Domain 1, pp. 63–65.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Governance and reporting for fraud risk programs · page 63
questions.sourceSection: Governance and reporting for fraud risk programs

questions.stem: Management must prioritize two fraud exposures: one has high inherent risk but strong controls; the other has moderate inherent risk with failed controls. Which TWO principles guide the choice?
options: Evaluate risk remaining after the effectiveness of existing controls
Spend only on the highest inherent risk regardless of compensating controls
Remove risks from the register whenever management disagrees with the rating
Treat an untested control as fully effective
Consider both consequence and likelihood when prioritizing remediation
questions.explanation: The guide calls for residual-risk assessment using control strength, likelihood and impact, then risk-based resource allocation. Domain 1, pp. 39–40 and 65.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk prioritization criteria · page 65
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk prioritization criteria

questions.stem: An employee can originate loan applications, approve them and reconcile settlement accounts alone. Which THREE actions would most directly reduce the vulnerability?
options: Periodically independently review incompatible access and exception transactions.
An increase in single-user approval limits
Separated initiation, approval and reconciliation, with effective independent checks
Restrict and log emergency overrides rather than granting routine self-approval.
An annual training module without authorization changes
A larger monthly fraud loss report
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties and effective four-eyes approval reduce the opportunity for one individual to commit and conceal internal fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Common gaps in fraud prevention
questions.sourceSection: Common gaps in fraud prevention

questions.stem: An audit tested only declined payments and concluded that wire-approval safeguards were effective. Which TWO changes would strengthen the assessment?
options: Test override pathways as well as the documented approval process
Treat the existence of dual authorization policy as definitive evidence of effectiveness
Include relevant completed transactions and exceptions when assessing control operation
Evaluate only rejected transactions as proof of all outcomes
Exclude transactions handled by senior personnel from all testing
questions.explanation: Control tests should inspect operating evidence and ways the control may fail or be bypassed, not just intended design or successful rejections. Domain 1, p. 66.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud control tests · page 66
questions.sourceSection: Fraud control tests

questions.stem: A fraud initiative proposes launching automated transaction blocks before data feeds, override governance, customer communications and appeal procedures are operational. Which roadmap improvement is most defensible?
options: Remove customer-impact testing from the delivery plan
Launch all blocks first and document any resulting errors next year
Treat technical deployment as the sole success criterion
Sequence dependencies and control readiness before activating consequential actions
questions.explanation: An implementation roadmap should coordinate practical prerequisites, responsible resources and milestones to achieve functioning controls. Domain 1, p. 106.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Creating a road map for enhancing fraud controls · page 106
questions.sourceSection: Creating a road map for enhancing fraud controls

questions.stem: A fraud program has three available projects: low-impact cosmetic reporting, a modest prevention enhancement with high residual risk reduction, and an expensive untested solution unrelated to current exposure. What is the basis for selecting the next investment?
options: Select the project that is easiest to publicize
Prioritize demonstrable mitigation of material residual risks within resource constraints
Spend equally on projects regardless of risk impact
Choose the project with the most attractive vendor presentation
questions.explanation: The guide recommends a risk-based implementation plan and prioritization of fraud controls against material exposure and available resources. Domain 1, p. 107.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Deploying a risk-based approach to fraud control prioritization · page 107
questions.sourceSection: Deploying a risk-based approach to fraud control prioritization

questions.stem: A payment provider sends fraud-awareness emails and celebrates a large delivery count. Which TWO evaluations would better test whether customers became more resilient to scams?
options: Measure whether safer behavior or reporting improves after the campaign
Count every customer who opened an email as a prevented fraud victim
Rely only on the number of awareness emails delivered
Assume that higher marketing reach proves a lower fraud loss rate
Test whether customers recognize relevant impersonation indicators
questions.explanation: The success of customer awareness depends on useful recognition and response outcomes rather than communication output volume alone. Domain 1, p. 69.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Raising customer awareness about fraud · page 69
questions.sourceSection: Raising customer awareness about fraud
