questions.stem: A previously well-rated bank suffers a severe loss after its chief executive repeatedly authorizes wires exceeding controls designed for every other employee. What general lesson from the Heartland Tri-State Bank case is most directly supported?
options: Only external hackers create existential fraud losses
Internal controls are irrelevant once an executive is trusted
A bank rated well before fraud cannot later suffer insolvency
Anti-fraud controls must apply to leadership and material overrides need effective oversight
questions.explanation: The Heartland example illustrates catastrophic executive-origin fraud and the need to apply effective controls to senior leaders as well as staff. Domain 1, p. 19.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud and financial stability (Case example: Heartland Tri-State Bank) · page 19
questions.sourceSection: Fraud and financial stability (Case example: Heartland Tri-State Bank)

questions.stem: In the Capital One case example, stolen customer personally identifiable information was transformed into counterfeit identification for branch withdrawals. Which control pairing most directly addresses both stages of that scheme?
options: Employee data-access oversight and robust identity verification at withdrawal
Removing audit trails to protect employee privacy
Assuming every document with valid personal details is genuine
Only a campaign about retail coupon redemption
questions.explanation: The case combines insider misuse of PII and fraudulent identity documents; access controls, oversight and verification are directly relevant. Domain 1, p. 23.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Data security and privacy (Case example: Capital One Bank internal fraud) · page 23
questions.sourceSection: Data security and privacy (Case example: Capital One Bank internal fraud)

questions.topic: Risk assessment: annual review and triggers
questions.stem: A fraud risk assessment was approved 11 months ago. Since then, the bank has launched instant payments, entered a new jurisdiction and encountered an emerging scam typology. Management wants to wait until the planned annual review. What does the guide’s feedback-loop approach indicate?
options: Treat annual timing as a ban on interim reassessment
Reassess only after the first confirmed financial loss
Update the risk assessment promptly when material changes occur and conduct regular reviews
Let product teams amend risk appetite without governance
questions.explanation: The guide expects fraud risk assessment to be dynamic, updated with operational and threat changes, and reviewed at least annually. Domain 1, pp. 39–40.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Principles for an effective fraud risk assessment · page 39
questions.sourceSection: Principles for an effective fraud risk assessment

questions.topic: Fraud control priorities: oversight versus operation
questions.stem: A fraud committee asks the second line of defense to become the permanent owner of all detection rules while also independently reporting whether the rules are effective. Which governance concern should be raised?
options: Operating and independently overseeing the same control can weaken separation of responsibilities
The second line must always conduct all front-line alert dispositions
A separation issue exists only when fraud losses exceed the appetite
Internal audit should not be involved in assurance
questions.explanation: The guide commonly positions operations and analytics in the first line and independent oversight in the second; governance must preserve effective challenge. Domain 1, pp. 37–38.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Key stakeholders in fraud risk management · page 38
questions.sourceSection: Key stakeholders in fraud risk management

questions.stem: A fraud incident report describes the amount stolen but omits affected systems, the control bypass, detection date and remedial actions. Which TWO additions would most improve its usefulness to governance?
options: Control deficiencies, impact and corrective actions
Suppression of uncertain findings to appear decisive
Chronology and fraud mechanism supported by evidence
A claim of zero future fraud risk
Personal opinions about the suspected actor unrelated to evidence
questions.explanation: A fraud incident report should communicate evidence-based event details, impact, control weaknesses and action, with uncertainty distinguished from findings. Domain 1, p. 82.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud incident report · page 82
questions.sourceSection: Fraud incident report

questions.stem: In the FTX case, insiders represented that sophisticated customer-asset protections existed while Alameda received exemptions to risk controls and access to customer funds. Which two failures most directly characterize the fraud risk?
options: Transparent reporting of related-party exposures
Undisclosed preferential access and diversion of customer assets
Independent review of customer-asset segregation
Strictly enforced trading limits for related parties
Misleading representations to investors about controls
questions.explanation: The guide highlights false assurances and concealed diversion or exceptions favoring Alameda, alongside failures of internal governance and safeguards. Domain 1, pp. 11–12.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Internal fraud (Case example: FTX) · page 12
questions.sourceSection: Internal fraud (Case example: FTX)

questions.stem: A business customer can initiate a high-value wire through an unrestricted account user. Which preventive arrangement from the fraud risk management process most directly reduces the opportunity for fraudulent disbursement?
options: Remove post-payment audit logs to simplify processing
Limit authorization to designated signatories with appropriate validation
Assign every payment to the same unverified username
Review only annual customer satisfaction survey responses
questions.explanation: The guide specifically notes restricted signatories and layered approval as preventive examples that reduce fraud opportunity. Domain 1, p. 36.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management process · page 36
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management process

questions.stem: Customer identity documents gathered for fraud investigations are offered to a product-marketing team for profiling. Which TWO issues must be addressed before considering any secondary use?
options: Whether files can be copied onto personal USB drives
Applicable privacy and permitted information-sharing requirements
Whether all records can be retained indefinitely
Whether processing is authorized for the new purpose
Whether marketing has more staff than fraud
questions.explanation: The guide stresses authorized purpose, access, retention and sharing controls for customer data, including restrictions on repurposing information. Domain 1, p. 22.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Data security and privacy · page 22
questions.sourceSection: Data security and privacy

questions.stem: A new fraud safeguard challenges every customer transaction regardless of risk. The resulting abandonment rate is high while confirmed fraud reduction is marginal. Which redesign would be most proportionate?
options: Strengthen every challenge equally, regardless of risk
Judge effectiveness only by the number of extra prompts
Remove the ability to monitor false positives
Apply more friction to higher-risk activity and measure fraud losses alongside genuine-customer disruption
questions.explanation: Fraud control design should manage risk while considering customer experience and false positives; indiscriminate friction is not necessarily more effective. Domain 1, pp. 58–60.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Developing fraud controls for organizations · page 58
questions.sourceSection: Developing fraud controls for organizations

questions.stem: Two business divisions report “account compromise,” but one includes coerced authorized payments and the other records only stolen credentials. What specific improvement would make fraud-loss reporting comparable?
options: Let each division classify identical events differently
Stop collecting information about payment authorization
Aggregate all suspected losses under a generic operational error label
Define taxonomy criteria distinguishing social engineering from unauthorized account access
questions.explanation: A shared fraud taxonomy supports consistent risk identification, controls and comparisons; superficially similar outcomes can involve different fraud mechanisms. Domain 1, pp. 32–33.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Fraud risk management framework · page 32
questions.sourceSection: Fraud risk management framework

description: 100 questions covering fraud governance, risk assessment, prevention, response and remediation.

title: Fraud Detection and Analytics
name: Fraud Detection and Analytics
subtitle: Domain 2 Knowledge Assessment

questions.stem: A fraud engine aggregates predictions from several algorithms rather than using one stand-alone detector. What technique is being employed?
options: Isolated scalar thresholding only
Ensemble learning
Manual case archival
Data extraction without modeling
questions.explanation: The guide discusses ensemble approaches that aggregate multiple models to improve robustness and detection.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Ensemble methods
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Ensemble methods

questions.stem: A pensioner typically pays domestic bills monthly, then makes three unusually high transfers to a new overseas payee in one afternoon. Which analytic comparison most directly supports an initial fraud-risk assessment?
options: Use the customer’s oldest completed KYC form as the only detection input
Compare transactions against the customer’s historical behavior and relevant context
Measure the institution’s annual aggregate assets instead of behavior
Automatically label every international payment fraud
questions.explanation: Descriptive and behavior-based analytics compare new events with established customer patterns, amounts, frequency and recipient characteristics.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags
questions.sourceSection: Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags

questions.stem: Across one week, accounts show unusually similar login-device patterns followed by repeat transfers to a clustered set of payees. What is the strongest analytical rationale for linking these alerts?
options: Any customer using mobile banking must be part of a criminal network
Common geography alone is sufficient proof of fraud
Every account shows identical total balances
The shared behavioral sequence may reveal a coordinated fraud typology
questions.explanation: Repeated combinations of behavioral indicators and linked flows can reveal patterns that isolated transaction reviews miss.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions
questions.sourceSection: Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions

questions.topic: Seasonal threats and controlled rule changes
questions.stem: Ahead of a regional holiday shopping surge, an e-commerce issuer sees a rising proportion of unusual first-time merchants, and last year's rule produced considerable false positives. Management proposes relaxing every restriction on transaction velocity for the entire holiday season. What is the BEST analytics response?
options: Apply last year’s thresholds unchanged because seasonal changes mainly affect transaction volume rather than fraud behavior.
Reduce every fraud rule threshold simultaneously so that fraudulent activity is intercepted, regardless of staffing impact.
Suspend the existing velocity rule entirely for the peak weeks, then restore it once transaction volume normalizes.
Assess seasonal fraud and legitimate transaction patterns by product and channel, make risk-targeted rule changes, and monitor both fraud capture and false positives.
questions.explanation: The guide calls for continued rule review and adaptation to emerging/seasonal trends while balancing protection with customer impact.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection rules review
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection rules review

questions.stem: A fraud team possesses a large history of transactions reliably classified as fraudulent or legitimate. Which machine-learning approach best fits the available labels?
options: Unsupervised clustering without considering past outcomes
An unvalidated model trained only on one fraud case
Supervised learning using correctly labeled historical examples
Rule deletion followed by purely random sampling
questions.explanation: Supervised learning learns from labeled examples of fraudulent and legitimate outcomes, unlike unsupervised pattern discovery.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection
questions.sourceSection: Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection

questions.stem: A new analytics project must locate payment and CRM data sources before deciding how to normalize attributes. Which stage is being performed FIRST?
options: Final model deployment
Model bias assessment
Data extraction and sourcing
Feature evaluation
questions.explanation: Extraction identifies the needed datasets and obtains them from source systems; cleaning and transformation follow.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Anti-fraud data extraction
questions.sourceSection: Anti-fraud data extraction

questions.stem: An anti-fraud analytics team detects an increase in a new payment scam. The team produces an accurate trend dashboard, but operations never changes its safeguards. What must happen for analytics to contribute to prevention rather than observation alone?
options: A dashboard alone automatically blocks new attacks
Confirmed fraud figures should be deleted once a chart is produced
The data should be kept separate from fraud operations
Insights should inform risk-based controls and operational action
questions.explanation: Fraud analytics adds preventive value when data-driven insights are translated into controls, timely interventions and monitoring. Fraud Detection and Analytics, pp. 8–10.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · What is fraud analytics? · page 8
questions.sourceSection: What is fraud analytics?

questions.stem: Analysts want to consume an external fraud feed containing sensitive personal information but have not assessed sharing authority. What should be resolved before integrating the data?
options: Only whether the data source is inexpensive
Whether the data can be imported with the existing file format
Legal access, privacy permissions, provenance and suitability for the detection purpose
Whether the source includes some high-profile examples
questions.explanation: Data sources need relevance, reliable provenance and lawful access; sharing and privacy restrictions must be respected.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · External sources of data for analytics
questions.sourceSection: External sources of data for analytics

questions.stem: The guide describes fraud analytics being used in a counterattack against changing fraud behavior. Which sequence best represents the underlying analytics process?
options: Freeze all rules indefinitely after the first successful detection
Observe patterns, identify vulnerabilities, adapt detection and monitor outcomes
Replace analytic evidence with a fixed list of criminal names
Classify every new customer as fraudulent
questions.explanation: The fraud counterattack case illustrates using observed fraud patterns to adjust fraud detection and response rather than treating rules as static. Domain 2, p. 9.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · What is fraud analytics? (Case example: Fraud counterattack) · page 9
questions.sourceSection: What is fraud analytics? (Case example: Fraud counterattack)

questions.stem: An insurance claim includes a provider address inconsistent with a permitted external professional registry. Which analytical technique directly tests cross-source consistency?
options: Retrospective model metrics without validating submitted information
Only time-series analysis of card spending
Data matching and corroboration of entity attributes
Randomly assigning an enhanced fraud risk score
questions.explanation: The guide describes data matching as cross-checking records for inconsistencies and validating source information.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data mining and matching
questions.sourceSection: Data mining and matching

questions.stem: A fraud team detects rapidly accumulating unauthorized transfer attempts. The available case evidence supports material risk and the next payments remain pending. Which analytical operating model has the most immediate mitigation value?
options: A rule that ignores earlier attempts once a payment succeeds
Elimination of all real-time event feeds
Timely risk scoring connected to proportionate alert and transaction intervention
A report issued only after monthly accounting close
questions.explanation: The guide links recognition of fraud behavior to timely intervention; analytics should support action while loss may still be avoided. Domain 2, p. 14.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags (Case example: A quick intervention) · page 14
questions.sourceSection: Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags (Case example: A quick intervention)

questions.stem: An online payment provider can assess transaction amounts and payment outcomes, but it also possesses a sequence of checkout interactions and device signals. Why can the additional behavioral information improve fraud detection?
options: It removes the need to assess the reliability of external data
It guarantees that every detected anomaly is fraud
It can capture interaction patterns missing from payment amount and success status alone
It makes all historical transaction labels irrelevant
questions.explanation: Behavioral patterns and transaction histories can jointly reveal suspicious activity that single financial attributes fail to distinguish. Domain 2, p. 17.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions (Case example: Checkout.com) · page 17
questions.sourceSection: Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions (Case example: Checkout.com)

questions.stem: A treasury team receives a video instruction that convincingly resembles a senior executive and requests an urgent transfer outside established payment routines. What is the key control implication of deepfake capability?
options: High visual fidelity conclusively proves the speaker’s identity
All video messages must be considered verified if they include a recognizable voice
Independent verification and established authorization controls remain necessary despite realistic audio or video
Digital communication removes the need for payment approval
questions.explanation: The guide’s deepfake case demonstrates that apparently authentic media can be manufactured to support social engineering. Domain 2, p. 19.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Use of artificial intelligence to defraud (Case example: Deepfake) · page 19
questions.sourceSection: Use of artificial intelligence to defraud (Case example: Deepfake)

questions.stem: A data science group changes detection thresholds without an audit trail, approval or periodic performance review. Which THREE controls address these governance weaknesses?
options: Retain an auditable history of rule thresholds, validation outcomes and rationale.
Replace formal governance with informal expert judgment
Prohibit model upgrades indefinitely
Disclose the model scoring formula to every external applicant
Document ownership, controls, validation, changes, performance and review responsibilities
Require documented approval and independent challenge for material model changes.
questions.explanation: Fraud model governance requires documented accountabilities, review, testing, performance tracking and controlled changes.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud compliance model governance
questions.sourceSection: Fraud compliance model governance

questions.stem: A loan officer is sent highly convincing AI-generated identity images and requests that exploit trust in visual appearance. Which TWO practices best mitigate synthetic impersonation?
options: Escalate deviations from expected transaction behavior rather than treating polished audio/video as sufficient proof.
Disable all fraud rules when the caller resembles an existing executive
Rely on perceived voice familiarity as primary approval evidence
Accept the request if a familiar photo appears in the message
Verify sensitive instructions via independent trusted channels plus layered identity signals
questions.explanation: Deepfakes can mimic identities; the guide highlights multi-layered verification, behavioral signals and tailored controls rather than trust in apparent identity.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Use of artificial intelligence to defraud
questions.sourceSection: Use of artificial intelligence to defraud

questions.stem: A platform explores a neural model designed to learn nonlinear relationships from large fraud-related datasets. Which modeling family most directly fits this approach?
options: One simple fixed transaction amount rule
A noncomputational fraud-response checklist
Deep learning with multi-layer neural representations
Only an interviewer’s qualitative judgment
questions.explanation: Deep learning uses layered neural-network models to discover complex relationships in data.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Deep learning
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Deep learning

questions.stem: A bank calculates the distribution of transaction amounts and typical frequency for the last year to establish customer norms. Which method best matches the described activity?
options: An exclusive real-time fund-recovery procedure
Purely causal experimentation establishing fraud guilt
Descriptive analytics summarizing what has already happened
A confirmation of future fraud without probability or uncertainty
questions.explanation: Descriptive analytics uses historical data to understand behavior and establish baselines against which outliers can be assessed.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Descriptive analytics for fraud detection
questions.sourceSection: Descriptive analytics for fraud detection

questions.stem: An issuer deploys stronger verification but experiences a surge in abandoned legitimate purchases. Which TWO changes create a more proportionate response?
options: Abandon fraud prevention as long as customer complaints exist
Review thresholds and verification design, communicate clearly, and measure false-positive impact
Keep all friction unchanged regardless of legitimate impact
Apply risk-based step-up verification rather than imposing the highest friction on all events.
Use the strictest possible checks for every activity without risk differentiation
questions.explanation: The guide stresses tuning controls for customer experience, transparent communication and measurable fraud mitigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience
questions.sourceSection: Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience

questions.stem: Customers report calls impersonating bank staff after visiting a fake support page. Within minutes, the same accounts show profile changes through mobile banking and high-value transfers through a separate payment channel. Individual channel teams see only their local records. Which TWO analytics steps provide the strongest basis for assessing a coordinated channel-switching pattern?
options: Correlate activity across telephone, web, mobile and payment events using shared identity and session indicators.
Rely on total fraud loss by month without connecting the activity sequence to a customer.
Evaluate the sequence and timing of events relative to each customer’s established normal behavior.
Treat each channel as an independent event so each team can complete its standard closure process.
Infer confirmed fraud solely from a shared IP address observed in several customer sessions.
questions.explanation: Cross-channel analysis links events and detects deviations from expected customer behavior; no single indicator necessarily proves fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Switching channels for fraud
questions.sourceSection: Switching channels for fraud

questions.stem: Analysts can access payment logs but not customer contact-history changes or help-desk interactions during suspected takeover. Which TWO steps create better analytic coverage?
options: Combine relevant transaction, customer, access, channel and interaction data with appropriate controls
Use transaction amount as the only permanent feature
Remove all customer history to reduce data volume
Preserve the sequence linking login attempts, customer profile edits and eventual payment requests.
Treat absent device information as evidence of no compromise
questions.explanation: The guide supports bringing together multiple internal customer, access, account and payment sources for a holistic risk picture.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Internal sources of data for analytics
questions.sourceSection: Internal sources of data for analytics

questions.stem: Claims records contain duplicate rows, blanks in key fields and contradictory formats across systems. Which TWO actions should precede model training?
options: Train the model and allow it to infer the intended business meaning of every error
Document and verify remediation logic so fixes do not invent unsupported transaction facts.
Discard the full dataset without investigating quality
Treat all duplicate records as independent fraudulent attempts
Clean and standardize the data using justified handling of missing values and duplicates
questions.explanation: The guide describes correcting duplicates, missing fields and format inconsistencies before analysis to prevent misleading patterns.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data transformation and loading
questions.sourceSection: Data transformation and loading

questions.stem: A training dataset mixes huge-valued numeric fields and text-coded payment-type categories. Which preparation pair is conceptually correct?
options: Delete all text categories and use no numerical scaling
Normalize numeric ranges; encode categorical values into numerical representations
Apply the same arbitrary value to every numeric and categorical feature
Encode transaction amounts as categories; normalize names alphabetically
questions.explanation: Normalization rescales numerical features; encoding converts categorical values into forms usable by algorithms.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data transformation and loading
questions.sourceSection: Data transformation and loading

questions.stem: An insurer collects many claim attributes but has insufficient confirmed labels for new abuse patterns. Which method is most useful for discovering unexpected groups or anomalies?
options: Supervised classification treating all unreviewed records as confirmed fraud
Only a fixed whitelist of historic known criminals
A control that assumes each novel transaction must be legitimate
Unsupervised learning to explore structure without required outcome labels
questions.explanation: Unsupervised methods can surface clusters and anomalies when trustworthy labels are unavailable or the pattern is emerging.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection
questions.sourceSection: Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection

questions.stem: A card-fraud analytics team validates a model against confirmed outcomes for one month. It flags 120 transactions, of which 48 are ultimately confirmed fraudulent. An additional 12 confirmed fraudulent transactions are not flagged. Senior management wants to compare the model's precision and recall before changing the decision threshold. Which measurement is most accurate?
options: Precision 40% and recall 40%.
Precision 80% and recall 80%.
Precision 40% and recall 80%.
Precision 80% and recall 40%.
questions.explanation: Precision = 48 / 120 = 40%; recall = 48 / (48 + 12) = 80%. The guide emphasizes evaluation metrics suitable for rare fraud events.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: An account changes device, adds several beneficiaries and sends unusual rapid payments. The customer recently replaced a phone. Which TWO interpretations best follow behavioral analytics principles?
options: A verified device replacement means later unusual transfers should never be examined
Rapid beneficiary additions and novel transfers can increase concern when combined with a device change
Device novelty by itself conclusively establishes account takeover
A new device may have a legitimate explanation and requires contextual assessment
All successful authentications rule out manipulation or compromise
questions.explanation: The combination and chronology of device and payment deviations matters, while a device change alone may be innocent. Domain 2, pp. 12–13.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags · page 13
questions.sourceSection: Fraudulent behavioral patterns and red flags

questions.stem: A card transaction is blocked as fraud, but investigation confirms it was an authorized customer purchase. Which classification is correct for the model outcome?
options: False negative
True positive
True negative
False positive
questions.explanation: A false positive is a legitimate event wrongly classified as fraudulent, contributing to customer friction.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: An account appears to transact from a familiar location, but the device fingerprint and browser environment change sharply immediately before an unusual transfer. What is the strongest reason to consider technology-platform data?
options: A device mismatch is always conclusive evidence of a criminal
Device and session attributes can add context not present in transaction amount or location alone
Location data alone makes device information redundant in all circumstances
Device information should replace every other fraud signal
questions.explanation: Technology platform data provides complementary device and access context for fraud assessment. Domain 2, pp. 32–33.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Leveraging data from technology platforms for fraud detection · page 32
questions.sourceSection: Leveraging data from technology platforms for fraud detection

questions.stem: A fraud classifier has excellent fitting metrics yet materially worse results during independent validation. Which TWO actions address this performance problem?
options: A guaranteed increase in recall without trade-offs
A proof that all historical fraud labels are accurate
Measure performance on separate unseen validation/test data and monitor drift after deployment.
The absence of any need for model retesting
Overfitting and inadequate generalization to new data
questions.explanation: Discrepancy between training and unseen-data performance signals poor generalization; validation/tuning should address it.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Training and tuning
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Training and tuning

questions.stem: A payments institution has reliable confirmed-fraud labels for historical account-takeover events but only weak signals for a new type of fraud that has not yet been formally classified. It wants to build a model portfolio rather than depend on one technique. Which TWO proposals are most appropriate?
options: Use unsupervised anomaly or cluster approaches to explore previously unrecognized patterns in unlabeled activity.
Train a supervised model against the quality-controlled historical labeled account-takeover transactions.
Train the supervised model on all unlabeled suspicious events as though they were confirmed fraudulent transactions.
Treat unusual cluster membership as conclusive proof that the customer committed fraud.
Discard the historical fraud labels because supervised and unsupervised learning cannot coexist.
questions.explanation: Supervised learning benefits from reliable historical labels; unsupervised learning can reveal structures and anomalies in unlabeled data, subject to validation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection
questions.sourceSection: Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection

questions.stem: An issuer’s low threshold catches many suspicious transactions yet overwhelms analysts with false positives. Which approach best balances competing results?
options: Raise thresholds to infinity, eliminating alerts
Remove all controls until complaints stop
Tune using detection quality, loss outcomes and customer-friction measurements
Optimize only the volume of alerts produced
questions.explanation: The guide calls for monitoring hit rates, false positives, risk appetite and customer experience when adjusting fraud rules.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection rules review
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection rules review

questions.topic: Training data leakage and point-in-time features
questions.stem: A fraud modeller creates a training variable called 'claim decision reached' that is recorded weeks after the original transaction. The feature produces a dramatic improvement in historical model performance, but it cannot be known when a live payment is authorized. The team wants the most defensible model design for real-time detection. Which is BEST?
options: Exclude post-transaction outcomes from decision-time features and validate using information available when the prediction would actually be made.
Move the transaction data into a single database so the decision-time constraint no longer matters.
Replace all transaction-time features with the final claim outcome to remove uncertainty from training labels.
Keep the variable because retrospective predictive power is evidence that it can support future live decisions.
questions.explanation: Preparing and selecting usable data for training must reflect information available for the intended live decision; retrospective outcome data should support labels, not unavailable live predictors.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Training and tuning
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Training and tuning

questions.stem: A customer’s salary receipts increase after verified employment changes. Which TWO practices would help the model avoid persistent false-positive alerts while preserving detection?
options: Permanently anchor the baseline to account-opening volumes
Assume any salary increase necessarily indicates first-party fraud
Corroborate the new salary or activity rather than automatically treating all deviations as fraud
Suppress every future alert once one legitimate change is verified
Update expected customer behavior when legitimate life circumstances materially change
questions.explanation: Expected activity should evolve with verified customer circumstances and still be evaluated against other suspicious indicators. Domain 2, pp. 16–17.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions · page 16
questions.sourceSection: Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions

questions.stem: A fraud system’s precision varies sharply between groups, and validation reveals nonrepresentative examples. Which TWO practices are appropriate remediation?
options: Compare performance and error rates across affected groups and document corrective actions.
Evaluate representation, consider augmentation/fairness constraints, and audit outcomes continuously
Use protected customer characteristics as conclusive evidence of fraud
Remove all model governance checks to increase speed
Ignore disparities because overall accuracy is high
questions.explanation: The guide recommends evaluating imbalanced data, representative examples, fairness-aware methods and continuous monitoring.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms
questions.sourceSection: Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms

questions.stem: An assurance team stages mock fraudulent behaviors to test if technical and human safeguards detect them. What is the primary purpose of these exercises?
options: To label every targeted employee a fraudster
To certify fraud has been eradicated permanently
To replace any later investigation into real losses
To simulate attacks and discover exploitable weaknesses before criminals do
questions.explanation: The guide describes fraud penetration testing as controlled attack simulation that reveals control, technical and training gaps.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud penetration testing
questions.sourceSection: Fraud penetration testing

questions.stem: Two acquired banks encode debit and credit signs differently. A combined fraud dataset is loaded without converting the sign conventions. Which ETL step was inadequately performed?
options: Employee interview preparation
Retrospective customer reimbursement
Transformation and consistent mapping before loading
Case narrative disposition
questions.explanation: ETL requires harmonizing source fields and meanings before analysis; inconsistent signs can invalidate calculations and patterns. Domain 2, p. 41.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data transformation and loading · page 41
questions.sourceSection: Data transformation and loading

questions.stem: A business shows a transaction spike just after an anticipated seasonal launch, producing an automated anomaly alert. How should the analyst interpret the alert?
options: As irrelevant because any unusual event is always benign
As conclusive evidence of a committed crime
As grounds to erase the customer’s legitimate history
As a signal requiring contextual validation and risk-based review
questions.explanation: Anomalies flag unusual behavior; human review and context establish whether the activity indicates fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Identifying patterns and anomalies in data
questions.sourceSection: Identifying patterns and anomalies in data

questions.stem: An insurance fraud analyst builds a network graph across claims, claimants, vehicles, garages and contact numbers. A suspiciously dense cluster shares a repair shop and two contact numbers, but several claims appear individually plausible. What is the BEST interpretation of this finding?
options: The graph is nonprobative unless every claimant is connected directly by an identical bank account number.
The shared relationships justify focused investigation and corroboration with independent claim evidence, but are not proof of fraud alone.
Every claim linked to the repair shop should be automatically denied because graph density directly measures criminal intent.
A cluster is less informative than isolated claim values and should be omitted from the investigative workflow.
questions.explanation: The guide explains that link and social-network analysis exposes hidden relationships and anomalies that help target, not replace, investigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Social network analysis and fraud graphs
questions.sourceSection: Social network analysis and fraud graphs

questions.stem: A fraud graph links every customer with the surname Rahman into one suspected ring. The analyst observes no matching addresses, accounts, devices or transaction connections. What is the main analytical defect?
options: Entity matching should never consider names
A weak common attribute has been treated as sufficient evidence of entity linkage
The graph contains too many confirmed criminal convictions
All shared surnames necessarily indicate shared account ownership
questions.explanation: Entity matching must distinguish weak similarities from meaningful corroborated connections to avoid false positives. Domain 2, pp. 42–43.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data mining and matching (Case example: Acme Bank) · page 43
questions.sourceSection: Data mining and matching (Case example: Acme Bank)

questions.stem: An analyst receives unstructured call transcripts and structured transfer data after reports of a new impersonation scam. Which initial workflow best fits the guide?
options: Use only a preassigned risk score without assessing underlying events
Reject all unstructured observations as inherently unusable
File a final confirmed-fraud result before corroborating source data
Collect and inspect structured and unstructured information, identify red flags, then refine risk hypotheses
questions.explanation: The guide describes collecting multiple raw data forms, examining them and identifying fraud indicators before reaching informed conclusions.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Using raw data and the initial risk assessment
questions.sourceSection: Using raw data and the initial risk assessment

questions.stem: An institution wants to identify patterns retrospectively from yesterday’s transactions while separately blocking risky transfers live. Which distinction is technically correct?
options: Batch analysis always blocks faster than real-time authorization
The two techniques are identical except for marketing language
Real-time analysis cannot use external data or fraud rules
Batch analysis reviews transactions in groups after they occur; real-time systems can act during authorization
questions.explanation: The study guide distinguishes batch pattern analysis over groups from live detection/authorization decisions.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Transaction monitoring for fraud
questions.sourceSection: Transaction monitoring for fraud

questions.stem: After ingesting payment data, the analytics team notices that certain transactions appear twice because both an authorizing system and a settlement system exported the same event. What preparation step should occur before trend calculations?
options: Replace distinct events with arbitrary averages
Identify and reconcile duplicate representations using reliable event identifiers
Count both records as two independent fraud attempts
Discard all completed payment information
questions.explanation: Data preparation should ensure consistent event definitions and accurate counts; duplicate source records can distort patterns and totals. Domain 2, pp. 39–45.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data preparation (Case example: QuickBank) · page 45
questions.sourceSection: Data preparation (Case example: QuickBank)

questions.stem: A fraudster fails online authentication and immediately calls the help desk claiming device loss, seeking a manual reset. Which TWO enhancements best expose channel-switching attacks?
options: Link cross-channel customer journeys and suspicious behavior across touchpoints
Correlate failed authentication, device intelligence and help-desk verification outcomes.
Analyze only transactions that ultimately settle
Monitor each channel separately to avoid combining unrelated events
Ignore failed access attempts once an alternate channel succeeds
questions.explanation: The guide covers fraudsters moving between digital and human-assisted channels and the value of joining touchpoint data.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Switching channels for fraud
questions.sourceSection: Switching channels for fraud

questions.stem: Fraudsters increasingly generate realistic impersonation messages. Which TWO control adaptations follow from that emerging fraud capability?
options: Retain independent confirmation routes for sensitive instructions
Reassess how apparently credible audio or text is authenticated
Classify every automated message as confirmed fraud without other evidence
Accept urgent video requests without mandate checks when a senior voice is recognized
Treat messages without spelling errors as verified
questions.explanation: AI-generated impersonation can be convincing; independent verification and layered authorization help manage the risk without presuming every new technology instance is fraudulent. Domain 2, pp. 18–19.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Use of artificial intelligence to defraud · page 18
questions.sourceSection: Use of artificial intelligence to defraud

questions.stem: A fraud manager uses a visualization showing historical loss by merchant category. The manager concludes that the chart by itself predicts which specific transaction tomorrow will be fraudulent. What is the conceptual error?
options: Descriptive analysis can never reveal fraud trends
Historical data cannot be visualized
Historical description is being mistaken for transaction-level prediction
Any fraud chart automatically creates a supervised classifier
questions.explanation: Descriptive analytics summarizes what has occurred; predicting future individual fraud generally requires additional modeling and validation. Domain 2, p. 55.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Descriptive analytics for fraud detection · page 55
questions.sourceSection: Descriptive analytics for fraud detection

questions.stem: An independent review identifies ten genuine scams the model marked as legitimate payments. How should these cases be recorded in a fraud confusion matrix?
options: True negatives
True positives
False positives
False negatives
questions.explanation: A false negative is a genuinely fraudulent event the model classifies as nonfraudulent, harming recall.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: An anti-fraud training set contains relatively few true fraud observations compared with normal transactions. Which TWO evaluation choices are warranted?
options: Consider class balance and precision/recall rather than relying on accuracy alone
Remove the fraud class from training altogether
Assume the data volume guarantees unbiased learning
Inspect false negatives and true positives rather than assuming majority-class accuracy is enough.
Use accuracy alone because majority-class dominance makes it reliable
questions.explanation: With imbalanced fraud data, high raw accuracy may mask missed fraud; class-aware evaluation and relevant balancing can help.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Model evaluation
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Model evaluation

questions.stem: A bank monitors branch, telephone, online and mobile activity. Which TWO design choices address the differences and connections between origination channels?
options: Include telephone or branch touchpoint information where it helps expose linked events
Assume a fraudster cannot move from telephone contact to a mobile payment
Treat a branch interaction as irrelevant whenever a transaction settles digitally
Require identical indicators across all channels regardless of how fraud originates
Use signals appropriate for mobile-device and session activity
questions.explanation: Fraud channels differ but interact; channel-specific evidence and integrated monitoring improve detection. Domain 2, pp. 21–24.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud origination channels · page 21
questions.sourceSection: Fraud origination channels

questions.stem: A group of merchant accounts is indirectly connected through beneficiary identifiers and devices. Which analytical approach best reveals the relationship structure?
options: A customer-specific transaction limit with no linkage analysis
Social network or graph analysis representing entities as nodes and relationships as links
A single average payment value
A quarterly dashboard of employee absences
questions.explanation: Social network analysis identifies hidden relationships across connected actors, accounts, devices and events.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Social network analysis and fraud graphs
questions.sourceSection: Social network analysis and fraud graphs

questions.stem: A group of seemingly unrelated insurance claims shares a small set of phone numbers, repair shops and receiving accounts. Individual claim amounts are not anomalous. Which approach is most suited to assessing the potentially connected pattern?
options: Graph or social-network analysis of shared entities and relationships
Concluding independence because claimants have different names
Deleting relationship attributes before modeling
Amount-based thresholding of each claim in complete isolation
questions.explanation: Social network analysis can reveal hidden relationships among parties, devices and resources not visible from individual amounts. Domain 2, pp. 56–57.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Social network analysis and fraud graphs · page 56
questions.sourceSection: Social network analysis and fraud graphs

questions.stem: A criminal changes credentials through a help desk, enters mobile banking and transfers funds. Which TWO analytics linkages are critical for recognizing this attack?
options: Connect downstream beneficiary and transfer activity to the same customer timeline
Treat each channel as an unrelated dataset without shared event identifiers
Exclude telephone records because the transfer was made through an app
Discard password-reset logs immediately after the call ends
Correlate help-desk credential-reset events with subsequent digital access
questions.explanation: Channel-switching fraud is detectable through linked event sequences across phone, login and payment activity. Domain 2, pp. 23–24.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Switching channels for fraud · page 23
questions.sourceSection: Switching channels for fraud

questions.stem: A network graph shows one phone number linked to dozens of suspicious accounts. The analyst wants to label the number’s owner as the ringleader immediately. Which statement better reflects sound graph interpretation?
options: Graph evidence is irrelevant unless every transaction exceeds a fixed threshold
A central node is an investigative lead; ownership, intent and connection meaning still require corroboration
Every central network node must belong to a criminal
Higher network degree proves the legal offense of fraud
questions.explanation: Graphs highlight connections and important nodes but do not independently establish identity or culpability. Domain 2, pp. 56–57.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Social network analysis and fraud graphs (Case example: SafeDrive Insurance) · page 57
questions.sourceSection: Social network analysis and fraud graphs (Case example: SafeDrive Insurance)

questions.stem: A fintech experiences origination scams involving inconsistencies between identity photos and submitted records. Which paired technique addresses the initiation point?
options: Removal of authentication controls to shorten onboarding
Robust identity proofing with document/data validation and targeted edit checks
Mandatory termination of every new applicant
Only monitoring customer transactions years after onboarding
questions.explanation: The guide treats identity proofing and data validation/edit checks as key controls against onboarding and application fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Using identity proofing as a key fraud control
questions.sourceSection: Using identity proofing as a key fraud control

questions.stem: A predictive fraud model ranks transactions by estimated fraud risk. Operations asks whether the rank should always mean an automatic decline. What is the most defensible distinction?
options: A model cannot support manual review or step-up authentication
A risk score is proof of fraud in every transaction above the median
Risk scores never need recalibration
Risk prediction should support proportionate decisions that reflect thresholds and business impact
questions.explanation: Predictive analytics estimates risk; operational decisions should account for loss prevention, uncertainty, and customer experience. Domain 2, p. 59.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Predictive analytics in anti-fraud efforts · page 59
questions.sourceSection: Predictive analytics in anti-fraud efforts

questions.topic: Analytics business impact: avoid proxy metrics
questions.stem: A new fraud model doubles the proportion of alerted payments, yet confirmed prevented losses barely change and legitimate customers experience more declines. Which conclusion should the business-impact review reach?
options: Alert growth necessarily means the model detects twice as much fraud
A higher alert rate alone is not evidence of improved fraud effectiveness
Every declined transaction should be counted as prevented criminal loss
The model has eliminated false negatives
questions.explanation: Business impact evaluation goes beyond number of alerts to detection quality, losses, operational efficiency and customer effects. Domain 2, p. 60.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Business impact of anti-fraud analytics · page 60
questions.sourceSection: Business impact of anti-fraud analytics

questions.stem: A fraud model performs well at launch but misses a newly emerging attack using unfamiliar transaction paths. The input data feed is unchanged and technically healthy. What type of issue best explains deteriorating detection?
options: Evolving fraud behavior that changes the relationship between inputs and fraud outcomes
A guaranteed improvement in model accuracy
The complete elimination of underlying fraud risk
An inability of any analytics system to process numeric data
questions.explanation: Fraud strategies change, so model performance can degrade without obvious technology failure; ongoing monitoring and tuning matter. Domain 2, pp. 61 and 96.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Challenges of using data analytics · page 61
questions.sourceSection: Challenges of using data analytics

questions.stem: A supervised fraud detector has transaction records but lacks contextual events and verified outcomes. Which TWO internal data enhancements are most relevant?
options: Connect account and event history to transactional features using stable keys
Use confirmed investigation outcomes as supervised training labels where reliable
Substitute marketing engagement counts for fraud outcomes
Treat every uninvestigated transaction as verified legitimate
Exclude previous fraud complaints because only monetary amounts matter
questions.explanation: Relevant internal data include case outcomes and customer or transaction records; reliable matching and labeling support usable training datasets. Domain 2, pp. 29–30.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Internal sources of data for analytics · page 29
questions.sourceSection: Internal sources of data for analytics

questions.stem: A fraud engine forecasts likely fraudulent behavior for new payment requests rather than merely describing past incidents. Which capability is primarily involved?
options: Predictive analytics applying learned patterns to future or incoming events
Descriptive aggregation only
Final reporting of recoveries
Manual archival of original customer documents
questions.explanation: Predictive models estimate potential outcomes for new events based on patterns learned from historical data.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Predictive analytics in anti-fraud efforts
questions.sourceSection: Predictive analytics in anti-fraud efforts

questions.stem: A payment firm is comparing a broad sensitive detector with a narrower detector whose alerts are more frequently correct. Which TWO statements about fraud-model precision and recall are accurate?
options: Precision measures true fraud among flagged cases; recall measures actual fraud caught among all actual fraud
Recall is the proportion of legitimate customers passed without review
A model can capture a high share of real fraud yet have poor precision if many flagged events are legitimate.
Both are identical measures of total case volume
Precision measures captured actual fraud; recall measures true alerts among all flagged
questions.explanation: Precision = TP/(TP+FP); recall = TP/(TP+FN). They capture different trade-offs in fraud models.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: A new payment product has too few reliably confirmed fraud labels to train a supervised model, yet transaction features can be analyzed for unusual clusters. Which approach is particularly relevant for initial discovery?
options: Unsupervised grouping or anomaly detection
Assuming that no fraud can be detected without convictions
Supervised training with fabricated confirmed-fraud labels
A zero-feature model that makes no comparisons
questions.explanation: Unsupervised methods can detect structure and anomalies without requiring a labeled outcome for every observation. Domain 2, p. 65.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection · page 65
questions.sourceSection: Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection

questions.stem: A payment classifier is trained from confirmed fraud and legitimate examples. Over time, human analysts change their disposition standards and stop feeding outcomes back to the training dataset. Which risk increases?
options: Automatic increase in detection recall
Label drift and poor alignment between model training and current fraud definitions
Guaranteed removal of mislabeled cases
Elimination of training-data dependency
questions.explanation: Supervised detection relies on useful and consistent outcome labels. Changes in annotation and missing feedback can undermine learning. Domain 2, pp. 65–66.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection · page 65
questions.sourceSection: Supervised versus unsupervised learning for fraud detection

questions.topic: Model types: interpreting a decision tree
questions.stem: A fraud manager asks why a simple decision-tree model flagged an account after a new device, rapid beneficiary addition and elevated payment value. Which characteristic is a practical advantage of this model type?
options: It requires no quality checks on the data used
Its output is necessarily free of bias
Its sequence of feature-based decisions can often be inspected
It guarantees zero false positives on new customers
questions.explanation: Basic machine-learning algorithms have differing transparency and performance characteristics; tree-based decisions can often be inspected. Domain 2, p. 68.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Basics of machine learning algorithms · page 68
questions.sourceSection: Basics of machine learning algorithms

questions.stem: A bank compares typing cadence and pointer movement against a customer’s established interaction patterns during an authenticated session. What is this control intended to contribute?
options: Replacement of all transaction and customer risk assessment
Behavior-based authentication or anomaly evidence beyond possession of login credentials
A guarantee that every keyboard pattern is unique in all conditions
Proof that a suspicious session was initiated by an employee
questions.explanation: Behavioral biometrics use interaction patterns to help identify unusual or potentially coerced/compromised behavior alongside other evidence. Domain 2, pp. 69–70.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Biometric analytical tools · page 69
questions.sourceSection: Biometric analytical tools

questions.stem: In evaluating an APP scam, the bank observes that the genuine customer authenticated successfully but interacted with the screen in a pattern inconsistent with previous sessions. What is the important analytical distinction illustrated by the guide’s National Australia Bank example?
options: Behavioral measures can identify the recipient’s criminal intent by themselves
Authentication conclusively rules out APP fraud
A known device must be ignored in every fraud review
An authorized payment may still show behavioral signs of manipulation
questions.explanation: Behavioral biometrics can provide additional evidence of manipulation even when credentials and payment authorization appear genuine. Domain 2, p. 70.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Biometric analytical tools (Case example: National Australia Bank) · page 70
questions.sourceSection: Biometric analytical tools (Case example: National Australia Bank)

questions.stem: Authentication and transfer logs come from systems recording timestamps in different timezones. Which TWO preparation actions reduce errors in sequence-based fraud detection?
options: Assume UTC and local timestamps are interchangeable
Order events alphabetically when chronology is ambiguous
Ignore timing when evaluating login-to-payment velocity
Convert timestamps into a consistent reference before joining event sequences
Preserve the original timezone and source provenance for auditability
questions.explanation: Reliable temporal analysis requires normalization of timestamps and preservation of source meaning and provenance. Domain 2, pp. 30 and 39–41.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Leveraging internal sources for data · page 30
questions.sourceSection: Leveraging internal sources for data

questions.stem: A team trains a fraud classifier on transactions but discovers halfway through development that business stakeholders disagree about whether the system should block payments or prioritize cases for review. Which upstream failure most threatens implementation?
options: The model’s decision purpose, intervention workflow and performance objectives were not agreed
A fraud detector cannot be applied to payment data
The presence of stakeholders always prevents implementation
Model training is impossible unless all transactions are fraudulent
questions.explanation: Model design begins with the decision it supports and target outcomes; misaligned operational objectives weaken technical success. Domain 2, p. 75.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model · page 75
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model

questions.stem: A model flags 240 payments. Subsequent investigation confirms 84 of those alerts as fraud. Another 36 actual fraud events were not flagged. If the fraud team is evaluating how reliable the positive alerts were, which metric and value apply?
options: Precision of 35%
Recall of 35%
Precision of 70%
Recall of 84%
questions.explanation: Precision = true positives / all predicted positives = 84/240 = 35%. Recall instead measures the proportion of all actual fraud detected (84/120 = 70%). Domain 2, pp. 76–77.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics · page 76
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: In a labeled evaluation sample, 90 fraudulent transactions were found. A detection rule correctly identified 72 but missed 18; it also flagged 108 legitimate transactions. Which estimate describes the rule’s ability to find actual fraud?
options: Precision of 80%
Recall of 80%
Recall of 40%
Accuracy of 80%
questions.explanation: Recall = true positives/(true positives + false negatives) = 72/(72+18) = 80%; precision is 72/(72+108) = 40%. Domain 2, pp. 76–77.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics · page 76
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: An e-commerce transaction looks unusual in amount but its legitimacy is unclear. Which TWO additional evidence types would most directly enrich the fraud assessment?
options: Classify every new device as fraudulent even with verified replacement records
Bring customer transaction history into the evaluation
Treat amount alone as conclusive proof of malicious intent
Use session and device information to contextualize the unusual order
Ignore credible external and technological signals because they are non-financial
questions.explanation: Integrating complementary financial and technical data sources supports stronger judgment than a single transaction attribute. Domain 2, pp. 32–35.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Leveraging data from technology platforms for fraud detection (Case example: Using multiple data sources) · page 33
questions.sourceSection: Leveraging data from technology platforms for fraud detection (Case example: Using multiple data sources)

questions.stem: A bank turns recent account-change events and transaction timing into a new per-customer risk indicator. Which technique has created the new analytic variables?
options: Feature engineering through derivation of informative attributes
Deleting historical records after loading
Final customer notification and restitution
Unsupervised labeling by human intuition only
questions.explanation: Feature engineering derives predictive variables from source fields, such as average spend, velocity and timing measures.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data transformation and loading
questions.sourceSection: Data transformation and loading

questions.stem: A vendor offers a broad external identity dataset, including sensitive fields not obviously related to fraud detection. Which TWO checks should precede integration?
options: Ignore the data provenance if the vendor has a reputable brand
Assume vendor access permission overrides the bank’s governance duties
Assess which fields are relevant, reliable and necessary for the fraud purpose
Ingest all sensitive fields by default because more features always improve performance
Confirm the supplier’s permission and restrictions for use of external data
questions.explanation: External enrichment requires data relevance, quality and authorized use; vendor availability alone does not settle governance obligations. Domain 2, p. 35.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · External sources of data for analytics · page 35
questions.sourceSection: External sources of data for analytics

questions.stem: A fraud model’s “legitimate” class includes every payment that has not received a completed fraud investigation. Which TWO concerns arise?
options: Uninvestigated outcomes should not automatically be treated as confirmed non-fraud
Transactions without customer complaints are always verified legitimate
Missing labels should be replaced with a fraud conviction assumption
Unknown or delayed fraud status can distort model training and validation
A very large dataset makes incorrect labels statistically harmless
questions.explanation: Labels have to represent credible outcomes; missing and delayed fraud decisions can make apparent non-fraud examples unreliable. Domain 2, pp. 36–37.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud datasets · page 36
questions.sourceSection: Fraud datasets

questions.stem: Model X detects 95% of confirmed fraud but issues 5,000 alerts per day, beyond the team’s review capacity. Model Y detects 90% but issues 700 alerts. Which evaluation is most defensible before selecting a production threshold?
options: Evaluate only the overall accuracy metric
Choose Model X automatically because recall is higher
Choose Model Y automatically because volume is lower
Compare missed-fraud cost, alert precision, operational capacity and customer impact
questions.explanation: Model selection requires balancing fraud recall, precision, false positives and real operational or customer consequences rather than a single headline rate. Domain 2, pp. 76–77 and 97.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics · page 77
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: A model already receives transaction amounts and individual timestamps but misses repeated rapid small-value attempts. Which engineered feature most directly captures the suspicious pattern?
options: The total number of employees at the bank
The color scheme of the account statement
An arbitrary hash of a customer’s first name
Count of transactions within a rolling time window
questions.explanation: Feature engineering transforms raw transactions into informative measures such as short-window frequency or velocity. Domain 2, p. 78.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Feature engineering · page 78
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Feature engineering

questions.stem: An existing model has a stable headline accuracy score, yet investigators discover a novel authorized-payment scam that escaped all current fraud alerts. A proposed model revision catches more of those transactions but creates uncertainty about customer friction in production. The risk committee asks for an evaluation before live interdiction. What is the MOST defensible approach?
options: Replace the old model immediately because identifying emerging fraud is the primary objective, and assess customer friction after deployment.
Validate performance on relevant fraud cases and run below-the-line testing to estimate missed fraud and the effect of revised rules before deployment.
Maintain the existing rule because its aggregate accuracy has remained stable across the full transaction population.
Use only the total number of alerts to decide because a larger alert volume indicates more fraud has been detected.
questions.explanation: The guide recommends selecting metrics appropriate to class imbalance and below-the-line testing to review false negatives without affecting the live operating model.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.topic: Feature engineering: PCA and informative components
questions.stem: A bank has engineered 80 correlated device, channel and transaction variables. Its analytics team proposes principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce the input dimension before modeling. Which interpretation of PCA is most consistent with the CAFS study guide?
options: It identifies components capturing data variation while reducing dimensionality; high variance alone does not prove fraud
It uses confirmed case outcomes to guarantee that every principal component identifies a fraudster
It assigns legal responsibility for suspected fraud to the variables with the largest weights
It removes the need for feature scaling, preprocessing or later model evaluation
questions.explanation: The guide explains PCA as a statistical method to reduce feature dimensions by identifying principal components that retain informative variation. PCA itself does not label transactions as fraudulent. Domain 2, p. 78.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Feature engineering · page 78
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Feature engineering

questions.stem: A fraud product team wants to deploy a deep-learning detector for a small, sparse dataset with unclear outcome labels because it is perceived as more advanced. What is the best governance response?
options: Assume all unlabelled data can be treated as confirmed fraud
Treat architectural complexity as a guarantee of fraud detection accuracy
Exclude model-validation controls whenever deep learning is used
Compare simpler alternatives and assess data sufficiency, explainability and performance
questions.explanation: Deep learning is an available technique, not automatically the best choice; solution fit, usable data, explainability and evaluation remain important. Domain 2, p. 80.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Deep learning · page 80
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Deep learning

questions.stem: The same fraud transactions are repeatedly used to tune thresholds and then reported as an independent final model test. Why is the reported performance potentially unreliable?
options: Evaluation becomes more independent as the same data are reused
The evaluation set has influenced tuning and no longer provides an independent generalization check
Only true-positive counts are affected by dataset selection
The approach guarantees a realistic future fraud distribution
questions.explanation: Training and tuning should be separated from an independent evaluation sample; repeated reuse can overstate generalization. Domain 2, pp. 81–82.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Training and tuning · page 81
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Training and tuning

questions.stem: A suspected fraud ring varies name spellings and account descriptions across records. Which TWO practices improve matching while limiting false associations?
options: Merge all customers sharing a common surname into one fraud case
Normalize names and related identifiers before comparison
Use corroborating attributes to assess whether similar records actually refer to the same party
Treat a high string-matching score as criminal evidence without further analysis
Reject every fuzzy match because only identical strings are useful
questions.explanation: Entity resolution benefits from normalized matching and corroboration; neither exact-only nor unqualified fuzzy matching is reliable. Domain 2, pp. 42–43.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data mining and matching · page 42
questions.sourceSection: Data mining and matching

questions.topic: Model evaluation: overfitting and unseen data
questions.stem: A fraud classifier achieves 99% performance on data used in model development, but only 65% when assessed against new unseen transactions. Its developers propose reporting the former number as production readiness. What inference is best supported by the model evaluation principles in the guide?
options: Evaluating unseen transactions is unnecessary when the training score exceeds 95%
The training result proves the model is more reliable on future transactions
A model with many features cannot overfit its training data
The result suggests poor generalization or overfitting that requires investigation before release
questions.explanation: The guide explains overfitting and emphasizes evaluating performance on unseen test data to measure generalization, rather than relying on training performance. Domain 2, pp. 78 and 82.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Model evaluation · page 82
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Model evaluation

questions.stem: An analytics manager builds a new payment fraud model and independently signs off its training sample, risks, monitoring criteria and go-live approval without challenge. Which governance risk is most apparent?
options: Lack of appropriate independent oversight and documented model review
An inability to generate any fraud alerts
Too much use of representative out-of-time evaluation
An unnecessary emphasis on documentation
questions.explanation: Fraud compliance model governance requires documented oversight and effective challenge of design, deployment and monitoring. Domain 2, p. 86.
