questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud compliance model governance · page 86
questions.sourceSection: Fraud compliance model governance

questions.topic: Data normalization and false velocity spikes
questions.stem: A fraud-detection deployment shows a sudden increase in velocity alerts immediately after ingesting data from two payment processors. A sample reveals that one processor stores timestamps in local time, the other in UTC, and retries sometimes create duplicated transaction identifiers. Which TWO data-preparation actions should occur before interpreting the rise as a new fraud typology?
options: Normalize time fields to a consistent temporal basis, preserving the correct event sequence.
Label all duplicated records as confirmed fraud for model retraining.
Investigate and resolve duplicate records using validated record identifiers and source context.
Raise the velocity threshold for all customer segments without checking the incoming data.
Suppress all velocity alerts until every customer profile has been manually reviewed.
questions.explanation: The guide treats data cleaning, duplicate handling and standardization of formats as necessary inputs to reliable fraud analytics.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data transformation and loading
questions.sourceSection: Data transformation and loading

questions.stem: A payment amount is ordinary for a large company but unprecedented for a small personal account. Which TWO controls on baseline interpretation best support a risk-based assessment?
options: Use the same fixed amount threshold for every retail and corporate account without context
Consider verified customer profile changes that may alter a baseline
Treat all large business payments as suspected fraud
Assume a low-value transfer is harmless in every customer segment
Assess unusual values relative to the relevant customer’s typical activity
questions.explanation: Contextual baselines allow analytics to distinguish meaningful deviations and changing customer circumstances. Domain 2, p. 44.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Using raw data and the initial risk assessment · page 44
questions.sourceSection: Using raw data and the initial risk assessment

questions.stem: A transaction model flags digital-wallet customers disproportionately often even though recent reviewed cases show no comparable increase in confirmed fraud in that segment. An audit finds wallet transactions were underrepresented among legitimate examples in the model's training data. Which TWO improvements are best supported by the guide?
options: Lower every fraud score regardless of segment and replace approval testing with customer satisfaction surveys.
Rebalance or improve the representativeness of the labeled training data and re-evaluate the model.
Remove digital-wallet transactions from all monitoring rules to eliminate the observed disparity immediately.
Compare false positive outcomes across affected segments and incorporate valid customer feedback into model refinement.
Retain the model without review because fraud is comparatively rare and some friction is unavoidable.
questions.explanation: The guide describes unfair model outcomes from skewed data and the need to adjust training data, evaluate algorithms and listen to customer feedback.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms
questions.sourceSection: Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms

questions.stem: The guide’s SoFi case concerns weaknesses in identity-proofing controls. In reviewing a similar onboarding deficiency, which analysis best captures why improving transaction detection alone may be insufficient?
options: Strong transaction models always reconstruct missing identity evidence
Every onboarding record becomes trustworthy once a customer makes one payment
Fraudulent identities may enter at origination, before later transaction models can rely on customer attributes
Identity verification matters only after accounts are closed
questions.explanation: The SoFi case illustrates the importance of effective identity proofing at account origination, alongside later transaction monitoring. Domain 2, pp. 87–88.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Using identity proofing as a key fraud control (Case example: SoFi) · page 88
questions.sourceSection: Using identity proofing as a key fraud control (Case example: SoFi)

questions.stem: A bank wants to buy an advanced fraud analytics platform without defining the business question or operational decision. Which TWO steps should come first?
options: Select data and success metrics aligned to that business purpose
Assume a sophisticated dashboard automatically improves preventive action
Define which fraud decision the analytics output must support
Treat model objectives as irrelevant once a vendor contract is signed
Purchase the most complex model before identifying relevant fraud risks
questions.explanation: Analytics design needs a clear fraud problem and suitable evidence or success criteria before choosing tools and algorithms. Domain 2, p. 50.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Data analysis framework · page 50
questions.sourceSection: Data analysis framework

questions.stem: A merchant abruptly processes 500 transactions in one hour, compared with a prior norm of ten per day, and changes payout details. Which TWO analytical considerations make this potentially unusual?
options: Conclude every high-velocity event is confirmed fraud
Consider the concurrent beneficiary and payout changes as corroborating context
Compare the volume change with the merchant’s own normal activity
Use only global industry average volume regardless of merchant size
Discard historic merchant activity when the sector is large
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection should use relevant behavior baselines and supporting changes rather than simplistic universal comparisons. Domain 2, p. 52.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Identifying patterns and anomalies in data · page 52
questions.sourceSection: Identifying patterns and anomalies in data

questions.topic: Analytics solution selection: fit for purpose
questions.stem: A vendor claims the highest overall classification accuracy in an unrelated retail dataset. The bank’s concern is missing a small number of costly fraud transactions. Which TWO factors should drive the bank’s selection?
options: False-negative costs and practical alert handling capacity
Vendor brand popularity as the sole decision criterion
Evaluation on representative bank data and relevant fraud outcomes
A rule that every new model must replace all current controls
Unverified accuracy without class distribution
questions.explanation: Choosing fraud solutions requires representative evaluation and objectives aligned to fraud loss and operational tradeoffs, not generic vendor accuracy claims. Domain 2, p. 64.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Choosing fraud data analytics solutions · page 64
questions.sourceSection: Choosing fraud data analytics solutions

questions.stem: A validation population has 20 actual fraud cases and 1,980 legitimate payments. A model predicts that every transaction is legitimate and reports 99% accuracy. Which TWO conclusions are correct?
options: No fraud risk remains because 99% of transactions are legitimate
The detector has zero recall for fraud in this population
The model detects 19.8 fraud cases on average
The model has 99% precision for flagged fraud
Overall accuracy alone conceals the failure to detect rare fraud
questions.explanation: Predicting all payments as legitimate classifies 1,980/2,000 correctly but detects none of 20 actual fraud cases; fraud recall = 0%. Domain 2, pp. 76–77.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics · page 77
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Selection and evaluation metrics

questions.stem: An application states that a customer is 19 years old but records a date of birth indicating age 56. The analytics pipeline accepts both values as valid because they are syntactically numeric. Which control is missing?
options: A logical cross-field validation or edit check
A post-closure interview protocol
A regression of historic fraud loss on marketing spending
A promotional propensity score
questions.explanation: Edit checks should assess logical consistency as well as field format, helping prevent incorrect or fabricated inputs contaminating decisions. Domain 2, p. 90.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Using data validation or edit checks · page 90
questions.sourceSection: Using data validation or edit checks

questions.stem: A transaction monitoring rule produces fewer alerts after a threshold increase. Subsequent reviews find more confirmed fraud below the new threshold. Which review activity most directly addresses the risk?
options: Increase the threshold again to eliminate operational work
Delete the misclassified events so precision appears higher
Judge success only from a smaller queue
Evaluate missed fraud and retune thresholds with representative outcomes
questions.explanation: Rule reviews should include false negatives, loss outcomes and impact of thresholds, not only lower alert volumes. Domain 2, p. 91.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection rules review · page 91
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection rules review

questions.stem: Two distinct fraud classifiers capture different attack patterns; a team considers combining their scores. Which TWO considerations matter when assessing the ensemble?
options: Using only training-set accuracy to approve production
Ignoring model errors because they cancel automatically
Assuming that more models always guarantee perfect fraud detection
Whether the combined approach improves performance on representative unseen data
The additional operational complexity and latency of multiple models
questions.explanation: Ensembles may help by combining model strengths, but performance and operational cost must be validated. Domain 2, p. 79.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud detection model: Ensemble methods · page 79
questions.sourceSection: Fraud detection model: Ensemble methods

questions.stem: A fraud control is tested by an authorized team using crafted account-opening and payment patterns to determine whether system safeguards detect or resist them. What distinguishes this exercise from reviewing historical fraud losses?
options: It removes the need to document test methods and findings
It substitutes for all production monitoring
It proves that criminals will never find another exploit
It proactively challenges control behavior under defined simulated attack conditions
questions.explanation: Fraud penetration testing can proactively exercise the detection or protection system against controlled attack behavior and identify weaknesses. Domain 2, p. 92.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Fraud penetration testing · page 92
questions.sourceSection: Fraud penetration testing

questions.stem: A detector flags a large transfer from an account with recent device changes. The user has a documented history of occasional high-value transactions but never from new devices. Which evidence would most strengthen case prioritization?
options: Only the absolute transaction value
Only the number of days since product launch
The account’s historic highest balance without any transaction context
Combination of beneficiary novelty, temporal sequence and authenticated customer context
questions.explanation: Transaction monitoring integrates multiple fraud risk indicators rather than treating one threshold as a complete risk determination. Domain 2, p. 93.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Transaction monitoring for fraud · page 93
questions.sourceSection: Transaction monitoring for fraud

questions.stem: A new fraud model performs well in a laboratory test. When deployed, a key mobile-device input is null for one payment channel. Which operational control should detect this condition early?
options: Only a pre-launch marketing review
Live data-quality monitoring and deployment validation with clear escalation
Assuming that good offline accuracy guarantees production integrity
Discarding all null-bearing events without measuring impact
questions.explanation: Implementing fraud detection requires monitoring actual operational data and controls; a model may fail due to defective production inputs. Domain 2, p. 95.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Implementing fraud detection systems · page 95
questions.sourceSection: Implementing fraud detection systems

questions.stem: A bank's new policy requires every established customer to perform the highest-friction authentication sequence for every mobile transfer, including recurring low-value payments to long-standing beneficiaries. Chargebacks decrease slightly, but abandonment and complaints rise sharply. The fraud analytics lead must propose a redesign within the bank's risk appetite. Which approach BEST balances those competing outcomes?
options: Remove authentication for all low-value payments and measure customer satisfaction without assessing residual fraud exposure.
Preserve blanket authentication because any reduction in fraud loss makes the customer abandonment rate irrelevant.
Apply risk-based, proportionate step-up authentication for transactions with meaningful behavioral or transactional anomalies and test the resulting fraud and friction outcomes.
Use a single transaction amount threshold as the only risk factor because behavioral indicators introduce excessive model complexity.
questions.explanation: The guide promotes strong fraud controls with attention to customer experience, using proportionate authentication and monitoring rather than indiscriminate friction.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience
questions.sourceSection: Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience

questions.stem: Criminals learn that a bank reviews transfers above a fixed amount and begin splitting payments into many lower-value transactions. Which analytical weakness does this expose?
options: Splitting transfers changes their legal authorization status
A static rule always provides full protection once documented
A static single-threshold rule can be evaded without behavioral or velocity features
Low-value payments can never be suspicious
questions.explanation: Fraud techniques adapt to published or inferred detection limits; layered, evolving patterns help mitigate fixed-rule limitations. Domain 2, p. 96.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Challenges and limitations of fraud detection techniques · page 96
questions.sourceSection: Challenges and limitations of fraud detection techniques

questions.stem: A fraud model’s overall accuracy meets its target, yet one legitimate customer segment experiences far more erroneous payment declines than comparable segments. What should governance evaluate next?
options: Only overall accuracy because it conclusively proves fairness
Whether that segment generates the fewest marketing leads
Segment-level error rates and whether the disparity reflects unjustified bias or data limitations
Whether the model’s source code contains the word fairness
questions.explanation: Bias and fairness must be assessed beyond aggregate accuracy by examining differential effects and potential causes across affected groups. Domain 2, pp. 98–99.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms · page 98
questions.sourceSection: Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms

questions.stem: A bank’s fraud system declines many genuine first-time international payments while successfully detecting a small number of scams. Which TWO aspects should the next optimization include?
options: Assumption that every flagged transaction was fraudulent
Fraud loss prevention and residual exposure
Ignoring verified customer outcomes when tuning the model
An instruction to remove all monitoring from international payments
False-positive cost and legitimate customer experience
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes balancing fraud mitigation against customer experience; both protective outcomes and legitimate-user friction matter. Domain 2, p. 97.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience · page 97
questions.sourceSection: Balancing fraud mitigation and customer experience

questions.stem: An institution trains a model using past investigation labels. Historically, one customer segment was reviewed more frequently and therefore has more recorded confirmed cases, despite uncertain underlying fraud prevalence. What bias risk should be considered?
options: Historical labels remove the need for fairness review
More investigations always prove greater underlying criminality
The model cannot learn from labels that originated with humans
Past investigation practices may influence labels and perpetuate unequal future treatment
questions.explanation: Historical detection and labeling practices may introduce bias; fairness review should evaluate how dataset creation and outcomes affect model behavior. Domain 2, pp. 98–99.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms (Case example: LuxCard) · page 99
questions.sourceSection: Bias and fairness in fraud detection models and algorithms (Case example: LuxCard)

questions.stem: A digital bank is launching an end-to-end detector that combines fraud signals, customer verification and operational review. Which implementation objective best matches the guide’s applied fraud-detection examples?
options: Maximize the number of disconnected models regardless of workflow
Join relevant controls and monitoring into a working operational decision process
Exclude feedback from investigations after the system goes live
Treat training accuracy as sufficient evidence of customer protection
questions.explanation: Fraud detection deployment must integrate analytics with real workflows, validation and continuous improvement rather than end at model training. Domain 2, p. 101.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Detection and Analytics · Implementing fraud detection systems (Case example: European digital bank) · page 101
questions.sourceSection: Implementing fraud detection systems (Case example: European digital bank)

description: 100 questions on detection methods, behavioral signals, data interpretation and analytics.

title: Fraud Investigations
name: Fraud Investigations
subtitle: Domain 3 Knowledge Assessment

questions.stem: A procurement employee creates a nonexistent supplier and routes payments for unprovided equipment to a controlled account. Which broad fraud category most directly captures the conduct?
options: Legitimate expense allocation because an employee approves it
Internal asset misappropriation involving diversion of organizational resources
A victim-authorized push payment scam by an unrelated external criminal
Unintentional money muling by a recruitment victim
questions.explanation: Phantom vendors, ghost employees and diverted company assets are examples of internal asset misappropriation schemes.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Asset misappropriation fraud
questions.sourceSection: Asset misappropriation fraud

questions.stem: Two alerts have equal monetary value, but one affects hundreds of customers and involves coordinated account compromise. Which TWO practices support stronger case allocation?
options: Combine risk exposure, financial value, customer impact and linked-incident severity
Reassess the case order when emerging intelligence changes the risk or number of affected customers.
Process all cases at identical speed regardless of risk
Prioritize only the largest nominal payment in every case
Rank exclusively by individual alert age
questions.explanation: The guide combines risk-based, monetary-based and customer-impact-based priorities and adjusts for linked incidents.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Case management strategies for fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Case management strategies for fraud investigations

questions.stem: An institution confirms that a long-standing customer used the account to conduct fraud through deliberately false documents. Loss containment is complete, but the relationship manager requests an immediate closure without formal case notes because the customer has an otherwise profitable history. What is the BEST course?
options: Report only to the customer’s private counsel and omit internal escalation to prevent reputational impact.
Close the account without investigation documentation because the evidence was independently reviewed by the relationship manager.
Follow documented escalation and approval procedures, retain supporting investigation evidence, meet applicable reporting duties and execute any exit consistently with policy.
Retain the relationship by default when profits exceed the direct fraud loss, so long as suspicious activity stops.
questions.explanation: The guide’s customer exit section emphasizes sufficient evidence, final authorization, documentation and compliance with organizational exit and reporting procedures.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer exit after a fraud investigation
questions.sourceSection: Customer exit after a fraud investigation

questions.stem: A fraud team receives a signed customer statement and a copied invoice. A suspected third-party merchant possesses the original invoice and refuses to provide it. Investigators also hold electronic logs that may be overwritten by ordinary retention processes. Which TWO steps are appropriate within the investigator's remit?
options: Remove the merchant’s original invoice without consent because the fraud unit suspects it was altered.
Preserve the institution’s existing logs and documents promptly, recording their origin, access and handling.
Withhold the customer statement from the case file because external evidence is more reliable than victim accounts.
Seek voluntary provision of relevant external evidence and use authorized law-enforcement processes where seizure is necessary.
Modify metadata in the logs to make timestamps consistent before preserving an evidential copy.
questions.explanation: The guide requires credible, relevant and well-preserved evidence; it distinguishes voluntary provision from seizure, which is a law-enforcement power.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Evidence gathering for fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Evidence gathering for fraud investigations

questions.stem: A transaction investigation indicates an employee with privileged system access may be altering beneficiary details and can view ordinary fraud-team case notes. The employee also maintains social relationships with several staff assigned to the initial review. Which TWO safeguards are most appropriate?
options: Allocate investigative responsibility to appropriately independent personnel and escalate through authorized fraud, HR and legal channels.
Restrict access to the investigation on a need-to-know basis and preserve sensitive systems evidence before it can be altered.
Delete unconfirmed witness reports to ensure the initial file contains only facts already substantiated.
Share the allegations with the employee’s entire department to identify potential witnesses quickly.
Ask the suspected employee to conduct a preliminary self-review of the relevant system logs for efficiency.
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes confidentiality, impartiality, safeguarding evidence and appropriate handling of sensitive employee investigations.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Investigating someone inside the organization
questions.sourceSection: Investigating someone inside the organization

questions.stem: An anonymous social media post names a suspected fraudster but provides no independently confirmed connection to the investigated account. Which TWO evidential practices follow the guide?
options: Record as confirmed fact because the material is public
Purchase unlawfully acquired personal records to verify the allegation
Disregard all publicly available information regardless of relevance
Treat as an investigative lead and corroborate through credible independent sources
Record source origin and timing so later reviewers can assess the credibility of the information.
questions.explanation: Public OSINT is potentially helpful but may be inaccurate; it should be corroborated and obtained ethically and lawfully.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Open-source intelligence for investigations
questions.sourceSection: Open-source intelligence for investigations

questions.stem: An investigator seeks to trace an international payment and attempt timely recovery with assistance from foreign correspondent banks. Which step is most appropriate?
options: Send confidential customer records without permissions to every bank in the network
Use applicable network tracing/recall options and coordinate with recipient institutions under required processes
Assume all SWIFT transfers are unilaterally reversible after settlement
Delay investigation until the recipient admits wrongdoing
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes use of payment networks and cooperative relationships for tracing and potential recovery, subject to rules and lawful powers.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Using global payment networks in fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Using global payment networks in fraud investigations

questions.stem: A buyer intentionally keeps delivered merchandise but falsely disputes the legitimate transaction as unauthorized. Which classification is BEST supported?
options: Employee financial-statement misrepresentation
A third-party identity-theft event necessarily involving stolen credentials
Deliberate first-party chargeback fraud
An accidental processor-name misunderstanding
questions.explanation: Knowingly disputing a genuine charge to retain the goods/services and reclaim payment constitutes deliberate chargeback fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Chargeback fraud
questions.sourceSection: Chargeback fraud

questions.stem: An alert flags a high-value new payee with unusual device activity, and payment release is pending review. Which TWO early-stage actions follow the guide?
options: Wait for the transaction to complete before reviewing an available live alert
Close the case solely because the detection system might produce false positives
Immediately declare that the customer committed fraud
Document the alert triage and relevant interim restrictions/assignments in the centralized case process.
Follow the fraud response policy/SLA, triage risk and take appropriate interim preventive action
questions.explanation: The guide begins alert response with applicable procedures and prioritization, then triage and permitted protective action before full investigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud alert response
questions.sourceSection: Fraud alert response

questions.stem: Investigators obtain a printed document and a dynamic web page relevant to a suspected procurement scheme. Which THREE steps most help preserve integrity and admissibility?
options: Record who obtained and handled items, and when each transfer occurred.
Rely only on investigators’ unrecorded recollections of each item
Permit unrestricted access so any employee can help organize the case
Preserve originals, log collection and transfers, secure storage and save dynamic website evidence
Capture screenshots/downloads of websites whose relevant content may change.
Annotate and alter original documents directly to simplify review
questions.explanation: Preserving original integrity and documented chain of custody includes acquisition details, controlled storage, transfer logs and capturing changeable online evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Evidence gathering for fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Evidence gathering for fraud investigations

questions.stem: A bank recovers much of the loss from a supplier-invoice diversion and plans to mark the event resolved. A later review shows a payment-detail change was accepted through a weak callback workflow, and two prior cases involved the same control. The board asks how the review should distinguish case resolution from program improvement. Which approach is BEST?
options: Report full remediation because most funds were recovered, treating follow-up on the callback control as discretionary.
Classify the risk as unavoidable external fraud because the original invoice originated outside the bank.
Retain the same callback workflow but ask investigators to devote more time to identifying individual customers at risk.
Document the incident outcome separately from the control failure, analyze repeated weaknesses and assign measurable corrective actions.
questions.explanation: The guide treats fraud root cause analysis and feedback as means to correct failed controls, beyond the immediate claim or recovery outcome.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud root cause analysis
questions.sourceSection: Fraud root cause analysis

questions.stem: An investigation team wants a planned, ethical and nonconfrontational method for accurate information gathering. Which interview framework most directly aligns with that approach?
options: An unstructured public accusation
The PEACE model
A requirement to reveal all interviewee records to every witness
The Reid technique’s admission-oriented approach
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes PEACE’s ethical/nonconfrontational fact-gathering focus from Reid’s behavioral/admission-oriented approach.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective interviewing techniques
questions.sourceSection: Effective interviewing techniques

questions.stem: A customer whose funds were manipulated is embarrassed and distrustful of the bank’s fraud team. Which TWO techniques best support a vulnerable victim?
options: Begin with broad and empathetic questions, then narrow after allowing the account to be given.
Ask the victim to agree with the investigator’s conclusions at the outset
Tell the customer there is no need to verify the claimed facts
Use a designated empathetic contact, clear questions, sensitivity and time for the victim to explain
Use accusatory technical language to pressure a quick admission
questions.explanation: The guide calls for compassion, advance preparation, simple language and trust-building while obtaining accurate information.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective communication for victims of fraud
questions.sourceSection: Effective communication for victims of fraud

questions.stem: An investigator plans interviews of a whistleblower, independent operational witnesses and colleagues of the accused. Which TWO methods improve interview reliability?
options: Only the suspected perpetrator should be interviewed
Use broad open-ended questioning first, then focus on details and corroborating evidence.
Suspect and close associates first; victim last
Victims or whistleblowers first, neutral parties next, people associated with the suspect later
Choose the order randomly to avoid collecting corroborating evidence
questions.explanation: The guide recommends interviewing victims/whistleblowers, then neutral stakeholders, then those linked to the suspect.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective techniques for interviewing victims, whistleblowers, and witnesses
questions.sourceSection: Effective techniques for interviewing victims, whistleblowers, and witnesses
Fraud investigative mindset
questions.stem: A fraud investigator sees three incoming transfers with similar descriptions and immediately labels the customer a mule. Additional account history shows comparable legitimate transfers over two years, but one recent recipient is unfamiliar. What best demonstrates an investigative mindset?
options: Wait for a formal confession before checking the account
Treat the first pattern as conclusive and avoid the additional history
Test competing hypotheses by examining normal behavior, the new recipient, source records and explanations
Delete the alert because previous transactions were legitimate
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes analytical curiosity, healthy skepticism and a systematic evaluation of anomalies. Similar transaction descriptions are neither proof of fraud nor proof of innocence. A sound investigator tests alternative explanations and corroborates the specific unfamiliar activity before reaching a conclusion.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud investigative mindset

questions.sourceSection: Importance of fraud prevention and detection
questions.stem: A team is classifying controls by when they act. Which TWO statements correctly distinguish fraud prevention from fraud detection?
options: Controls that flag transactions after attempted execution can never be detective
Detection eliminates the need for preventive controls
Preventive controls are designed to reduce the likelihood that fraud can occur
Prevention is relevant only after funds have been stolen
Detective controls identify and react to suspected activity that is under way or has occurred
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes proactive prevention from detection of activity occurring or already completed. Both are essential, and combining them creates a more resilient anti-fraud program.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Importance of fraud prevention and detection

questions.topic: Fraud victim impact beyond direct loss
questions.sourceSection: Impact of fraud on victims
questions.stem: After a romance fraud, a victim reports anxiety, embarrassment and reluctance to contact family, even though the immediate financial loss has been repaid. Which interpretation is most consistent with the guide?
options: The victim’s reluctance to speak establishes complicity
Psychological harm and damaged trust can persist independently of recovered funds
Only criminal proceedings can create emotional distress
Reimbursement eliminates the effects of the incident
questions.explanation: The study guide describes fraud victims experiencing psychological distress, shame, betrayal and social consequences alongside monetary damage. Financial recovery alone does not resolve those effects; investigator communication should remain sensitive to the victim’s circumstances.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Impact of fraud on victims

questions.sourceSection: Fraud program thresholds that trigger a fraud alert
questions.stem: A fraud strategy team is designing an alert rule for digital banking. Which TWO signals are examples of triggers the guide considers appropriate for threshold design?
options: The mere fact that a customer owns a mobile phone
A stable monthly salary paid on its customary date
Unexpected IP/geolocation changes or failed multi-factor authentication
A customer’s positive savings balance alone
Several small-value payments within a short period
questions.explanation: The guide lists frequency/velocity and digital access anomalies, including MFA failures and location changes, as examples of possible fraud alert triggers. An actual threshold must still be tailored to the institution’s risk and customer behavior.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud program thresholds that trigger a fraud alert

questions.stem: A suspected staff member has access to the emails and logs that could corroborate allegations of phantom vendor payments. Which TWO protective practices are appropriate?
options: Restrict sensitive case information to necessary people and maintain an evidence custody trail.
Coordinate with HR/IT and relevant owners to secure evidence and handle employee protections lawfully
Publish the allegations to all staff to solicit opinions
Ask the suspected employee to delete copies of disputed documents
Demand an immediate confession before gathering any records
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes confidentiality, legal compliance, protecting the employee and organization, and HR/IT support for access and evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Investigating someone inside the organization
questions.sourceSection: Investigating someone inside the organization

questions.stem: Several concluded fraud cases expose the same weakness in beneficiary edits and customer verification. Which TWO steps complete the improvement cycle?
options: Close cases and prevent any further discussion of root causes
Limit corrective work to customer reimbursement only
Assign outcome metrics and owners to control changes, then track effectiveness over time.
Share root-cause findings with analytics and risk management, implement targeted controls and measure outcomes
Assume a single corrective memo is enough without a testable action plan
questions.explanation: The feedback loop takes case findings through analytics/investigation/risk management to corrective action and measurable monitoring.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud feedback loop
questions.sourceSection: Fraud feedback loop

questions.topic: First-party customer exit versus victim treatment
questions.stem: A borrower knowingly orchestrates account fraud and the investigation conclusively establishes the customer as perpetrator. Which exit approach best fits the guide?
options: Avoid legal/compliance involvement when the losses are material
Treat the proven offender only as an innocent third-party victim
Guarantee uninterrupted access because tenure exceeds five years
Use risk-appropriate authorization, reporting, careful documentation and possible prohibition on future relationships
questions.explanation: Confirmed first-party perpetrators may require escalated approval, exit, reporting and restrictions, unlike customers victimized by third parties.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer exit after a fraud investigation
questions.sourceSection: Customer exit after a fraud investigation

questions.stem: A fraud team reviews millions of rows and discovers repeated IP addresses linking otherwise unrelated small-value payments. Which combined approach most strengthens the finding?
options: Analyze only a single transaction and discard surrounding history
Use cleaned data and analytics to reveal relationships, followed by contextual human assessment
Accept every automated association as confirmed criminal guilt
Avoid external corroboration because it may challenge the model
questions.explanation: The guide stresses data quality, technology-assisted pattern detection and human interpretation to build defensible narratives.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Analyzing large databases to uncover patterns for an investigation
questions.sourceSection: Analyzing large databases to uncover patterns for an investigation
Leading an investigation
questions.stem: An investigation leader is preparing for a complex insider-fraud case. Which TWO actions strengthen the team’s ability to undertake a legally defensible investigation?
options: Avoid creating a plan because investigations naturally evolve
Make the suspected employee the sole custodian of relevant records
Secure management backing and adequate appropriately allocated resources
Clarify applicable legal constraints and preserve findings with supporting records
Start external publicity before establishing facts
questions.explanation: The guide advises leadership commitment, resources, legal awareness, systematic documentation and preservation. These safeguards do not require prejudging guilt, public disclosure or uncontrolled handling of evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Leading an investigation

questions.stem: A false invoice passed approvals because new employees lacked training, and managers had not checked whether training was completed. Which TWO outcomes should a well-designed RCA deliver?
options: Identify underlying control design/execution causes by probing why failures occurred and propose durable remediation
Define both immediate control fixes and longer-term prevention and testing actions.
Stop after calculating the direct cash loss
Attribute every incident solely to one employee’s personal characteristics
Keep systemic control weaknesses out of management reporting
questions.explanation: RCA follows the sequence of enabling conditions and asks why until actionable root causes and short/long-term improvements are found.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud root cause analysis
questions.sourceSection: Fraud root cause analysis
Case management strategies for fraud investigations
questions.stem: A regional fraud team needs a supervisory dashboard. Which TWO measures would directly support the case-management responsibilities described in the guide?
options: Case-stage tracking and the volume of unresolved referrals
Investigators’ personal social media activity unrelated to the case
A list of employee birthdays
Assignment ownership and approaching SLA deadlines
Marketing conversions unrelated to fraud
questions.explanation: Centralized case management and management dashboards help track responsibility, progress and SLA adherence. These are operational controls distinct from unrelated personnel or marketing metrics.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Case management strategies for fraud investigations

questions.stem: A company delays recognizing expenses and records unsupported asset values to improve current profitability. Which underlying fraud type is the primary concern?
options: A normal temporary difference requiring no supporting analysis
A phishing attack dependent on an external impersonator
Financial statement misrepresentation through revenue, asset or liability manipulation
Money muling restricted to low-value accounts
questions.explanation: The guide identifies fictitious sales, inflated assets, deferred expenses and concealed liabilities as financial statement fraud indicators.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Financial statement fraud
questions.sourceSection: Financial statement fraud
Legal and ethical considerations in fraud investigations
questions.stem: Fraud investigators request a data exchange with an external payment institution. Which TWO safeguards align with the study guide?
options: Verify the legal authority or permissions for sharing the information
Ignore applicable privacy requirements when the amount is large
Send full case files to any contact who claims to represent the institution
Limit disclosures to relevant information and preserve how evidence was obtained and handled
Replace the source data with unsupported summaries before sharing
questions.explanation: The guide requires appropriate permissions when interacting with external institutions, lawful collection and proper evidence management. Data sharing needs an authorized basis and an accountable audit trail.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Legal and ethical considerations in fraud investigations

questions.stem: A customer is repeatedly warned about money-moving requests but consciously avoids asking where the funds come from. Which money-mule category BEST fits the guide’s definitions?
options: Unwitting mule with no meaningful warning signs
Complicit mule necessarily advertising criminal services
Victim of card-present fraud
Witting or willfully blind mule
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes willful blindness from genuinely unwitting involvement and fully complicit participation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Money mules and their role in fraud
questions.sourceSection: Money mules and their role in fraud
Social engineering
questions.stem: An employee is approached by a caller claiming to be a trusted supplier. Which TWO elements most strongly point toward social engineering rather than a routine commercial inquiry?
options: A request to clarify the expected delivery date
A call scheduled through the supplier’s independently verified contact channel
A fabricated emergency demanding immediate disclosure of confidential credentials
An impersonated authority figure applying emotional pressure to bypass normal verification
An invoice supported by a verified purchase order and previously validated bank details
questions.explanation: The guide links social engineering to impersonation, pretexting and emotional manipulation. A legitimate-looking contact can still be fraudulent when it uses urgency to obtain access or evade standard controls.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Social engineering

questions.stem: A case owner records observations directly onto physical evidence and stores unrelated investigations in the same unsecured file. Which practice best follows the guide?
options: Destroy all notes immediately after interviews
Maintain separately dated, securely retained notes without altering originals
Publish the full notebook to make investigations transparent
Write directly on source documents to avoid separate notes
questions.explanation: Notes should not alter source documents, should be dated, separately retained and protected according to confidentiality and retention rules.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Retaining notes on an investigation
questions.sourceSection: Retaining notes on an investigation

questions.stem: An account’s address, recovery number and approved device change immediately before unauthorized transfers. Which hypothesis and evidence combination is most persuasive initially?
options: Account takeover supported by authentication/device and profile-change history
A victim-authorized investment payment proved by the new address
Chargeback fraud evidenced only by delivery confirmation
An advance-fee scam proved solely by a marketing email
questions.explanation: Account takeover often involves unauthorized access and control of credentials or account details, supported by device/login change evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Account takeover fraud
questions.sourceSection: Account takeover fraud

questions.stem: A victim voluntarily initiates an instant payment after being tricked into believing the recipient is bank security. Which feature most specifically identifies APP fraud?
options: A new account is necessarily opened with stolen identity documents
The criminal obtains physical access to the victim’s debit card
The victim is deceived into authorizing and pushing the payment
The issuing bank initiates a card-network chargeback
questions.explanation: APP fraud involves social engineering that induces the victim to authorize a transfer; authorization does not establish legitimacy.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Authorized push payment fraud
questions.sourceSection: Authorized push payment fraud

questions.stem: An investigator receives a referral about suspicious loan originations involving several employees and hidden beneficiaries. Which plan content most directly supports a defensible investigation?
options: Only the maximum possible fraud loss with no action owners
Scope, objectives, assignments, timelines, evidence tasks, communications and possible reporting needs
An assumption that the original allegation is conclusively true
A requirement to use all external sources regardless of legality
questions.explanation: The investigation plan should specify scope, time frames, fact gathering, stakeholders and escalation/reporting responsibilities.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud investigation plan
questions.sourceSection: Fraud investigation plan

questions.stem: A case review combines value/frequency data with interview themes and witness perceptions. Which distinction is accurate?
options: Transaction amounts/counts are quantitative, while narrative motivations and perceptions are qualitative
Interview narratives are numerical simply because they can be counted later
Qualitative evidence is always less credible than transaction logs
Quantitative evidence cannot reveal patterns or trends
questions.explanation: Quantitative evidence contains measurable numerical values; qualitative evidence captures nonnumeric themes, observations and reasons.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Analyzing quantitative information
questions.sourceSection: Analyzing quantitative information
Fraud investigator roles and responsibilities
questions.stem: A fraud unit considers its responsibility finished as soon as it classifies a detected suspicious payment. What essential function is overlooked?
options: Delegating all case documentation to the victim
Setting all of the institution’s strategic credit limits
Maintaining and escalating emerging threats and supporting preventive responses
Approving every customer refund regardless of evidence
questions.explanation: The guide places alert review and investigation within a wider role: documenting cases, escalating emerging fraud threats to management and helping prevent recurrence. Alert classification without escalation or learning is incomplete.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud investigator roles and responsibilities

questions.sourceSection: Account takeover fraud
questions.stem: A bank receives allegations of account takeover after suspicious mobile-service disruptions. Which TWO records would help distinguish an attacker-controlled session from a routine customer login?
options: Authentication and device-session logs correlated with customer contact-detail changes
Relevant telecommunication/SIM changes and customer confirmation through a trusted channel
A screenshot of the bank’s home page with no transaction metadata
An unrelated advertisement found on social media
The customer’s employer’s annual balance sheet alone
questions.explanation: Account takeover investigations should examine compromised credentials, contact detail changes and authentication behavior. Corroboration across systems is stronger than relying on a generic screenshot or unrelated account information.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Account takeover fraud

questions.stem: An online-banking takeover attempt exposes stolen credentials but no fraudulent transfer has yet settled. Which organizational arrangement is most appropriate?
options: Do nothing because no loss has settled
Have a central lead coordinate cyber/fraud investigations with defined tasks and SLAs
Transfer all decisions to the customer service desk and close the case
Treat cybersecurity access records as irrelevant to financial crime
questions.explanation: Joint AFC cases can require cyber collaboration even before losses; a central coordination function should assign responsibilities and deadlines.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Internal joint AFC investigations
questions.sourceSection: Internal joint AFC investigations

questions.stem: A victim’s recollection has been summarized without confirmation that the final statement reflects what was said. Which TWO safeguards increase the reliability of the signed statement?
options: Remove contradictory details to simplify the prosecution theory
Document a neutral factual account with relevant metadata and signed/dated confirmation
Keep only a verbal recollection without a case reference
Corroborate material claims against available independent records without inserting investigator opinion.
Add investigator speculation where the witness was uncertain
questions.explanation: The guide calls for factual, neutral statements with case/interviewee details, events, supporting evidence and signed accuracy declarations.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Taking statements
questions.sourceSection: Taking statements
Identity fraud
questions.stem: A fraudster may have used another person’s identity to open an account. Which TWO findings would be most useful for testing this hypothesis?
options: A long account number without any other evidence
The presence of a complete application form alone
Inconsistencies between submitted identification and independently verified identity records
An applicant’s preference for electronic statements by itself
Evidence that application contact details, devices or delivery addresses are controlled by unrelated persons
questions.explanation: The guide discusses stolen identity information, manipulated documents and attempts to establish unauthorized account access. A mismatch with independent records and evidence of attacker-controlled communication channels are meaningful investigative leads.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Identity fraud

questions.stem: A caller appears to read from scripted answers and refuses to explain a large urgent transfer to a newly added payee. How should the investigator interpret this behavior?
options: As manipulation or coercion indicators requiring careful corroboration
As conclusive proof the customer is the offender
As irrelevant because only the transfer amount matters
As proof that the transaction is legitimate once authorization exists
questions.explanation: The guide treats nervous, coached and urgency-driven behavior as red flags, not stand-alone proof of fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer manipulation red flags
questions.sourceSection: Customer manipulation red flags

questions.stem: A processor counts recovered and unrecovered theft but omits call center cost, investigation time and training expense. Which TWO practices correctly assess the impact?
options: Distinguish actual, attempted and prevented losses and include operational and other indirect costs
Exclude investigation costs because they are not in the payment ledger
Record attempted and prevented losses separately, without treating them as confirmed stolen cash.
Treat stopped attempted fraud as cash already lost
Report direct stolen funds only
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes actual, attempted, prevented losses and direct/indirect costs when assessing impact.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Estimating financial losses from fraud
questions.sourceSection: Estimating financial losses from fraud

questions.stem: An investigator wants to challenge suspected friendly fraud under the relevant debit-card network’s processes. Which reference should govern the claim procedure?
options: An investigator’s prior preferred response regardless of scheme
The AML risk appetite statement in place of dispute rules
Only a general anti-fraud awareness pamphlet
The applicable card network and local scheme rulebooks
questions.explanation: Scheme rulebooks define chargeback handling, indemnities, dispute timelines and allocation of liability.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Using card payment scheme rulebooks in fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Using card payment scheme rulebooks in fraud investigations

questions.stem: Victim funds move from a recipient wallet to multiple intermediaries before appearing as purchases of assets. Which stage of money laundering most directly describes the intervening transfers?
options: Placement because money first enters the financial system
None, because fraud proceeds cannot be laundered
Layering because transfers obscure the money trail
Integration because every transfer is a legitimate-asset purchase
questions.explanation: The guide uses placement, layering and integration when explaining tracing; successive transfers that obscure origins are layering.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Tracing fraudulent transactions
questions.sourceSection: Tracing fraudulent transactions

questions.stem: An onboarding reviewer detects replaced text boxes and altered account details on a genuine source document. Which distinction is most accurate?
options: The document is reliable if the logo is visually correct
An altered genuine document can never be used to commit identity fraud
Counterfeit and forged documents both necessarily originate from authentic paper
A forged document is genuine but altered; a counterfeit document is fabricated to resemble an official original
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes alteration of a genuine document (forgery) from fabrication imitating an official document (counterfeit).
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer documents red flags
questions.sourceSection: Customer documents red flags

questions.stem: A fraudulent voice call claiming to be a bank fraud agent persuades a customer to disclose their login password. Which contact-channel label is most accurate?
options: Smishing through text messages
Phishing through email
Vishing through voice communications
Card-present counterfeiting
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes voice phishing (vishing), SMS phishing (smishing), and email phishing.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Phishing, vishing, and smishing
questions.sourceSection: Phishing, vishing, and smishing
Card-not-present fraud (Case example: Missed delivery text scam)
questions.stem: The guide includes a missed-delivery message case. Which TWO features make that approach effective for payment-card fraud?
options: The scheme relies only on employee expense fraud
The scam requires the customer to be physically present at a card terminal
The message proves the sender is the real shipping company
A deceptive delivery problem encourages the customer to follow a link and enter information
Apparently ordinary delivery branding or timing can lower the customer’s suspicion
questions.explanation: The case demonstrates how a realistic shipping pretext and message link can induce disclosure of card or personal information for subsequent misuse. It is a deception-led card-not-present risk, not evidence of a legitimate courier contact.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Card-not-present fraud (Case example: Missed delivery text scam)

questions.sourceSection: Fraud program thresholds that trigger a fraud alert
questions.stem: A new rule flags every transaction above a single fixed amount, although normal payment behavior differs greatly between product types. Which adjustment is best supported by the guide?
options: Remove all monetary triggers because genuine customers sometimes pay large amounts
Treat identical amount thresholds as legally mandatory for every account
Send every trigger directly to law enforcement without triage
Calibrate relevant thresholds using transaction frequency, customer patterns, product exposure, typologies and risk appetite
questions.explanation: Thresholds are based on risk appetite, product context, typical customer behavior, fraud typologies and applicable policies. A single indiscriminate threshold creates avoidable noise and may miss anomalous lower-value behavior.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud program thresholds that trigger a fraud alert

questions.sourceSection: Case management strategies for fraud investigations
questions.stem: A bank has distributed fraud case assignments through personal spreadsheets and cannot establish whether urgent referrals breached required response deadlines. Which capability is missing?
options: A financial loss report with no case-level information
A rule prohibiting investigations from involving more than one staff member
A requirement to close all cases after 24 hours
A central case management system with ownership, status, deadline tracking and management oversight
questions.explanation: The guide recommends central case management and production dashboards for oversight, assignments, metrics and service-level agreement compliance. Individual spreadsheets without consolidated tracking can conceal delays and gaps in accountability.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Case management strategies for fraud investigations

questions.sourceSection: Legal and ethical considerations in fraud investigations
questions.stem: An investigator is personally acquainted with a suspected employee and chooses to ignore evidence favorable to that employee. Which fundamental investigative requirement is being compromised?
options: Only the customer compensation process
Only the format of the final report
The banking system’s payment authentication mechanism
Objectivity, fairness and accountable handling of relevant evidence
questions.explanation: The guide requires legal compliance and an objective, fair approach to evaluating evidence. Selectively suppressing exculpatory material undermines credibility and ethical investigation standards, independent of the final suspicion level.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Legal and ethical considerations in fraud investigations

questions.sourceSection: Setup: Diego's choice
questions.stem: In the study guide’s Diego case, the fraud system holds a payment associated with apparent sextortion of a 17-year-old. Which step is presented as the most appropriate FIRST response?
options: Release the transfer because he authorized it
Ask the investigator to decide criminal charges before opening a case
Escalate the alert internally for investigation under the bank’s policy
Immediately inform Diego’s parents without following organizational procedures
questions.explanation: The Diego teaching case instructs the investigator to escalate the held transaction under the bank’s internal policy for further review. The existence of a victim and emotional pressure requires care, but neither unilateral disclosure nor immediate release replaces the prescribed investigation process.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Setup: Diego's choice

questions.stem: An OSINT review records discovered profiles without dates, keywords, search strings or the reasoning for ruling out name matches. Which documentation practice is required for a defensible audit trail?
options: Preserve only records supporting the conclusion
Delete unresolved research once the report is drafted
Log search logic, keywords, dates/times, positive and negative results and match-resolution rationale
Store everything without any access restrictions
questions.explanation: The guide stresses contemporaneous search strings, time stamps, negative searches, source reliability and why apparent matches were dismissed.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Documenting your research
questions.sourceSection: Documenting your research

questions.stem: A suspicious payment is held; device and behavioral data indicate potential misuse requiring additional evidence. How should the alert be handled under the study guide?
options: Mark nonproductive because the fraud has not been criminally proven
Treat as productive and assign appropriate follow-up investigation
Complete law-enforcement reporting as a substitute for investigation
Release automatically because the claimant authenticated successfully
questions.explanation: A productive alert has evidence of fraud or potential fraud and warrants investigation; it need not begin with a proven crime.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud alert response
questions.sourceSection: Fraud alert response
Application fraud
questions.stem: A lender receives a wave of applications sharing near-identical employer information and unusual supporting documents. Which TWO actions support investigating possible origination fraud?
options: Corroborate employer and income details independently and compare document anomalies
Delete applications that contradict a preferred fraud theory
Treat successful online form submission as conclusive verification
Assume every customer from one postal code is fraudulent
Analyze links across applications, including contact details, devices and other repeat identifiers
questions.explanation: Application fraud can involve false statements and forged supporting records. Cross-application linkage and independent validation are sound ways to test the hypothesis, while avoiding automatic guilt by association.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Application fraud

questions.sourceSection: Internal fraud
questions.stem: Which TWO examples illustrate organizational insider fraud rather than an unrelated outsider account attack?
options: An employee diverts company funds to a bank account under their control
A criminal impersonates a retail customer from another continent with no insider help
A victim responds to a fake parcel-delivery text
A customer authorizes a transfer because of a romance scam
A manager accepts a concealed kickback to influence a contract decision
questions.explanation: The guide treats asset diversion and corrupt influence by organizational insiders as forms of internal fraud. Outsider deception may involve external fraud even when internal processes are affected.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Internal fraud

questions.stem: A customer sees repeated small online card transactions followed by higher-value remote purchases at unfamiliar merchants. Which fraud typology fits the sequence?
options: Physical inventory misappropriation by an employee
In-person counterfeit-card fraud requiring a swiped physical clone
A first-party bust-out using a newly granted loan
Card-not-present fraud including possible stolen-card testing
questions.explanation: CNP fraud uses stolen card details remotely, and small test purchases can precede larger unauthorized activity.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Card-not-present fraud
questions.sourceSection: Card-not-present fraud
Setup: The CEO’s alleged email
questions.stem: In the guide’s CEO-email case, the finance team receives an urgent acquisition-related wire instruction reinforced by a trusted colleague. Which check would have most directly prevented the transfer?
options: Reply to the same email thread asking if it is genuine
Approve because time sensitivity itself confirms executive authority
Telephone the CEO using an independently verified number and confirm the instruction
Accept the colleague’s seniority as a substitute for verification
questions.explanation: The case feedback identifies direct telephone verification with a known correct number as the best response. It also shows that an insider can collude with external criminals, so apparent employee trustworthiness is not a substitute for independent confirmation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Setup: The CEO’s alleged email

questions.sourceSection: Social engineering
questions.stem: A caller claims to be from an internal IT help desk, invents a device-security emergency, and asks an employee to reveal login credentials. The caller does not exploit a software vulnerability. What is the principal mechanism?
options: Authorized penetration testing by definition
Financial statement falsification
A bank-card counterfeit based on magnetic stripe data
Pretexting through social engineering
questions.explanation: The guide identifies pretexting and impersonation as social engineering techniques that exploit trust and urgency. The attack depends on manipulating a person to disclose credentials rather than on compromising software directly.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Social engineering

questions.stem: A customer reports a transfer made after receiving repeated urgent phone calls. A junior investigator plans to ask: 'The caller was clearly a scammer and instructed you to conceal the payment, correct?' The lead investigator needs an account that can be tested against phone records and transaction logs. Which interviewing approach is most appropriate?
options: Begin with a detailed theory of the suspected crime so the interviewee can confirm or reject the conclusion immediately.
Begin with open and neutral questions, establish a chronology in the customer’s own words, and test specifics with documentary evidence.
Avoid recording the customer’s corrections because revisions can weaken the apparent consistency of the report.
Use only binary questions to obtain a consistent statement that can be scored by the investigator.
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes effective interviewing, careful questioning and accurate statements, supporting unbiased evidence gathering and corroboration.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective interviewing techniques
questions.sourceSection: Effective interviewing techniques
Identity fraud (Case example: Abraham Abdallah)
questions.stem: In the guide’s Abraham Abdallah case, what made the attempted large-scale fraud especially distinctive?
options: The collection of wealthy individuals’ identity details, diversion of deliveries and an attempted very large transfer
A legitimate customer voluntarily wiring money after a romance conversation
The use of fabricated employee payroll records to trigger bank disbursements
The creation of a fake refund portal to dispute retail purchases
questions.explanation: The case documents identity information gathered about numerous wealthy individuals, fake delivery arrangements and a reported suspicious US$10 million transfer request. These methods illustrate identity theft and attempted account access, not employee payroll or friendly fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Identity fraud (Case example: Abraham Abdallah)

questions.stem: A longstanding customer signs in using their own device, successfully authenticates, and sends funds to a new payee. During the fraud interview the customer explains that an impersonator claimed to be from the bank's security team and instructed them to transfer their balance into a supposedly safe account. No evidence indicates the credentials were stolen. Which classification is most supportable at this stage?
options: A confirmed account takeover because all unusual transfers imply third-party control of credentials.
A suspected authorized push payment scam because the customer initiated the payment under deception.
First-party chargeback fraud because the customer approved the transaction before reporting the loss.
A conventional unauthorized card-not-present transaction because the payee was previously unknown.
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes manipulated customer-authorized payments from unauthorized account takeovers and other fraud types.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Authorized push payment fraud
questions.sourceSection: Authorized push payment fraud
Investment fraud
questions.stem: A fraud report describes an investment promoter promising abnormally high returns with almost no downside and discouraging independent verification. What is the strongest initial fraud concern?
options: An ordinary low-risk fixed deposit because returns are discussed
Investment fraud exploiting unrealistic profitability claims
A confirmed insider trading offense without securities records
A standard chargeback dispute
questions.explanation: The guide describes investment fraud as misleading investors through false representations and exaggerated returns. Unrealistic assurances and resistance to verification justify further inquiry but do not, alone, establish the complete offense or a particular securities violation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Investment fraud

questions.sourceSection: Advance fee fraud
questions.stem: A person is told a large inheritance can be released only after paying processing fees to an unfamiliar account. Each time a fee is paid, another payment is demanded. Which typology fits best?
options: Advance fee fraud
ATM skimming
First-party subscription fraud
A legitimate collateral requirement established by the message
questions.explanation: Advance fee fraud induces a victim to pay upfront for a promised benefit that never materializes. Successive fees can sustain the deception. Payment demands and promised windfalls are indicators requiring verification rather than evidence of a genuine inheritance.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Advance fee fraud

questions.sourceSection: Friend and family fraud
questions.stem: A caregiver uses access provided by an elderly relative to divert funds without authorization. The victim hesitates to report because the suspected offender is a family member. What complicates this investigation?
options: All payments made by relatives are automatically authorized
Trust, dependency and emotional pressure may impede disclosure and recognition of exploitation
Family relationships remove any possibility of a criminal offense
A family connection proves a synthetic identity was created
questions.explanation: The guide discusses fraud arising through relationships of trust. Investigators should assess authorization, financial evidence and victim circumstances carefully; family relationships do not automatically legitimize withdrawals or establish their fraud classification.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Friend and family fraud

questions.sourceSection: Financial statement fraud
questions.stem: An internal investigation reviews performance figures immediately before an equity raise. Which TWO practices would be potential financial-statement fraud if intentional?
options: Disclosing a verified valuation methodology
Concealing liabilities to misstate the financial position
Recording fictitious sales to inflate revenue
Correcting a clerical error with a documented adjustment
Reconciling cash to bank statements
questions.explanation: Financial statement fraud involves deliberate manipulation of reported performance or position, including invented income and hidden obligations. Legitimate transparent corrections and reconciliations are control practices, not fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Financial statement fraud

questions.sourceSection: Application fraud
questions.stem: A loan applicant supplies employment letters showing a high salary. Independent employer confirmation contradicts the claimed occupation and the pay slips contain inconsistent figures. Which fraud exposure is most directly being examined?
options: Card-present skimming
Only investment fraud involving securities
A SWIFT recall failure
Application fraud through misrepresented qualifying information
questions.explanation: The guide describes application fraud involving false information and documents when seeking products or credit. Independent verification of employment and income helps assess the authenticity of application claims.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Application fraud

questions.sourceSection: Application fraud (Case example: COVID-19 relief fraud)
questions.stem: What general fraud-control lesson follows from the guide’s COVID-19 relief application-fraud example?
options: High-volume urgent lending or relief processes are vulnerable when applicants misrepresent eligibility and supporting details
An approved application proves the applicant’s representations were true
Emergency programs remove the need to verify eligibility
All applications submitted through a government program are fraudulent
questions.explanation: The study-guide case illustrates how perpetrators exploited emergency program processes and false information. Speed and high volume can intensify origination-fraud exposure, underscoring the need for proportionate validation and later detection.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Application fraud (Case example: COVID-19 relief fraud)

questions.sourceSection: Bribery and corruption
questions.stem: A fraud unit suspects a supplier selection was manipulated. Which TWO findings would most strongly justify further bribery/corruption investigation?
options: A timely delivery of contracted goods alone
Undisclosed benefits transferred to the procurement decision-maker by the selected vendor
Use of an openly advertised competitive tender by itself
Repeated unusual overrides favoring that vendor without a documented commercial basis
A supplier’s possession of a normal tax registration number
questions.explanation: Personal benefits and unexplained selection overrides can indicate corrupt influence over business decisions. They require corroboration through financial and process records and should not be treated as conclusive merely from suspicion.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Bribery and corruption

questions.sourceSection: Fraud indicators for organizations
questions.stem: Which TWO observations align with the guide’s categories of customer information and customer-document red flags?
options: Conflicting customer identity details that cannot be independently reconciled
A long-standing customer relationship alone
A stable identity record supported by independently verified documents
Apparent document alterations, false supporting information or suspicious inconsistencies
An account holder’s preference for paper correspondence alone
