questions.explanation: The guide separates discrepancies in customer information and irregularities in supporting documents as different red-flag categories. Investigators should verify and contextualize those findings rather than equating them with proven fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud indicators for organizations

questions.stem: An investigator concludes an allegation lacks evidence after exhausting valid leads and documenting required internal review. Which TWO elements should be resolved before closure?
options: Whether the customer is satisfied with the likely outcome
Whether documented evidence meets policies and relevant standards, required steps are complete and actionable leads/escalations are resolved
Whether all money has been recovered in full
Assess any applicable escalation or legal/reporting obligations, including evidence of unresolved red flags.
Whether the original alert was generated by a machine-learning system
questions.explanation: Closure depends on sufficient evidence and procedures, no actionable leads and appropriate escalation, not necessarily full recovery.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · When do you have enough evidence?
questions.sourceSection: When do you have enough evidence?
Bribery and corruption
questions.stem: A procurement officer agrees to award a contract to a particular supplier in return for undisclosed personal payments. Which internal-fraud mechanism most directly applies?
options: Bribery involving improper influence over an organizational decision
Unintentional money muling by an unaware customer
A third-party account takeover
An accidental payment formatting error
questions.explanation: The guide identifies bribery and corruption as internal fraud categories. A personal benefit accepted in exchange for influencing a business decision is different from accidental procedural error or an unrelated external digital account attack.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Bribery and corruption

questions.sourceSection: Customer manipulation red flags
questions.stem: A bank officer interviews a customer who is trying to make an unusual payment while receiving repeated phone instructions. Which TWO observations would increase suspicion of coercion or manipulation?
options: The customer asks for a copy of the bank’s public schedule of fees
The customer shows unusual urgency, anxiety or reliance on a third party for answers
The customer insists on secrecy because the caller instructed them not to contact the bank
The customer has a normal debit card and online access
The payment beneficiary was established several years ago and is independently verified
questions.explanation: The guide identifies secrecy, pressure and third-party coaching as indicators of potential victim manipulation. Those signs support a careful protective discussion, not an automatic conclusion that the customer is committing fraud.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer manipulation red flags

questions.sourceSection: Discrepancies in customer information red flags
questions.stem: An application lists two incompatible addresses and a telephone number that cannot be reconciled with previous verified records. How should these inconsistencies be treated?
options: As conclusive evidence of identity theft
As indicators warranting verification and contextual review, not automatic proof of fraud
As irrelevant if the balance is positive
As a reason to overwrite older data without recording changes
questions.explanation: The guide lists customer information discrepancies among fraud red flags. Investigators must corroborate apparent inconsistencies and determine whether they reflect error, legitimate changes or deliberate misrepresentation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Discrepancies in customer information red flags

questions.sourceSection: Customer documents red flags
questions.stem: A submitted wage statement contains unusual formatting and the issuing organization cannot independently confirm it. What is the appropriate evidential interpretation?
options: The discrepancies increase the need to authenticate the source and examine related application information
The document automatically proves internal corruption
All documents with unusual fonts must be classified counterfeit
Visual authenticity alone is enough to approve it
questions.explanation: The guide identifies document inconsistencies and questionable supporting information as potential fraud indicators. A format anomaly is a lead for source checking, not a final determination of fabrication.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer documents red flags

questions.sourceSection: Unusual account activity red flags
questions.stem: A savings account with minimal historic activity suddenly receives numerous unrelated credits and immediately sends most proceeds onward. Which initial classification is best?
options: A confirmed card-network dispute
Normal account activity by definition because incoming credits are allowed
Established criminal guilt solely because activity is rapid
Potentially anomalous account behavior requiring review of source, purpose and counterparties
questions.explanation: Unusual funding and rapid onward movement are among patterns considered during investigative assessment. The guide treats such activity as a red flag rather than conclusive proof; ordinary behavior and explanations must be evaluated.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Unusual account activity red flags

questions.sourceSection: Transactions inconsistent with the customer’s profile red flags
questions.stem: A customer described as conducting only domestic retail transactions begins making large international supplier payments with no evident business change. What makes the activity suspicious?
options: Departure from known customer purpose and transactional profile
A foreign beneficiary always confirms sanctions evasion
Use of an international channel automatically constitutes fraud
The absence of chargebacks on the account
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes comparing transactions with the customer profile, typical behavior and legitimate economic purpose. A material profile deviation justifies verification and investigation, without necessarily proving a fraudulent scheme.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Transactions inconsistent with the customer’s profile red flags

questions.sourceSection: Account takeover fraud
questions.stem: A customer reports losing mobile service shortly before the attacker receives authentication messages and changes account details. What vulnerability deserves immediate examination?
options: A standard merchant refund request
Financial statement overvaluation
Possible SIM-swap-enabled account takeover despite use of SMS-based authentication
An ordinary card chargeback by the genuine accountholder
questions.explanation: The guide describes account takeover through compromised credentials and highlights limitations of SMS-based multi-factor authentication where an attacker gains control of the phone number. Investigators should examine telecom, login and profile-change evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Account takeover fraud

questions.sourceSection: Money mules and their role in fraud
questions.stem: A job advertisement offers commission to receive transfers into a personal bank account and forward them to strangers. The applicant is told to describe the deposits as family support. Which risk is most directly raised?
options: Proof of an innocent account holder without investigation
Potential money-mule recruitment and laundering of fraud proceeds
A verified charity collection
A routine payroll process with employer controls
questions.explanation: The guide covers money mules as intermediaries moving funds linked to fraud. Job offers requiring personal accounts, unexplained incoming funds and onward transfers warrant examination of intent, recruitment and payment trails.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Money mules and their role in fraud

questions.sourceSection: Customer manipulation red flags
questions.stem: A customer insists a transfer must be made in minutes and says a supposed security adviser forbade speaking to branch employees. Which feature heightens concern?
options: The customer’s use of mobile banking itself
The existence of a savings account
The insistence on secrecy and urgency consistent with manipulation
A transfer value below the reporting threshold
questions.explanation: The guide highlights secrecy, urgency and coached or pressured behavior in fraud victim manipulation. Those behavioral signals should lead to careful questioning and verification, rather than automatic attribution of wrongdoing to the customer.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer manipulation red flags

questions.stem: An investigator examines an allegedly fraudulent cross-border transfer that moved from a retail account through multiple correspondent relationships. Available records include a SWIFT message, the bank's debit record and an external payee name whose spelling varies. The goal is to build a defensible payment chronology and pursue recovery. Which TWO next steps are best?
options: Delete intermediate transaction records once the payment’s final jurisdiction has been identified.
Reconcile internal transfer timestamps and references with available payment-message identifiers and beneficiary information.
Assume the beneficiary-name discrepancy proves the recipient owns the entire laundering network.
Coordinate through authorized channels with relevant institutions to obtain trace information and consider possible recovery actions.
Treat the payment’s initial account debit as proof that no later layering or transfer could have occurred.
questions.explanation: The guide describes tracing flows across transaction records and networks and using appropriate interbank cooperation to follow and potentially recover funds.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Tracing fraudulent transactions
questions.sourceSection: Tracing fraudulent transactions

questions.stem: A live high-risk payment triggers a rule after a new payee was added from an unusual device. An operations analyst receives the alert while the payment is still pending, but an initial customer callback goes unanswered. The bank’s response manual authorizes temporary holds and rapid escalation under defined conditions. Which TWO actions BEST protect the investigation without prematurely concluding fraud?
options: Escalate and document the alert, supporting indicators and attempted verification according to the response procedure.
File a conclusive fraud finding as soon as the callback fails because silence establishes customer complicity.
Change historical account login records to mark the unusual device as an established customer device.
Release the payment automatically because the absence of customer confirmation cannot prove fraud.
Apply the relevant risk-based temporary payment restriction if policy criteria are satisfied.
questions.explanation: The guide prioritizes following alert-response procedure, documenting evidence and undertaking authorized interim steps pending investigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud alert response
questions.sourceSection: Fraud alert response
Evidence gathering for fraud investigations
questions.stem: An investigator receives both original transaction records and an anonymous allegation about the same payments. Which TWO practices support evidential quality?
options: Assume anonymous allegations are always false and irrelevant
Preserve original or authenticated records with clear provenance and access history
Alter original transaction logs to fit the allegation’s timeline
Disclose all internal information publicly to solicit opinions
Treat the unverified allegation as a lead to test against reliable independent material
questions.explanation: The guide requires relevant, reliable evidence obtained lawfully and preserved appropriately. Allegations initiate inquiry but must be tested; they do not displace stronger primary records or justify changing evidence.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Evidence gathering for fraud investigations

questions.sourceSection: Analyzing quantitative information
questions.stem: A team finds 200 linked transfers after creating a network report. Which TWO follow-up checks most effectively avoid treating a statistical pattern as proof of fraud?
options: Exclude conflicting records to simplify interpretation
Rely on a visualization alone without inspecting underlying payments
Treat correlation as conclusive criminal intent
Corroborate meaningful links with other records and the customer context
Verify source-data quality and whether relationships have legitimate explanations
questions.explanation: The guide addresses quantitative analysis and the role of human review. Repeated links can identify suspicious behavior, but reliable interpretation also depends on data quality, context and corroboration.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Analyzing quantitative information

questions.sourceSection: Sources of evidence in fraud investigations
questions.stem: An investigator has a screenshot of a supposed payment confirmation but bank settlement records show no payment. Which principle should govern the finding?
options: Independent transactional records and provenance should be compared before accepting the screenshot
Only interviews may be used to establish the amount transferred
The screenshot is superior because it resembles a bank interface
Any payment screenshot is inadmissible regardless of context
questions.explanation: The guide addresses obtaining and assessing evidence from different sources. Records must be evaluated for authenticity, accuracy and relevance; contradictory independent data may undermine a screenshot even when it looks credible.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Sources of evidence in fraud investigations

questions.sourceSection: Who reads the fraud investigation report, and why?
questions.stem: A significant internal payment fraud has regulatory implications. Which TWO audiences may appropriately require an investigation report, depending on the circumstances and authorization?
options: Relevant internal leadership, compliance/legal teams or internal audit
Regulators or law enforcement where permitted or required
Every employee in the institution regardless of their role
The general public before factual findings are tested
Any unrelated vendor that asks for it
questions.explanation: The guide lists internal business, legal, compliance, senior management and audit stakeholders, as well as external regulators and law enforcement. Report access depends on severity, purpose and lawful communication responsibilities.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Who reads the fraud investigation report, and why?

questions.sourceSection: External resources for complex fraud investigations
questions.stem: A merchant will not voluntarily provide original records, and a fraud investigator wants to compel production by personally entering the merchant’s office. Which principle applies?
options: The merchant’s refusal requires immediate deletion of internal evidence
Bank investigators may exercise general seizure powers whenever fraud is suspected
Compulsory seizure belongs to authorized law-enforcement or legal processes; the team should pursue permitted cooperation and escalation
A suspected fraud claim automatically transfers property rights to the bank
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes available investigative resources from powers held by authorities. The fraud team should preserve its own records and use lawful procedures and relevant external partners when compelled access is necessary.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · External resources for complex fraud investigations

questions.sourceSection: Fraud reporting requirements
questions.stem: A confirmed fraud event triggers internal escalation requirements and potential external reporting obligations. Which TWO actions are consistent with the guide?
options: Avoid maintaining records once an external report is filed
Use documented internal reporting channels to gather and escalate relevant facts
Identify applicable jurisdictional recipients and mandatory reporting timescales
Provide reports to any external party irrespective of permissions
Delay every report until all money is recovered
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes internal reporting and external obligations that vary by jurisdiction and fraud type. Reporting teams should comply with relevant requirements and deadlines while maintaining appropriate investigation records.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud reporting requirements

questions.sourceSection: Open-source intelligence for investigations
questions.stem: An online advertisement promoting a fraudulent investment may disappear. Which action most improves later evidential review?
options: Capture its content, URL, retrieval date and surrounding context while documenting how it was found
Rely on an investigator remembering the advertising language
Treat the advertisement as a judicial finding that fraud occurred
Edit the live page to prevent changes
questions.explanation: The guide encourages careful OSINT collection and documentation of sources. Capturing dynamic public material with provenance supports later corroboration and provides an audit trail when websites or posts change.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Open-source intelligence for investigations

questions.sourceSection: Tracing fraudulent transactions
questions.stem: A fraud investigation confirms an outgoing transfer was induced by an impersonation scam only minutes earlier. What consideration should shape the team’s immediate response?
options: Early engagement with relevant banks and approved recall or blocking channels while preserving the trace
Delay all recovery requests until the case report is fully drafted
Close the customer account before contacting receiving institutions
Treat a completed electronic transfer as impossible to pursue
questions.explanation: Tracing fraudulent transactions and seeking rapid coordination can improve the prospects of fund recovery. The guide describes using payment trails and external financial institutions; recovery efforts should proceed through authorized channels without waiting for the full report.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Tracing fraudulent transactions

questions.sourceSection: Using card payment scheme rulebooks in fraud investigations
questions.stem: A dispute handler believes a card transaction is fraudulent but the claim is close to the applicable chargeback deadline. What must the handler consult?
options: The investigator’s general preference for refunding
The customer’s annual salary
Only the organization’s marketing refund promises
The relevant global or local card scheme’s evidential requirements and dispute time limits
questions.explanation: The guide says card network and local payment scheme rulebooks govern chargeback evidence, conditions and timescales. A substantive fraud suspicion does not remove the need to observe the applicable process.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Using card payment scheme rulebooks in fraud investigations

questions.stem: A customer is distressed after losing savings in a romance scam and demands an immediate promise of reimbursement. Investigation and reimbursement eligibility are not yet determined, while preliminary case review is under way. Which response is most appropriate for a fraud investigator?
options: Explain the known facts, investigation and potential recovery steps empathetically, avoid guaranteeing an outcome and provide a clear channel for updates.
Focus exclusively on the customer’s failure to recognize the scam, as advice on victim behavior is more important than explaining next steps.
Commit to a full refund immediately to restore trust, with eligibility to be checked only after the case is closed.
Tell the customer not to contact the bank again until investigators confirm whether criminal charges will be filed.
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes sensitive victim communication, clear expectations and informing customers without compromising investigations or promising unsupported outcomes.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective communication for victims of fraud
questions.sourceSection: Effective communication for victims of fraud

questions.topic: Closing an investigation with sufficient evidence
questions.stem: A reported first-party chargeback claim has been investigated using device logs, customer communications and merchant evidence. Several indicators support intentional misuse, but the file lacks documentation of why some apparently contradictory evidence was discounted. A manager proposes closing the case immediately because the analytical conclusion is strong. What is the MOST defensible response?
options: Complete a balanced evaluation of the contrary evidence, confirm required procedures and documentation, and assess any remaining actionable lines of inquiry before closure.
Close immediately because an investigator’s conclusion outweighs contradictory material once the file is otherwise substantial.
Close on the basis of the merchant’s records alone because additional customer evidence can only introduce uncertainty.
Keep the case open indefinitely until the subject confesses, irrespective of the other corroborated evidence.
questions.explanation: The guide requires evaluating evidence against internal policy, following investigation procedures and checking that there are no further actionable leads.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · When do you have enough evidence?
questions.sourceSection: When do you have enough evidence?
Effective interviewing techniques
questions.stem: An investigator plans to interview a suspect after hearing witnesses, but has not prepared for explanations that contradict the original allegation. Which improvement most directly follows the guide?
options: Use only closed accusations to obtain immediate agreement
Invite all witnesses to the suspect interview together
Prevent the suspect from explaining discrepancies
Prepare relevant questions, anticipate possible answers and assemble evidence for a balanced interview
questions.explanation: The guide recommends a planned interview, including the interviewer, key questions and likely responses, after gathering information from victims and witnesses. Preparation helps assess differing accounts without prejudging the outcome.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective interviewing techniques

questions.sourceSection: Documenting your decision-making process
questions.stem: A fraud team changes the focus of an investigation after new evidence contradicts the initial assumption. Which TWO items belong in a defensible decision log?
options: An edited version of the record that conceals mistakes
Dates, decisions, owners and next steps that allow the change to be reconstructed
The evidence and reasoning that justified changing investigative direction
Only the original allegation with later developments omitted
A statement that investigators never reconsider a theory
questions.explanation: The guide requires documentation of the evolving investigative approach, including why the strategy changed. A transparent decision trail supports audit and later review and distinguishes measured reassessment from unsupported reversals.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Documenting your decision-making process

questions.sourceSection: Customer exit after a fraud investigation (Case example: The money mule mastermind)
questions.stem: The guide’s money-mule-mastermind case describes a bank ending a relationship after confirming deliberate fraud. Which TWO lessons follow from that case?
options: Keep the relationship automatically because the customer is long-standing
Gather sufficient evidence and obtain the required authorization before exiting the customer
Close every fraud alert without verifying who committed the crime
Erase the case after customer termination
Carry out relevant reporting and preserve supporting records as part of an accountable exit process
questions.explanation: The guide’s case emphasizes evidential sufficiency, approval and appropriate documentation before customer exit. Closing an account is an organizational outcome, not a substitute for compliance or investigative controls.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Customer exit after a fraud investigation (Case example: The money mule mastermind)

questions.sourceSection: Potential organizational outcomes of an investigation
questions.stem: An investigation is stopped early to save staff costs despite unresolved reporting duties and material evidence gaps. What risk categories does the guide identify?
options: Only cyber infrastructure damage
Only potential credit market losses
Regulatory, financial, legal and reputational
Only lost marketing opportunities
questions.explanation: The guide explicitly groups the potential consequences of continuing or ending investigations too soon into regulatory, financial, legal and reputational risks. Apparent short-term efficiency does not negate these exposures.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Potential organizational outcomes of an investigation

questions.sourceSection: Retaining supporting documents
questions.stem: Two investigation teams hold relevant electronic records in personal folders with inconsistent naming and retention arrangements. What is the most defensible improvement?
options: Allow every team to delete its documents after interview completion
Store all records on personal messaging accounts
Restrict evidence retention to paper statements only
Agree a secure filing system at the beginning of investigations and retain material according to policy and law
questions.explanation: The guide recommends a formal filing structure known to investigators and secure retention of both paper and electronic supporting documents under organizational and legal retention requirements.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Retaining supporting documents

questions.sourceSection: Investigation report structure and format
questions.stem: A fraud report contains definitive accusations but no account of evidence examined, inquiries performed or reasons for the conclusions. Which element is missing?
options: More technical jargon in place of the evidence
A list of unrelated fraud trends
A structured, objective explanation of allegations, methods, findings and rationale
A guarantee that the first suspicion is correct
questions.explanation: The guide describes reports that outline the allegation, inquiries, people engaged, findings and rationale, potentially with recommendations. The report should be clear and objective so decision-makers can understand how conclusions were reached.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Investigation report structure and format

questions.topic: Reasons to retain a fraud-linked account
questions.sourceSection: Maintaining an account after fraud activity
questions.stem: An institution confirms fraud risk on an account but cannot immediately close it because a court order applies. Which response is most consistent with the guide?
options: Remove all restrictions because the account remains open
Ignore the court order because all fraud-linked accounts must be exited
Document the reason for retention, comply with applicable obligations and apply appropriate monitoring and mitigations
Erase records of the suspected activity to protect privacy
questions.explanation: The guide allows circumstances in which an account remains open despite confirmed fraud, including legal orders, contractual obligations and risk-appetite decisions. Remaining open requires documented governance and appropriate risk mitigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Maintaining an account after fraud activity

questions.sourceSection: Effective techniques for interviewing victims, whistleblowers, and witnesses
questions.stem: A witness recalls seeing a suspect at a branch, but access logs place the suspect elsewhere at that time. Which next action best supports an objective interview?
options: Disregard the access log because human memory is always more accurate
Explain the discrepancy neutrally, ask the witness to clarify the timeline and compare both records with independent evidence
Tell the witness to change the signed statement to match the investigator’s preferred theory
Conclude the witness is deliberately lying without further inquiry
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes careful, non-leading interviews and corroboration. A contradiction between recollection and objective records should be examined rather than resolved by automatic disbelief or pressure on the witness.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Effective techniques for interviewing victims, whistleblowers, and witnesses

questions.sourceSection: Fraud feedback loop
questions.stem: An institution has completed root cause analysis of repeated beneficiary-change fraud. Which TWO steps are needed to turn the findings into measurable improvement?
options: Assign actionable control recommendations to relevant teams and define measurable outcomes
Limit the findings to a single investigator’s private notes
Treat every closed fraud case as evidence that all control weaknesses are resolved
Test whether new or modified controls reduce the identified weakness over time
Stop updating fraud models after the first corrective action
questions.explanation: The guide describes a feedback loop where investigations and root causes are shared with relevant resolution teams that implement controls. Measurable targets and ongoing effectiveness checks complete the cycle.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud feedback loop

questions.stem: A fraud manager receives two urgent referrals. Case A concerns one customer with a large but potentially recoverable transfer. Case B involves many small transfers linked by device and beneficiary evidence, with new customer complaints arriving each hour. Both have the same initial estimated exposure and identical regulatory reporting deadlines. The team has capacity for one intensive investigation first. Which factor should have the GREATEST influence on its priority decision?
options: Consider linked incidents, continuing risk, customer impact and the possibility of further losses, not merely single-case monetary value.
Work Case A first because a larger individual payment should outrank any cluster of smaller payments.
Assign Case B solely on the basis of alert volume, regardless of severity, current impact or evidence quality.
Prioritize whichever referral was recorded in the case management system first, since chronological ordering is most consistent.
questions.explanation: The guide supports combining risk-based, monetary and customer-impact approaches, with adjustments for linked incidents and emerging trends. A case’s wider and continuing consequences affect allocation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Case management strategies for fraud investigations
questions.sourceSection: Case management strategies for fraud investigations

questions.stem: An automated fraud alert identifies a potentially urgent transaction, but the available facts do not yet establish wrongdoing. The investigator must choose a proportionate and documented early-stage response. An alert flags a high-value new payee with unusual device activity, and payment release is pending review. Management prefers a quick decision, but independent challenge requires the action to be supported by the scenario rather than a convenient assumption. Which TWO early-stage actions follow the guide?
options: Wait for the transaction to complete before reviewing an available live alert
Close the case solely because the detection system might produce false positives
Immediately declare that the customer committed fraud
Document the alert triage and relevant interim restrictions/assignments in the centralized case process.
Follow the fraud response policy/SLA, triage risk and take appropriate interim preventive action
questions.explanation: The guide begins alert response with applicable procedures and prioritization, then triage and permitted protective action before full investigation.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Fraud Investigations · Fraud alert response

The applicable card network and local scheme rulebooks
Only a general anti-fraud awareness pamphlet
An investigator’s prior preferred response regardless of scheme

questions.stem: A financial institution is reconciling customer complaints, loss data and unusual employee activity. Senior management wants the response to distinguish suspected fraud from ordinary processing failures and unsupported assumptions. A payments provider struggles to spot scams that spread across institutions without appearing significant inside any one institution. The proposed action will affect customer treatment and control effectiveness, so the reviewer must distinguish the immediate fraud issue from broader process improvements. Which TWO design principles best fit a responsible consortium approach?
options: A nonconsortium model using only internal records
Apply lawful information-sharing safeguards to partner data used for fraud detection.
A product-level system that excludes other market participants
A consortium model pooling permissible cross-organization fraud signals
A spreadsheet of only the bank’s resolved cases
questions.explanation: Consortium approaches combine multiple participants’ data/insights and can reveal patterns hidden within individual institutions.

questions.stem: A financial institution is reconciling customer complaints, loss data and unusual employee activity. Senior management wants the response to distinguish suspected fraud from ordinary processing failures and unsupported assumptions. A bank wants to compare user location with prior usage to verify unusual login attempts. The organization has limited investigative and control resources. The best answer should address the most relevant weakness without overstating what the observations prove. Which additional requirement does the supplied guide highlight?
options: Retain precise location data indefinitely for convenience
Device location is a substitute for every other identity factor
Obtain relevant opt-in/consent and meet privacy requirements for location tracking
Location data can always be captured without customer consent
questions.explanation: The guide notes that device intelligence may leverage geolocation, but location tracking requires relevant customer permission under privacy rules.

questions.stem: At an annual enterprise fraud risk assessment, the first line has reported a previously underestimated threat and the second line is challenging the proposed risk treatment. The board wants a decision backed by relevant evidence. Management wants to assess a rare but potentially catastrophic insider collusion event that historical averages barely capture. A recent quality review found that staff had relied on a superficially persuasive explanation. This time the decision must reflect the specific facts and purpose of the control. Which tool best probes this risk during the assessment?
options: Randomly lowering all transaction limits
Replacing the entire audit function with dashboards
Scenario analysis of low-likelihood, high-impact events
Only historical mean transaction size
questions.explanation: The guide highlights scenario analysis for risks that are unlikely but capable of producing severe losses.

True positive
True negative
False positive

Sarbanes-Oxley Act
The UK Payment Services Regulations
Dodd-Frank consumer whistleblower provisions alone

An investigation team wants a planned, ethical and nonconfrontational method for accurate information gathering. The PEACE model
A requirement to reveal all interviewee records to every witness
The Reid technique’s admission-oriented approach

Missing values and differences in format are producing inconsistent analysis outcomes. A high-value transfer triggers an outlier score, but the customer recently sold a property and has legitimate documentation. The fraud team must defend the resulting decision to an oversight committee and explain why an alternative that sounds reasonable would not adequately resolve the identified issue. How should the analyst interpret the alert?
options: As conclusive evidence of a committed crime
As grounds to erase the customer’s legitimate history
As a signal requiring contextual validation and risk-based review
As irrelevant because any unusual event is always benign
questions.explanation: Anomalies flag unusual behavior; human review and context establish whether the activity indicates fraud.

questions.stem: A mid-sized bank has two competing investment proposals. An account-takeover upgrade addresses a high-frequency threat, while a new check-control project addresses an infrequent but potentially catastrophic insider event. The business heads defend their respective budgets using historical losses, but the bank has also launched a new digital product and changed its customer mix. The chief risk officer must recommend which project should be funded first. What is the MOST defensible basis for this decision?
options: Rank both projects by their previous twelve-month direct loss totals and fund the higher amount.
Complete a refreshed enterprise fraud risk assessment covering emerging exposure, control effectiveness, residual risk, impact and likelihood before prioritizing funding.
Allocate funding in proportion to transaction volumes, since higher-volume activities necessarily create the greatest overall exposure.
Give precedence to the project with the strongest vendor demonstration because implementation feasibility determines the correct risk priority.
questions.explanation: An updated enterprise-wide assessment compares inherent exposure, current controls and remaining residual risk, including evolving threats and business changes. Historic losses, channel volumes and vendor readiness are inputs, but none alone establishes the highest fraud priority.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS Study Guide v1.03 · Building a Fraud Risk Management Program · Principles for an effective fraud risk assessment

To label every targeted employee a fraudster
To simulate attacks and discover exploitable weaknesses before criminals do
To replace any later investigation into real losses
questions.explanation: The guide describes fraud penetration testing as controlled attack simulation that reveals control, technical and training gaps.

A suspected staff member has access to the emails and logs that could corroborate allegations of phantom vendor payments. A second line reviewer asks the team to explain the distinction between similar-sounding remedies before accepting its recommendation. Which TWO protective practices are appropriate?
options: Restrict sensitive case information to necessary people and maintain an evidence custody trail.
Coordinate with HR/IT and relevant owners to secure evidence and handle employee protections lawfully
Publish the allegations to all staff to solicit opinions
Ask the suspected employee to delete copies of disputed documents
Demand an immediate confession before gathering any records

Exclude investigation costs because they are not in the payment ledger
Treat stopped attempted fraud as cash already lost
Record attempted and prevented losses separately, without treating them as confirmed stolen cash.

Whether documented evidence meets policies and relevant standards, required steps are complete and actionable leads/escalations are resolved

Whether the original alert was generated by a machine-learning system

Inspect false negatives and true positives rather than assuming majority-class accuracy is enough.

questions.stem: During pilot validation, a fraud model alerts on 160 transactions. Investigation confirms that 64 alerts are fraudulent and 96 are legitimate. Separately, quality sampling identifies 16 fraudulent transactions that the model failed to alert. The model owner wants the board to understand alert precision and actual-fraud recall before lowering the threshold. Which statement correctly reports the two measures?
options: Precision 80% and recall 40%.
Precision 40% and recall 80%.
Precision 40% and recall 40%.
Precision 80% and recall 80%.
questions.explanation: Precision equals confirmed fraud among flagged items: 64/160 = 40%. Recall equals flagged fraud among all actual fraud: 64/(64+16) = 80%. Changing the threshold should consider false positives and missed fraud together.

The manager wants a metric that specifically assesses how consistently the model recognizes legitimate cases rather than labeling them fraudulent. Which performance measure is the most direct fit?

Allocate identical resources to all products regardless of risk
Delay all spending until a confirmed fraud event occurs
Incorporate emerging fraud patterns and likely customer impacts when reviewing controls.
Approve the most expensive preventive tool before assessing exposure

Assume a defined age group is automatically culpable

questions.stem: A consumer lending business prepares its risk and control self-assessment. Its staff have identified manipulation of income documents, a high potential loss if controls fail, and an automated verification control that has not been tested after a recent systems change. Management labels the exposure “low residual risk” solely because the control is listed in a policy. Which TWO actions would most improve the assessment?
options: Assess the inherent impact and likelihood, then test the actual effectiveness of the verification control before assigning residual risk.
Document material gaps, responsible owners, deadlines and resources in a prioritized corrective action plan.
Calculate residual risk using the existence of documented policies without operational testing.
Defer the assessment until there is confirmed fraud rather than hypothesized exposure.
Transfer ownership of the full assessment to marketing because customer perception is part of fraud impact.
questions.explanation: RCSA assesses identified risks, likelihood, impact and the operating strength of current controls, then turns critical gaps into tracked actions. Merely documenting a control is not evidence that it effectively mitigates risk.

questions.stem: A fraud classifier performs exceptionally on historical transactions used for training but much worse on newly collected applications. Model developers discover that several fraud typologies emerged after the training period and that the original model was heavily optimized against a small labeled sample. Which TWO steps best address the evidence?
options: Test on truly unseen observations and use cross-validation to assess generalization rather than judging training fit alone.
Refresh the labeled training information, tune the model and monitor future results as fraud patterns evolve.
Keep parameters unchanged because a strong original training result establishes effective live discrimination.
Adopt the highest score threshold without validation so the number of false positives immediately decreases.
Remove the separate evaluation data and use the full historic sample to report stronger training performance.
questions.explanation: Poor performance on unseen data can indicate overfitting or changing fraud patterns. The guide supports cross-validation, out-of-sample assessment, retraining on updated labeled data and controlled threshold tuning.

Delay investigation until the recipient admits wrongdoing

The vendor has passed a commercial tender, while a bank employee responsible for the contract has a previously undeclared relationship with one of its directors. Procurement says the price is favorable and the contract should start. Which response BEST reflects the guide’s employee and vendor fraud controls?
options: Proceed with restricted systems access and leave conflict-of-interest review until the first annual renewal.
Conduct risk-appropriate vendor and relevant-person screening, assess security controls and employee conflicts, and monitor the relationship throughout its term.
Concentrate on screening the vendor’s published customer list, because that predicts whether employees will collude.
Limit diligence to a one-time background check of the employee, since vendor cybersecurity does not relate to fraud risk.

It involves deliberate deception for an improper advantage

It requires breakdown of at least one technology control

The investigator finds a pending high-value payment, incomplete access logs and a pattern of similar earlier complaints. The risk committee requests a review of whether the new measures work and separate assurance that the fraud program has not overlooked wider control weaknesses. Which TWO assignments best preserve the respective lines of defense while providing meaningful challenge?
options: Fraud operations and analytics own day-to-day detection and response, and provide evidence of how the controls are working.
Internal audit performs an independent assessment of control effectiveness and tests how management addressed the weakness.

questions.stem: A bank identifies a deliberately falsified application and stops it before disbursing funds. A manager argues that the absence of a booked loss means the incident can be omitted from reporting consideration. Which decision is most defensible?
options: Confine reporting to internal operational loss records because no money left the bank.
Assess the attempted conduct against the applicable fraud-reporting obligations and retain the rationale, even when the attempted fraud caused no loss.
Treat the rejected application as a training event and defer any reporting decision until a similar attempt succeeds.
Report only if an eventual criminal conviction establishes that the applicant intended to deceive the bank.
questions.explanation: The guide explains a duty to report suspected fraud and relevant reporting obligations; a thwarted attempt is not automatically irrelevant simply because financial loss was prevented.

questions.stem: A bank's education page receives many visits, yet victims of a new impersonation scam continue to disclose OTPs during telephone calls. Which change most directly tests whether customer education is effective?
options: Hold customers solely responsible for failing to read the existing page.
Refresh the online fraud-warning page quarterly and measure readership, without checking whether customers recognize or report live impersonation attempts.
Introduce scam-specific simulations and measure whether customers recognize warning signs and report attempted manipulation.
Replace fraud alerts with a one-off generic annual policy notice.
questions.explanation: The guide treats education as an ongoing, current-threat program, not a distribution exercise. Recognition and timely reporting test whether awareness translates into protective action; traffic, generic notices, and liability assumptions do not establish this. The strongest competing approach falls short because readership alone measures exposure to a message, not how the customer behaves when a live fraud attempt occurs.

questions.stem: A whistleblower reports manipulated staff-expense reimbursements. The investigator intends to speak to the whistleblower, a neutral finance control owner and three colleagues who regularly socialize with the suspected employee. The head of department asks that the accused employee’s close colleagues be interviewed first, using leading questions, because this may accelerate a confession. Which TWO approaches best support defensible information gathering?
options: Start with the whistleblower and other firsthand information, then neutral stakeholders before associates of the suspected person.
Use planned, broad open-ended questions before moving to focused clarification and corroboration.
Begin with questions that assume misconduct because this reduces variation in witness answers.
Ask all witnesses to jointly agree on one narrative before formal statements are recorded.
Delay receiving the whistleblower’s account until investigators have drawn conclusions from the suspect’s associates.
questions.explanation: The guide recommends an interview sequence beginning with victims or whistleblowers, then neutral stakeholders and later suspect-linked witnesses, combined with broad and non-leading initial questions.

questions.stem: A fraud modeller uses a bank's internal transaction records to detect account takeover but misses identities previously flagged at other institutions. Which data strategy most directly addresses the blind spot?
options: Import external suspicious-person names as definitive fraud outcomes, without testing the match quality or linking them to the customer's activity.
Add unrelated advertising data without defining a fraud detection purpose.
Combine internal behavior and known-fraud data with appropriately authorized consortium, credit bureau, or law-enforcement intelligence, then reconcile entity identifiers.
Use only confirmed losses recorded by the bank because external patterns are always irrelevant.
questions.explanation: The guide identifies complementary internal and external fraud datasets. The useful extension is linked external intelligence, not replacing the internal baseline or gathering data without an analytical purpose. The strongest competing approach falls short because external fraud markers are not reliable labels unless the bank confirms identity matches and reconciles them with its own evidence.

questions.stem: During a digital session, a customer enters valid credentials but navigation and pointer movement diverge sharply from their established pattern while remote-control activity appears. Which interpretation best reflects the NAB case?
options: Behavioral anomalies can support real-time intervention despite correct credentials; they are risk signals rather than automatic proof of fraud.
Unusual pointer activity proves the customer knowingly collaborated with a criminal.
Behavioral biometrics are limited to comparing static face or fingerprint records at onboarding.
Permanently block any session with anomalous pointer behavior without considering accessibility, context, or independent evidence of compromise.
questions.explanation: NAB's example concerns continuous interaction characteristics, including typing and navigation, that detect possible manipulation after login. The stronger interpretation triggers proportionate verification rather than treating the signal as guilt or ignoring it. The strongest competing approach falls short because a behavioral anomaly can have innocent causes, so identity attribution and permanent sanctions require further assessment.

options: Treat it as a lead for identity and relationship corroboration, not a conclusive attribution of criminal involvement.
Publish the profile as an identified suspect before legal review so that other potential victims can comment.
Ignore all public-source intelligence because no information gathered outside the bank can assist a fraud investigation.
Use the profile name as definitive proof that the recipient is the scammer, even where identity has not been established.
Validate identity, source reliability and relevance before incorporating the information into a formal report.
questions.explanation: The guide highlights external and open-source material for complex investigations but warns that public-source content can be inaccurate. Validate identity, source reliability and relevance before incorporating the information into a formal report.

questions.stem: A customer’s genuine credentials were used, but the payment followed a new-device registration and unusual location with no prior comparable activity. An analyst closes the case because correct credentials were entered. What is the flaw?
options: Credential use alone means the transfer must be treated as intentional first-party fraud regardless of other indicators.
A new device proves the customer willingly transferred the funds and removes any need for customer verification.
Account takeover is possible only if the attacker submits an entirely fictitious identity during account opening.
Valid credentials do not settle whether access was authorized; evaluate account-change, authentication, behavioral and customer evidence together.
questions.explanation: The guide’s account-takeover typology involves unauthorized use of compromised credentials and requires broader analysis.

questions.stem: An elderly customer insists that a first-time crypto transfer is for family expenses, repeatedly looks toward someone on a live call, and uses phrases that sound rehearsed. Which assessment is strongest?
options: Ignore the visible coaching because only completed losses count as fraud indicators.
Evaluate possible third-party coaching alongside the payment profile and protect the customer's ability to explain the purpose independently.
Classify the customer as an intentional money mule solely because cryptocurrency is involved.
Escalate only when the customer admits a third party is coaching them, despite contradictory behavioral and payment evidence.
questions.explanation: The guide highlights prompting and coached explanations as customer-manipulation indicators. They warrant sensitive inquiry and corroboration; neither a denial nor the payment medium establishes intent or innocence. The strongest competing approach falls short because coached victims may deny influence because the scammer controls their narrative, making admission an unreliable trigger.

questions.topic: Using card payment scheme rulebooks in fraud investigations
questions.stem: A cardholder disputes a card-not-present purchase. The investigator assumes that the bank’s internal fraud narrative automatically establishes a valid chargeback against the merchant. Which missing step is most important?
options: Assess the card scheme’s applicable dispute rules, reason codes, time limits and supporting evidence requirements.
Apply international wire-recall procedures in place of the card network’s dispute mechanism.
Approve the chargeback solely because the customer alleges fraud, regardless of the network’s process or available documentation.
Wait until criminal proceedings conclude, because card disputes cannot be assessed while any police investigation is pending.
questions.explanation: The guide stresses that effective card fraud investigation requires understanding the schemes’ chargeback rulebooks and relevant evidence and timelines.

questions.topic: Behavioral patterns and past fraudulent transactions (Case example: Checkout.com)
questions.stem: A payment processor spots repeated tiny authorizations within seconds and a sudden high-value spike from the same account. Select TWO ways to apply the Checkout.com case lessons without simply blocking all busy customers.
options: Measure transaction frequency and value across defined short windows for the account, payment instrument, or IP address.
Tune thresholds against historical legitimate high-volume behavior and false-positive outcomes.
Use only the total monthly value because rapid sequences are not informative.
Set a fixed system-wide short-window threshold without separating known high-volume legitimate merchants from newly risky accounts.
Treat each flagged payment as confirmed fraud and remove human review.
questions.explanation: Checkout.com used velocity patterns derived from past cases and tuned thresholds to retain legitimate activity. Frequency and behavioral context both matter; fixed unvalidated thresholds or aggregate monthly totals miss the short-window signal. The strongest competing approach falls short because a universal threshold can mistake legitimate payment bursts for criminal testing when operating patterns differ.

questions.topic: Key stakeholders in fraud risk management
questions.stem: A payment product launch is approved by sales. Fraud operations says its role begins only after customers complain, while compliance believes the business line need not own fraud exposure because the second line has issued a policy. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: Assign business accountability for fraud exposure and preventive controls while using specialist functions for challenge, expertise and independent assurance.
Make the chief executive the owner of every transaction-level alert, eliminating the need for delegated operational responsibilities.
Establish documented escalation and oversight responsibilities linking front-line control owners with fraud, compliance and assurance functions.
Have internal audit operate the preventive controls as the first line and independently test the same controls later.
Give fraud investigations unilateral authority over the product’s commercial risk appetite so the business can remain detached.
questions.explanation: The fraud risk management framework relies on delineated stakeholder responsibilities, business ownership, governance and effective independent review. Establish documented escalation and oversight responsibilities linking front-line control owners with fraud, compliance and assurance functions.

questions.topic: Transactional fraud risk: Customer, jurisdiction, product, channel
questions.stem: A new wallet serves verified customers but launches instant cross-border transfers via an unattended mobile channel. The sponsor treats verified identity as sufficient mitigation of all transaction fraud risk. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: A jurisdiction-only rating, because payment products and channels cannot independently contribute to fraud exposure.
A static enterprise fraud score that remains unchanged when new products and delivery channels are introduced.
Identify specific controls for the new product/channel combination and periodically reassess the residual exposure.
A multidimensional assessment of the customer, jurisdiction, product and delivery channel rather than relying on customer verification alone.
A review of customer age alone, because the origination channel can be presumed low risk after successful onboarding.
questions.explanation: The guide explicitly separates customer, jurisdiction, product and channel as transactional fraud risk dimensions, which should be assessed together. Identify specific controls for the new product/channel combination and periodically reassess the residual exposure.

Training performance is strong, but the validation sample and evidence of customer impact raise unresolved questions. A classifier performs inconsistently across demographic groups due to skewed training data and limited ongoing checks. The case has been escalated because two plausible interpretations lead to different operational outcomes. Choose the interpretation that is most defensible on the evidence. Which TWO practices are appropriate remediation?
options: Compare performance and error rates across affected groups and document corrective actions.
Use protected customer characteristics as conclusive evidence of fraud
Remove all model governance checks to increase speed
Ignore disparities because overall accuracy is high
Evaluate representation, consider augmentation/fairness constraints, and audit outcomes continuously
questions.explanation: The guide recommends evaluating imbalanced data, representative examples, fairness-aware methods and continuous monitoring.

questions.topic: Data mining and matching (Case example: Acme Bank)
questions.stem: Acme Bank finds the same phone, email, and device identifier linked to multiple otherwise unrelated accounts. What analytical conclusion should be documented first?
options: A single matching IP address is enough to attribute every transaction to one perpetrator.
The shared attributes form a linked cluster warranting account-takeover investigation and verification of whether the linkage has a legitimate explanation.
Group accounts by one common attribute and immediately attribute every transaction in that cluster to the same controller.
The accounts are independent because each has a unique account number.
questions.explanation: The Acme Bank case illustrates data matching and clustering to uncover possible coordinated compromise. Links create a testable hypothesis, not conclusive attribution; unique account IDs do not erase shared operational indicators. The strongest competing approach falls short because shared attributes can arise from household, business, or technical relationships and do not alone establish shared control.

questions.stem: Terria improves a detection model after deployment as fraud tactics change. Select TWO characteristics that support defensible continued use of such a model.
options: Retune or retrain when validated feedback shows performance deterioration, documenting the change.
Evaluate performance on representative unseen data and monitor new patterns after implementation.
Retrain only after public fraud reports appear, rather than using validated production outcomes and emerging internal patterns.
Automatically reject all new device signatures without checking legitimate customer impact.
Use in-sample fit as conclusive evidence that future fraud will be detected.
questions.explanation: The guide's Terria case emphasizes training, tuning, and adaptation. The two sound actions address generalization and ongoing change; static thresholds, training-only success, and indiscriminate blocks can conceal deterioration or harm legitimate use. The strongest competing approach falls short because waiting for public confirmation can miss early deterioration visible in validated production feedback.

questions.stem: A mystery-shopper exercise submits an invoice with a legitimate supplier name but altered beneficiary banking details. Two authorized approvers process the payment correctly under the formal maker-checker procedure, yet the payment-detail verification rule fails to alert because the difference falls below a configured tolerance. The team concludes the entire control is effective because two signatures were recorded. What conclusion is BEST?
options: The approval process operated, but the combined control design or execution has a detectable gap that needs remediation and retesting.
The controls are sufficient because a fraudster would have to breach both approval and payment systems simultaneously.
The test should be invalidated because deliberately simulated fraudulent invoices are unsuitable for operating-effectiveness testing.
The control framework should be treated as failed in all circumstances, regardless of transaction characteristics or test evidence.
questions.explanation: Control testing assesses whether control layers prevent or identify the simulated fraud, not whether formal approvals happened. An unflagged beneficiary discrepancy demonstrates a weakness requiring improved criteria and further testing.

questions.topic: Application fraud (Case example: COVID-19 relief fraud)
questions.stem: In a review of emergency relief applications, investigators identify multiple businesses with conflicting payroll claims and documents inconsistent with eligibility requirements. What is the most useful lesson from the PPP fraud example?
options: Rapid disbursement objectives do not remove the need to validate material application representations and investigate linked anomalies.
High application volumes make identity and supporting documentation irrelevant to fraud controls.
A successful application automatically establishes that the underlying business existed and qualified.
Increase payment speed further but restrict verification to a random sample after funds have been disbursed.
questions.explanation: The guide uses PPP misuse to illustrate exploitation of expedited processes and false claims. A proportionate verification and anomaly response addresses the mechanism; approval alone and indiscriminate shutdowns do not. The strongest competing approach falls short because post-disbursement sampling may leave material false claims funded before meaningful preventive verification occurs.

questions.topic: Best practices for setting up an anti-fraud technology portfolio
questions.stem: A supplier demonstrates 96% test accuracy for a new fraud engine. Its proposal provides no operating-cost estimate, case management integration assessment, or evidence about customer friction. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: Purchase the tool first, then decide which fraud typologies it should address once it is deployed.
Use defined selection criteria and evidence of implementation benefit to evaluate alternatives in a wider control portfolio.
Approve because reported detection accuracy is sufficient evidence of portfolio-level value and return on investment.
Compare the tool against assessed fraud risks, integration feasibility, total operating costs and expected customer impact before committing funding.
Exclude qualitative customer impacts from the assessment because only prevented monetary losses indicate anti-fraud effectiveness.
questions.explanation: The guide directs technology choices toward risk exposure and implementation feasibility rather than stand-alone vendor performance claims. Use defined selection criteria and evidence of implementation benefit to evaluate alternatives in a wider control portfolio.

questions.stem: A transaction monitoring team extracts payment amounts but omits device-registration logs and customer-contact records needed to investigate cross-channel takeovers. At which stage should this design gap first be corrected?
options: Use only the payment warehouse's existing convenient fields and add missing channel evidence manually during closure.
By deleting any cases involving missing device or contact events.
By compensating for absent fields through a larger training sample containing the same omissions.
At source identification and extraction planning, by specifying needed fields, source systems, extraction method, and data lineage.
questions.explanation: The guide describes extraction as identifying necessary data and how to obtain it. Missing cross-channel sources cannot be repaired by model size; input selection and traceability must come before downstream analysis. The strongest competing approach falls short because missing sources often change the interpretation of the whole journey and cannot be reliably reconstructed only at closure.

questions.stem: A serious internal fraud allegation is reported, but the team has no agreed investigative authority, legal guidance, or preservation plan. What should the lead investigator secure before conducting intrusive inquiries?
options: Unrestricted access to every employee's private devices without legal review.
Management support, a lawful mandate, appropriate resources, a documented plan, and evidence-preservation responsibilities.
Begin confidential interviews immediately on management's informal verbal support, leaving legal authority and preservation decisions for later.
A closure date chosen before identifying relevant witnesses or data sources.
questions.explanation: The guide's leadership section stresses authorization, legal parameters, resources, and documentation. Premature accusations, blanket access, and predetermined conclusions threaten fairness and evidential integrity. The strongest competing approach falls short because informal approval does not settle investigative powers, evidence duties, or legal boundaries before sensitive actions.

questions.topic: Effective communication for victims of fraud
questions.stem: A fraud victim repeatedly changes details of a scam call while visibly distressed. An investigator argues that the contradictions prove deliberate deception and decides to adopt a confrontational tone. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: Use empathetic, nonjudgmental questioning and carefully corroborate the account without treating distress or imperfect recall as automatic proof of fraud.
Inform the customer that the investigation will close unless every remembered detail is perfectly consistent on the first interview.
Give clear updates and preserve the victim’s account alongside independently obtained transaction and device evidence.
Press for an immediate admission that the payment was voluntary, because victims under stress cannot be reliable witnesses.
Avoid explaining next steps or response times so the investigator does not create expectations that could influence the outcome.
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes respectful victim communication, listening and systematic evidence assessment rather than premature judgment. Give clear updates and preserve the victim’s account alongside independently obtained transaction and device evidence.

questions.sourceSection: Effective communication for victims of fraud

questions.topic: Fraud detection model: Training and tuning
questions.stem: A new fraud model performs nearly perfectly on transactions used to tune its thresholds but deteriorates sharply when applied to a later unseen cohort. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: Assess whether the chosen parameters work beyond the sample on which they were optimized.
Keep adjusting model thresholds until training-set accuracy reaches 100%, then freeze performance reporting.
Discard the unseen cohort because only data used in model development can be considered representative.
Include future confirmed-fraud labels in past feature records so the algorithm learns from all available observations.
Separate training, tuning and independent evaluation data, checking out-of-sample fraud outcomes and overfitting.
questions.explanation: The model-building section distinguishes training and tuning from the independent evaluation of generalization. Assess whether the chosen parameters work beyond the sample on which they were optimized.

questions.stem: During an online-shopping peak, a fraud rule causes a 45% increase in blocked transactions. Confirmed fraud capture improves slightly, but customer complaints and abandonment increase markedly. The product manager requests a systemwide suspension of velocity rules until the seasonal peak ends. Which TWO analyses should precede an approved change?
options: Measure legitimate and fraudulent activity by segment or channel to identify where threshold adjustments may be proportionate.
Evaluate model or rule performance, customer friction and fraud exposure during the change, with review of the outcomes.
Suspend the rule for all products because the decline in customer experience shows the fraud risk has been overstated.
Increase all velocity thresholds by an identical percentage before studying observed alerts or confirmed outcomes.
Use raw fraud alert counts as the sole indicator of effectiveness because customer outcomes are outside model evaluation.
questions.explanation: The guide stresses regular rule review, adaptive thresholds and balancing legitimate-customer experience against fraud prevention. Changes should be informed and monitored rather than indiscriminate.

questions.stem: An analytics pipeline joins payments stored in three currencies and two time zones; apparent velocity spikes appear only after the join. Which control best tests whether these anomalies are real?
options: Exclude all international payments to simplify the dataset.
Convert currency amounts but retain source-local timestamps without normalization because the model can learn regional differences.
Assume that the transformed table is correct because the load completed successfully.
Normalize units and timestamps, verify transformations against source records, and reconcile loaded totals before interpreting patterns.
questions.explanation: The transformation stage must produce comparable amounts and event times. Apparent spikes may be artifacts of inconsistent formats; changing model thresholds or excluding a whole segment does not validate the source-to-target mapping. The strongest competing approach falls short because comparable amounts are still misleading if event order and velocity calculations use inconsistent time standards.

questions.topic: Money mules and their role in fraud
questions.stem: Two accounts receive scam proceeds and rapidly distribute them. One holder openly advertised account-rental services; the other says an online employer directed them to transfer funds as a supposed payroll task. Select TWO measures or conclusions that address the evidence most defensibly.
options: Whether each holder knowingly participated or was manipulated, supported by the recruitment communications and account-use evidence.
Whether either customer is unemployed, because employment status determines intentional versus unintentional money muling.
Whether the transfers were round amounts, because round numbers alone establish informed participation.
Whether both accounts ultimately transferred money, which automatically establishes the same level of criminal intent.
Preserve recruitment messages, payment instructions, timing and evidence relevant to knowledge and control of the account.
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes intentional money muling from people unknowingly recruited or manipulated into moving fraudulent funds. Preserve recruitment messages, payment instructions, timing and evidence relevant to knowledge and control of the account.

questions.topic: Social engineering (Case example: Bank help desk)
questions.stem: A caller posing as a bank help-desk employee asks John for his login credentials and OTP, claims his account is in danger, and requests secrecy. Select TWO defensible findings from the guide's teaching case.
options: The bank should encourage independent verification using a trusted contact channel rather than the caller's instructions.
An OTP can safely be shared when the caller claims it is needed for security.
No fraud risk exists until money leaves the account.
Advise John to call back the phone number displayed in the incoming caller ID before sharing credentials.
The urgency and request for authentication secrets are signs of an impersonation/social-engineering attempt.
questions.explanation: The case combines authority impersonation, urgency, secrecy, and a request for authentication data. Independent verification interrupts the manipulation; accurate biographical details and the absence of a posted loss provide no authentication. The strongest competing approach falls short because caller ID can be spoofed; independently obtained contact details are stronger than information supplied by the suspected caller.

Link analysis or social-network graphing connecting entities, accounts, and shared events.
Build a network graph using account connections but exclude payment sequences and transaction relationships from the interpretation.
Relying on the number of records alone without examining relationships.
Treating each recipient's largest transaction as proof of criminal leadership.
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes quantitative and qualitative intelligence and uses graphing and link analysis to expose relationships. Connectivity and flows support hypotheses; surname sorts, transaction size, and volume alone cannot establish network roles. The strongest competing approach falls short because a graph stripped of transaction sequence may show proximity without the flow information needed to test coordination.

Only the vendor's accuracy figure from a demonstration environment.
Compare prevented losses against licensing cost but omit legitimate-payment rejection and customer-service effects.
Fraud prevented and residual losses, with the relevant investigation costs.
Legitimate approval rates, false declines, customer friction, and operational handling demand.
questions.explanation: The guide describes fraud analytics as balancing loss prevention, customer experience, efficiency, and trust. Both risk reduction and adverse effects are necessary; a single alert or vendor metric cannot show net business benefit. Refresh guidance as new scams emerge and measure staff understanding after training.
Use continuous, role-specific scenarios, escalation instructions and emerging typologies

Review thresholds and verification design, communicate clearly, and measure false-positive impact
Keep all friction unchanged regardless of legitimate impact
Apply risk-based step-up verification rather than imposing the highest friction on all events.
Use the strictest possible checks for every activity without risk differentiation

questions.stem: A payments firm has high-quality labels for established account-takeover fraud but suspects a newly emerging scam has different behavior and almost no confirmed examples. The head of analytics proposes training one supervised model using every currently suspicious alert as confirmed fraud, expecting that this will quickly capture the new scheme. Which TWO approaches provide a more defensible model portfolio?
options: Use established confirmed labels for the supervised account-takeover detector, monitoring its performance.
Use anomaly detection or clustering on unlabeled activity to identify patterns that investigators can then corroborate.
Treat anomalous cluster membership as sufficient evidence of perpetrator intent and close the associated cases.
Treat all unreviewed suspicious alerts as verified positive labels to maximize available model training data.
Discard existing historical labels because the emergence of new typologies makes all supervised learning inappropriate.
questions.explanation: Supervised techniques depend on reliable known outcomes, while unsupervised analysis can reveal unfamiliar relationships in unlabeled records. Anomalies need validation before they are treated as fraud.
