questions.stem:
A fraud investigator draws a network connecting six beneficiary accounts through common phone numbers, shared devices and payments from suspected victims. The resulting visualization appears to show one central organizer. However, the central node is a widely used payment intermediary, and several supposedly shared telephone numbers are actually a call-center hotline. Two beneficiary accounts do share a less common device identifier and move funds through matching rapid transfer sequences. The chief investigator wants to use the graph to select next interviews and records; a colleague proposes listing every connected customer as a confirmed conspirator. The firm may also have incomplete data for closed accounts that predate a platform migration.

What is the best interpretation of the network?
options: Use the graph to prioritize suspects, but defer validation of common intermediary nodes until after account restrictions are imposed.
Use graph links to generate hypotheses, separate ordinary shared infrastructure from stronger connections, and seek corroboration.
Label the intermediary as the organizer because it has the highest number of links.
Treat all shared identifiers as equally probative pending an eventual interview, because the graph was generated from internal records.
questions.explanation: Network tools help reveal possible relationships, but hubs can represent benign infrastructure and datasets may be incomplete. Connections require contextual verification.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Using data to uncover fraud patterns (pp. 77–82)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Using data to uncover fraud patterns (pp. 77–82)

questions.topic: Prompt interdiction before guilt is established
questions.stem:
A wire transfer triggers an alert because the customer recently changed contact details and has never before sent funds to the beneficiary. The payment is within the institution’s permitted hold window. The customer service representative says the customer asked the bank to transfer the money and therefore any hold is improper. A fraud investigator observes that the caller’s voice sounded unlike earlier calls, but audio quality was poor and the customer frequently travels. The fraud policy permits temporary risk-based interventions pending verification; the investigator does not yet have evidence sufficient to conclude that the customer is an impostor. A senior manager asks whether acting to prevent potential loss must wait until the fraud has been conclusively proved.

Which response is best supported?
options: Automatically release every suspicious transfer because customer contact is incomplete.
Apply permitted proportionate hold and verification procedures, gather evidence and avoid claiming that an alert itself proves fraud.
Release the wire but refer the suspected impersonation for a retrospective investigation, as proof of fraud remains incomplete.
Freeze the customer relationship indefinitely on the basis of voice-quality differences alone, pending a full forensic examination.
questions.explanation: Fraud detection allows prompt preventive action within policy, while conclusions must remain evidence-led and fair.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Fraud investigator roles and responsibilities; investigative mindset (pp. 8–11)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Fraud investigator roles and responsibilities; investigative mindset (pp. 8–11)

A temporary fraud-control intervention can be justified by a risk signal before the investigation has conclusively established criminal conduct.
options: True

questions.topic: Sufficient evidence under a regulatory deadline
questions.stem:
A disputed online purchase has been investigated for several weeks. The merchant has produced shipping records and a device identifier previously seen in the cardholder’s history; the cardholder has submitted travel details and says an estranged family member had access to the shared computer. The investigator can explain what each record proves but cannot establish exactly who pressed the purchase button. A manager refuses to close the case until every theoretical alternative is disproved, while a different reviewer wants to deny solely on the historic device match. The applicable complaint deadline is approaching, and the institution must communicate a defensible determination supported by the evidence actually available.

What is the most appropriate closure principle?
options: Assign decisive weight to the device match unless the cardholder provides proof that the estranged relative performed the purchase.
Extend the investigation beyond its applicable deadline to obtain absolute attribution, while keeping the customer informed of progress.
Evaluate the corroborated record and applicable standards, document uncertainties and reasoning, and reach a timely fair decision.
Issue a favorable decision solely because the case contains conflicting evidence, without assessing its relevance.
questions.explanation: The guide focuses on enough relevant evidence to justify an outcome, documentation of how it was reached and timely treatment of the customer.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • When do you have enough evidence?; fraud case closure (pp. 87–89)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • When do you have enough evidence?; fraud case closure (pp. 87–89)

In a complex fraud claim, the inability to eliminate every imaginable hypothesis necessarily prevents a defensible case decision.

False
questions.explanation: Case closure relies on sufficient credible evidence and applicable requirements, not absolute elimination of every hypothetical possibility.

questions.stem:
A customer says a fraudster called on Monday to request credentials; her written complaint places the same call on Wednesday, and call logs show an inbound interaction on Tuesday. The investigator plays an archived recording to clarify the date. A colleague proposes silently changing the written statement and discarding the first version so the final narrative is consistent. The customer is willing to review a corrected statement and sign an attestation. The case also contains a forwarded email with no preserved headers and a handwritten note taken during a rushed first interview. Legal requests a reproducible explanation of any corrections before the bank presents its case to an external authority.

What should the investigator do?
options: Keep the original accounts and supporting records, document the reconciliation, obtain a corrected verified statement and explain unresolved discrepancies.
Prefer the customer’s latest recollection to the recording and document the call log as potentially inaccurate without validation.
Assume the forwarded email is complete proof of its sender without checking original headers.
Replace the original statement with a corrected attested one while retaining only a summary of the earlier discrepancy.
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes accurate statements, provenance and documentary support. Changes should be transparent and verified, not hidden.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Taking statements; documenting evidence (pp. 74–75, 91–95)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Taking statements; documenting evidence (pp. 74–75, 91–95)

questions.topic: Insurance claim denial based on a single inconsistency
questions.stem:
An insurer suspects an exaggerated property claim after an applicant reports storm damage. The initial claim description states that water entered on Sunday, but a contractor’s invoice gives Monday as the site visit date. Satellite weather information indicates heavy rain across both days, and two photographs were uploaded from a device belonging to a relative. The insurance company’s automated system labels the inconsistent dates 'confirmed fraud' and proposes immediate denial. The claimant explains that damage happened overnight and the contractor inspected it the following morning. Investigators have not verified the repair estimate, original photo timestamps or whether the claimant had a motive to inflate the loss.

Which conclusion is best supported by the available facts?
options: Accept the model’s confirmed-fraud classification as the operative finding unless the claimant can independently disprove it.
The discrepancy merits clarification and corroboration, not an immediate inference of intentional deception.
Make a preliminary adverse determination from the conflicting dates but leave the device and repair evidence for any customer appeal.
Treat the relative-owned device as neutral and rely solely on the contractor’s later inspection date to decide intentional misstatement.
questions.explanation: Fraud entails intentional deception, and seemingly inconsistent records may have benign explanations. An evidence-led investigation must test alternatives.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Common fraud typologies; evidence-based investigation (pp. 12–55, 62–65)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Common fraud typologies; evidence-based investigation (pp. 12–55, 62–65)

questions.topic: Preserving a confidential insider investigation file
questions.stem:
A fraud specialist prepares a report alleging that an employee and a vendor collaborated to change supplier payment details. The draft contains a persuasive chronological narrative, but several decisive exhibits exist only as links to a shared folder scheduled for automatic deletion. The investigator’s notes do not identify which witness supplied each allegation or whether a conversation was transcribed from memory. Human Resources proposes circulating the report to the employee’s entire department, while a legal adviser notes that unnecessary disclosure could reveal a whistleblower and jeopardize the investigation. The investigation is expected to be independently reviewed and may require follow-up long after the original analyst leaves the institution.

What is the most important reporting improvement?
options: Maintain an accurate, secured and traceable evidential file with source references, retained notes, justified conclusions and controlled circulation.
Replace evidence references with a statement that the investigator is highly experienced.
Rely on the detailed written chronology while retaining only those exhibits specifically quoted in the report.
Circulate the report to all department managers with identifying details redacted, before preserving the expiring source exhibits.
questions.explanation: A defensible investigation report needs source support, protected records, transparent reasoning and appropriate confidentiality.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Documenting research; retaining notes and support (pp. 91–96)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Documenting research; retaining notes and support (pp. 91–96)

questions.topic: Post-investigation loop after a confirmed control gap
questions.stem:
An investigation confirms that an impostor obtained a contact-number change through weak telephone verification and subsequently transferred customer funds. The bank reimburses the victim, closes the fraud case and improves the help-desk verification script. Three weeks later, analysts detect the same attack against a newly acquired product whose customer-service workflow has not been updated. The fraud investigation report included the root cause but was not shared with the analytics team responsible for monitoring other products. The executive dashboard counts only reimbursed loss amounts and case-closure speed; it does not monitor whether remediation was rolled out or whether similar attempts continue. The board asks what a meaningful post-investigation feedback loop should achieve.

What is the best post-investigation program action?
options: Distribute the new script to remaining product teams but omit testing and monitoring of whether it operated as designed.
Send the customer a final letter and prevent any further use of the case information.
Link root cause and typology intelligence to cross-product control updates, monitoring, training and measurable verification of remediation.
Close the original case after reimbursement and require each product team to consider the root cause at its next annual review.
questions.explanation: The guide’s feedback loop uses investigation outcomes to refine controls and detect repeat or emerging attacks across the program.
questions.source: ACAMS CAFS v1.03 · Fraud Investigations • Post-investigation fraud program updates; fraud feedback loop (p. 103)
questions.sourceSection: Fraud Investigations • Post-investigation fraud program updates; fraud feedback loop (p. 103)
